Pradesh (UP), India 
This section should help your chatbot answer users who do not know the name of a 
scheme. 
The official Government of India myScheme portal already uses this general model: citizens 
enter demographic/profile information, the system searches relevant government schemes, 
and users can then view eligibility, benefits, required documents and application information. 
(myScheme)

Eligibility Status Data 
Use these four statuses:

Final verification is still required. 
 
 
POTENTIALLY ELIGIBLE

is missing. 
 
 
NOT ELIGIBLE 
 
A known mandatory eligibility condition does not match. 
 
 
UNABLE TO DETERMINE

Available information is insufficient to reliably determine 
eligibility. 
 
 
Why Matched 
Example: 
Scheme: XYZ Scholarship 
 
Status: Potentially Eligible 
 
Why Matched:

✓ Student 
✓ Applicable education level

Why Not Eligible

Reason: 
✗ Scheme maximum age: 25 
User age: 28 
 
Alternative:

without this age restriction.

Important Government-Source Behaviour 
The official myScheme platform follows essentially the same three-step discovery model: 
Enter details → Search relevant schemes → Select a suitable scheme and proceed to 
its application information. It provides eligibility, benefits, application procedures and 
required-document information. (myScheme)

As of July 2026, myScheme says it contains more than 4,700 Central and State/UT 
government schemes, with more being added. It currently redirects applicants to the 
concerned department's application page rather than itself processing every scheme 
application. (myScheme) 
For SetuAI, the safe final decision chain should therefore be: 
User Profile 
 ↓ 
Need Detection 
 ↓ 
UP + Applicable Central Scheme Search 
 ↓ 
Eligibility Filtering 
 ↓ 
Potential Matches 
 ↓ 
Official Scheme Information 
 ↓ 
Benefits + Documents + Application 
 ↓ 
Official Department / Application Portal 
 
15/15 main corpus categories are now covered. This completes the major Uttar Pradesh 
citizen-welfare knowledge scope you listed for SetuAI.

English.13. Land & Property — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
UP Bhulekh / Land Records 
State: Uttar Pradesh​
Category: Revenue / Land Records​

System: UP Bhulekh​
Purpose: Digital access to revenue land-record information. 
The UP Bhulekh ecosystem maintains digitized land records and cadastral-map information 
across Uttar Pradesh. Its official dashboard tracks revenue villages, village Khatauni 
records, scanned maps, verified maps, Bhu-Naksha linkage and geo-referencing. 
(Upbhulekh) 
Core Land Terminology 
Khatauni 
→ Record containing landholding/tenancy-related revenue entries. 
 
Khasra 
→ Plot/cultivation-related revenue record. 
 
Gata / Plot Number 
→ Identifier associated with a particular parcel/plot. 
 
Khata 
→ Account/holding-related land-record reference. 
 
Revenue Village 
→ Revenue administration unit under which land records are maintained. 
 
Tehsil 
→ Revenue administrative subdivision. 
 
Mutation / Dakhil-Kharij 
→ Process for updating the revenue record following an eligible transfer/change.

Bhu-Naksha 
→ Digital cadastral/map information linked with land parcels. 
 
SetuAI should keep these concepts separate instead of treating “Khatauni”, “Khasra” and 
“map” as the same document.

14. Grievance & Government Portals — 
Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
Jansunwai – Samadhan 
System: Integrated Grievance Redressal System​
Government: Government of Uttar Pradesh​
Category: Citizen Grievance​
Purpose: Online registration, tracking and monitoring of grievances.

The official UP Government describes Jansunwai as an integrated grievance-redressal 
system designed to provide communication between citizens and government 
departments/offices. Citizens can register and track grievances online, while departments 
can process and monitor them through the same system. (Jan Sunwai) 
Core Functions 
The official portal currently provides four important citizen functions: 
Register Grievance 
Track Grievance 
Send Reminder 
Give Feedback 
 
(Jan Sunwai) 
Complaint Registration 
Jansunwai allows grievance registration using mobile OTP. The grievance can then enter the 
relevant government redressal workflow. (Jan Sunwai) 
Store: 
Citizen 
Mobile Number 
Grievance Category 
Department 
District 
Location 
Complaint Description 
Supporting Information 
Reference / Complaint Number 
Registration Date 
Current Status 
Department Action

Disposal 
Reminder 
Feedback 
 
Good Complaint Structure for SetuAI 
For chatbot assistance: 
Problem: 
What exactly happened? 
 
Department: 
Which government service is involved? 
 
Location: 
District / Tehsil / Block / Village / City 
 
Previous Action: 
Was an application or complaint already submitted? 
 
Reference: 
Application / complaint / beneficiary number 
 
Expected Resolution: 
What legitimate service/action is being requested? 
 
SetuAI can use this information to help the user generate a clear grievance.

Track Grievance 
Jansunwai allows citizens to track registered grievances using their registered details. Its 
current complaint tracker requests a complaint/reference number, mobile number, security 
code and OTP verification. (Jan Sunwai) 
The tracker currently notes that details of disposed references are viewable there for up to 
the previous three months. (Jan Sunwai) 
Status Queries 
How can I check my Jansunwai complaint? 
Where is my complaint number? 
My complaint is pending. 
My complaint was disposed. 
No action has been taken. 
The department says the complaint is resolved but my problem remains. 
 
 
Send Reminder 
If a grievance crosses its stipulated resolution timeline, Jansunwai provides a Send 
Reminder function. (Jan Sunwai) 
Chatbot flow: 
Complaint Filed 
↓ 
Reference Generated 
↓ 
Track Status 
↓ 
Still Pending Beyond Applicable Timeline

↓ 
Send Reminder 
↓ 
Continue Tracking 
 
 
Feedback After Disposal 
Jansunwai allows citizens to provide feedback regarding the quality of grievance disposal. 
The official portal states that higher officials evaluate this feedback and may 
regenerate/reopen a disposed reference where appropriate. (Jan Sunwai) 
This is important for queries like: 
“My complaint says disposed but nobody solved the problem.”

Chapter 5: Ration & Food Security (UP Food & Civil 
Supplies) 
Nodal Department: Department of Food and Civil Supplies, Uttar Pradesh 
Official Portal: fcs.up.gov.in 
Helpline Numbers: 1800-1800-150 / 1967 
1. Ration Card Categories & Eligibility Criteria 
Uttar Pradesh issues ration cards under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, 
categorized primarily into two operational groups: 
A. Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Red Card 
●​ Target Group: The poorest of the poor households, destitute families, widows, 
terminally ill individuals, and landless agricultural laborers. 
●​ Income Limit: Extremely low income households identified by the Gram 
Sabha/Urban Local Body. 
●​ Entitlement: Fixed 35 kg of food grains per card/family per month (14 kg Wheat 
and 21 kg Rice). 
B. Priority Household (PHH / Patra Grihasthi) — White Card 
●​ Target Group: BPL and lower-middle-income families not covered under AAY. 
●​ Income Limit: 
○​ Rural Areas: Annual family income must not exceed ₹46,080. 
○​ Urban Areas: Annual family income must not exceed ₹56,460. 
●​ Entitlement: 5 kg of food grains per registered member/unit per month (2 kg 
Wheat and 3 kg Rice per unit). 
Ineligibility & Exclusion Criteria (UP State Rules) 
A household is automatically disqualified from receiving a PHH/AAY ration card if any 
member: 
●​ Owns a four-wheeler vehicle, tractor, or heavy machinery. 
●​ Owns an air conditioner (AC) or a generator of 5 KW or more. 
●​ Owns a residential plot exceeding 100 sq. meters in urban areas or 80 sq. meters in 
municipal corporations. 
●​ Owns more than 5 acres of irrigated land in rural areas. 
●​ Pays Income Tax or has a professional enterprise.

3. Citizen Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) 
A. Application for a New Ration Card 
1.​ Submission: Apply online through a Jan Seva Kendra (CSC) or e-Sathi UP portal 
(edistrict.up.gov.in). 
2.​ Required Documents: 
○​ Aadhaar card copies of all family members to be listed. 
○​ Income Certificate issued by Tehsildar (valid within 3 years). 
○​ Photograph of the female head of the family (Selfie/Passport size). 
○​ Bank Passbook copy (Female head of family). 
○​ Electricity Bill / LPG Connection papers for address proof. 
3.​ Verification: Sent to the Block Development Officer (BDO) in rural areas or Supply 
Inspector (SI) in urban areas. Field verification completed within 30 days. 
B. Addition / Deletion of Member (Unit Modification) 
●​ Adding a Newborn/Child: Submit Form-B at CSC with the child's birth certificate 
and updated Aadhaar card. 
●​ Adding a Newly Married Wife: Requires marriage certificate, deletion certificate 
from her previous household ration card, and updated address proof. 
●​ Deleting a Member: Mandatory upon death (death certificate required) or 
marriage/relocation (marriage certificate/address transfer proof required). 
C. Correction of Details & Address Change

●​ Name/Age Correction: Updated details must first reflect in the member's Aadhaar 
database. Once updated, submit a correction request via e-District with the updated 
Aadhaar. 
●​ Address Change (Within District): Submit an application with a new local residency 
proof. Supply Inspector updates the allocated Fair Price Shop (FPS) dealer. 
D. e-KYC & ID Seeding 
●​ Purpose: Eliminates duplicate, ghost, or deceased units from the registry. 
●​ Process: Every listed member must visit their allocated FPS dealer and authenticate 
their iris or fingerprint on the e-PoS (Point of Sale) machine. 
●​ Status Check: Check seeding status on fcs.up.gov.in under the "Ration Card 
Eligibility List" search tool. 
E. Duplicate / Lost Ration Card Reissuance 
1.​ File an application at the Tehsil Supply Office or CSC. 
2.​ Provide the Ration Card Number, head of family's Aadhaar, and an affidavit stating 
loss/damage. 
3.​ Pay the official token fee (₹20). 
4.​ Print the e-Ration Card directly from the e-District/FCS portal. 
4. Fair Price Shops (FPS / Kotedar) & One Nation One Ration Card 
(ONORC) 
Fair Price Shop (FPS) Operations 
●​ Distributions are managed via electronic Point of Sale (e-PoS) devices connected to 
central servers. 
●​ Weights are strictly integrated with electronic weighing scales connected directly to 
e-PoS machines to prevent manual weighing fraud by dealers (Kotedars). 
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) & Intra-State Portability 
●​ Intra-State Portability: A ration card holder from one district (e.g., Gorakhpur) 
residing in another district (e.g., Lucknow) can collect their monthly quota from any 
local FPS in Lucknow. 
●​ Inter-State Portability: Migrant workers from UP residing in other participating 
states can draw their monthly quota using their Aadhaar-linked ration card via 
biometric verification on e-PoS devices. 
●​ Mera Ration App: Allows beneficiaries to locate the nearest FPS shop, check their 
entitlement balance, and view recent transaction history. 
5. Grievance Redressal & Oversight Mechanisms 
A. Grievance Escalation Hierarchy 
1.​ Level 1: Regional Supply Inspector (SI) / Area Officer. 
2.​ Level 2: District Supply Officer (DSO) / Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). 
3.​ Level 3: District Magistrate (DM) / Jansunwai IGRS Portal. 
B. Common Violations & Remedies 
●​ Overcharging / Underweighing: Report directly to the Toll-Free Helpline 
(1800-1800-150) or log an IGRS complaint. Inspection is mandated within 72 hours. 
●​ Refusal to Issue Ration: If a Kotedar denies ration despite successful biometric 
authentication, the e-PoS logs a failed transaction report, enabling strict departmental 
action including license suspension. 
●​ Vigilance Committees (Sartarkta Samiti): Local committees formed at Gram 
Panchayat and Ward levels to monitor monthly grain arrivals, shop opening hours, 
and stock registers.

## TOPIC 1: RATION CARD BASICS 
 
**Definition:** A Ration Card is an official document issued by the State Government (Food 
& Civil Supplies Department) that identifies a household as eligible to receive subsidized 
food grains under the Public Distribution System (PDS). It also serves as a proof of identity 
and residence in many contexts. 
 
**Key Concepts:** 
- **PDS (Public Distribution System):** The mechanism through which the government 
distributes subsidized food grains to eligible households via Fair Price Shops (FPS). 
- **TPDS (Targeted PDS):** The system that targets specific categories (BPL, AAY, etc.) 
rather than universal distribution. 
- **NFSA (National Food Security Act, 2013):** The central law that governs food security 
entitlements; ration cards issued under NFSA are called NFSA cards. 
- **Ration Card Number:** A unique identification number assigned to each household card, 
used for tracking, search, and verification. 
- **Household/Unit:** Refers to all members registered under one ration card who typically 
share cooking arrangements. 
- **Head of Family (HoF):** The primary registered member responsible for the card; often 
(but not necessarily) the eldest male/female earning member. 
 
**Department:** Uttar Pradesh ration cards fall under the **Department of Food and Civil 
Supplies (Khadya evam Rasad Vibhag), Government of Uttar Pradesh**. 
 
**Difference: Ration Card vs NFSA Card** 
- A ration card is the physical/digital document. 
- NFSA card specifically denotes that the household is covered under the National Food 
Security Act and receives entitlements as per Act provisions (AAY/PHH categories). 
- Not all ration cards are NFSA cards (there can be non-priority/APL type cards without 
NFSA subsidy in some contexts). 
 
**Official Source:** UP Food & Civil Supplies Department; NFSA, 2013 (Central Act).

## TOPIC 2: CARD CATEGORIES IN UP 
 
**Definition:** UP issues ration cards under different categories based on household 
economic status. 
 
**Categories:** 
1. **Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY):** For the poorest of poor households — identified 
through specific vulnerability criteria (landless laborers, destitute, elderly without support, 
etc.). Highest priority category with fixed higher entitlement per household. 
2. **Priority Household (PHH) / Eligible Household:** Covers economically weaker families 
identified as per State-approved criteria under NFSA; entitlement is per person (not fixed per 
household like AAY). 
3. **Non-NFSA / APL cards (where applicable):** Households not covered under NFSA 
subsidy but may still hold a ration card for identity/record purposes in some state provisions. 
 
**AAY vs PHH — Key Differences:** 
| Aspect | AAY | PHH | 
|---|---|---| 
| Target group | Poorest of poor | Priority/eligible households | 
| Entitlement basis | Fixed per household | Per person in family | 
| Identification | Special vulnerability criteria | Income/asset-based criteria | 
| Priority level | Highest | High | 
 
**Category Change:** A household can apply for category change (e.g., PHH to AAY) if it 
meets revised eligibility criteria, subject to verification by local authorities. 
 
**Official Source:** NFSA 2013; UP State Government Orders on category identification 
criteria. 
 
--- 
 
## TOPIC 3: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA 
 
**Who is Eligible:** 
- Permanent residents of Uttar Pradesh (rural or urban). 
- Households falling within income/asset criteria defined by the State for PHH/AAY 
categories. 
- Families without a ration card in any other state/UT. 
- One ration card per household (not per individual). 
 
**Who is NOT Eligible / Exclusion Criteria (general principles applied nationally, State may 
customize):** 
- Households owning motorized four-wheelers/agricultural equipment (tractors) in some 
criteria versions.

- Government employees (Class III/IV exceptions may vary by state). 
- Income taxpayers. 
- Households with large landholding beyond specified limits. 
- Families owning substantial pucca residential property beyond defined limits. 
- Persons already holding a ration card in another state (must surrender before applying in 
UP). 
 
**Special Cases:** 
- **Migrant workers:** Can apply for portability benefits (see ONORC) instead of/along with 
new card. 
- **Tenants:** Can apply using rental agreement + local verification as residence proof. 
- **Unmarried persons/students:** Generally included in parental household card; separate 
card only after establishing independent household. 
- **Newly married couples:** Wife typically needs deletion from parental card before addition 
to husband's card (or new card formation). 
- **Homeless persons:** Special provisions exist for identification without conventional 
address proof (via local verification/certificate). 
- **Senior citizens/widows/disabled:** Eligible under standard criteria; additional priority may 
apply under AAY identification norms in certain cases. 
 
**Official Source:** NFSA Act Section 10; UP eligibility criteria GO (Government Order) — 
verify latest version.

## TOPIC 4: NEW RATION CARD APPLICATION PROCESS 
 
**Definition:** Process to apply for a new ration card for a household not currently holding 
one. 
 
**Where to Apply:** 
- **Online:** UP Food & Civil Supplies Department portal / Integrated Citizen portal. 
- **Offline:** Common Service Centre (CSC)/Jan Seva Kendra, Tehsil office, Block office 
(rural), Nagar Palika/Nagar Nigam office (urban). 
 
**Step-by-Step Process:** 
1. Collect required documents (see Topic 5). 
2. Fill application form (online via portal or offline physical form). 
3. Upload/attach documents including family photograph. 
4. Submit application — receive an **Application/Reference Number**. 
5. Application routed to the concerned **Supply Inspector / Tehsildar / Zonal Officer** for 
verification. 
6. **Field verification** may be conducted (physical visit to confirm residence and family 
details). 
7. Upon successful verification, card is approved and generated (digital + printable). 
8. Card gets linked with FPS (Fair Price Shop) based on address. 
 
**Online vs Offline:**

- Online: Self-service, tracked via application number, faster interface but requires document 
scanning/upload capability. 
- Offline: Assisted by CSC operator/Jan Seva Kendra for a service charge; useful for those 
without digital access. 
 
**Verification Authority:** Depends on jurisdiction — Supply Inspector (rural/urban), 
Tehsildar, or designated District Supply Officer (DSO) staff. 
 
**Fees:** Nominal application fee may apply (varies) + CSC service charge if applied offline 
through a center. *(Verify current fee structure from official source.)* 
 
**Timeline:** Official processing timelines are specified under State Right to Public Service 
Act / departmental service charter — typically ranges from a few weeks depending on 
verification load. *(Verify current SLA.)* 
 
**Official Source:** UP Food & Civil Supplies Department application guidelines.

2. **Residence Proof** — electricity bill, rent agreement, voter ID, or property document. 
3. **Income Certificate** — issued by competent authority (Tehsildar/SDM).

## TOPIC 6: APPLICATION STATUS TRACKING 
 
**How to Check Status:** 
1. Visit official UP Food & Civil Supplies portal. 
2. Navigate to "Application Status" / "Track Application" section. 
3. Enter **Application/Reference Number** (provided at submission) OR registered mobile 
number. 
4. View current status. 
 
**Status Meanings:** 
- **Pending:** Application received, awaiting processing/verification. 
- **Verification in Progress:** Field officer assigned, physical/document verification ongoing. 
- **Approved:** Application cleared; card generation in process. 
- **Rejected:** Application denied — reason usually specified (see Topic 22). 
- **Card Generated:** Ration card created; ready for download/collection. 
 
**Common Problems:** 
- Status not updating: Could indicate backlog at verification stage — contact concerned 
Supply Inspector/DSO office. 
- Application number lost: Can often be retrieved via registered mobile number search on 
portal, or contact CSC where applied.

## TOPIC 12: ADDRESS CHANGE / MIGRATION 
 
**Scenarios:** 
1. **Same village/city address change** — minor correction, local verification. 
2. **District change within UP** — requires surrender of old card/transfer request; new FPS 
linkage based on new address. 
3. **UP to another state migration** — old UP card must generally be surrendered; new 
application in destination state (or use ONORC provisions for temporary portability, see 
Topic 20). 
4. **Another state to UP migration** — surrender/cancel previous state's card, then apply 
fresh in UP. 
 
**Process for Within-State Transfer:** 
1. Apply for address/FPS change via portal or local office. 
2. Submit new residence proof. 
3. Old FPS linkage deactivated; new FPS assigned based on updated address. 
 
**Portability vs Permanent Transfer:**

- **Portability (ONORC):** Temporary arrangement allowing ration collection from any FPS 
nationwide without changing home card details — ideal for migrant workers. 
- **Permanent Transfer:** Complete address/FPS update in the ration card record for those 
permanently relocating. 
 
**Official Source:** UP FCS migration/transfer guidelines; ONORC scheme documentation.

## TOPIC 13: AADHAAR SEEDING 
 
**Definition:** Linking Aadhaar numbers of all ration card family members with the ration 
card record for identity verification and duplicate elimination. 
 
**Is it Mandatory:** Generally yes — Aadhaar seeding of all members is required for 
continued benefit under NFSA (with documented exceptions for those without Aadhaar, 
subject to alternate ID proof provisions). 
 
**How to Link:** 
1. Visit FPS with e-POS machine, or 
2. Use online portal Aadhaar-seeding module, or 
3. Visit CSC/Jan Seva Kendra for assisted linking. 
 
**Common Issues:** 
- **Mismatch:** Name/DOB differs between Aadhaar and ration card records — requires 
correction in one of the two databases. 
- **Duplicate Aadhaar:** Same Aadhaar linked to multiple ration cards — triggers 
investigation/removal of duplicate entry. 
- **Authentication Failure:** Biometric mismatch during seeding — retry or use OTP-based 
alternate authentication if available. 
 
**After Aadhaar Update:** If Aadhaar details change (name, DOB, address), 
re-seeding/re-verification with ration card may be required to maintain consistency. 
 
**Official Source:** UIDAI-NFSA seeding guidelines; UP FCS seeding module.

## TOPIC 14: e-KYC (Know Your Customer) FOR RATION CARD 
 
**Definition:** A periodic re-verification process requiring beneficiaries to confirm their 
identity (usually via Aadhaar-based biometric or OTP authentication) to keep their ration card 
active. 
 
**Who Needs to Do It:** All existing ration card holders/members, as mandated by periodic 
government orders. 
 
**How It's Done:**

1. Visit the linked FPS (Fair Price Shop) with e-POS machine. 
2. Biometric authentication (fingerprint/iris) against Aadhaar. 
3. Alternatively, some processes allow online e-KYC via portal/mobile app with OTP. 
 
**Special Cases:** 
- **Elderly/disabled with biometric failure:** Manual exception process — supervisor-level 
authentication or alternate ID verification, as per department provisions. 
- **Deadline sensitivity:** e-KYC often has government-notified deadlines; missing deadline 
may result in **card holding/suspension** until compliance. 
 
**Checking e-KYC Status:** Available via portal member-wise status check or by asking 
dealer at FPS. 
 
**Effect of Not Doing e-KYC:** Risk of ration entitlement suspension for that 
member/household until e-KYC is completed. 
 
**Official Source:** Latest UP Government Order on e-KYC deadlines (verify current 
cycle/date — this changes periodically).

## TOPIC 16: RATION ENTITLEMENT 
 
**Definition:** The quantity of food grains a household/individual is entitled to receive 
monthly under their card category. 
 
**General Entitlement Structure (verify current quantities from official source):**

- **AAY households:** Fixed quantity per household per month (regardless of family size). 
- **PHH households:** Per-person entitlement — total quantity depends on number of units 
(members) in the household. 
 
**Items Typically Covered:** Wheat, rice, and in some allocations, coarse grains — 
proportions vary as per State/Central allocation orders. 
 
**Issue Price:** Highly subsidized rate per kg (may be free under specific central/state 
schemes during announced periods — always confirm current status as "free ration" 
schemes have specific active/inactive windows). 
 
**Entitlement Changes:** 
- Adding a family member increases total household entitlement (for PHH). 
- Removing a member decreases entitlement correspondingly. 
 
**How to Check Current Entitlement:** Via portal's "Ration Card Details" section showing 
unit count and category-based entitlement, or ask FPS dealer directly. 
 
**Official Source:** NFSA Section 3 & 4; Latest UP State allocation Government Order. 
**(Quantities/prices must be verified from current official notification before publishing.)**

## TOPIC 17: DISTRIBUTION PROCESS 
 
**Definition:** The monthly process through which ration is issued to beneficiaries at their 
linked Fair Price Shop. 
 
**Key Points:** 
- Distribution typically occurs on notified dates each month (varies by state cycle — verify 
current schedule). 
- Beneficiary must complete biometric/OTP authentication at FPS via e-POS machine to 
receive ration. 
- **Receipt:** Beneficiary should receive a printed/SMS transaction receipt confirming 
quantity issued. 
 
**Common Issues:** 
- **Ration missed for a month:** Generally does NOT carry forward automatically — check 
with FPS/DSO regarding any make-up provisions for that cycle (varies by policy). 
- **Dealer has no stock:** Report to Supply Inspector/District Supply Office; stock allocation 
delays should be escalated. 
- **Partial ration received:** Insist on written acknowledgment/receipt from dealer noting 
shortfall; report to grievance cell.

## TOPIC 18: FAIR PRICE SHOP (FPS) / KOTEDAR (DEALER) 
 
**Definition:** FPS is the authorized retail outlet through which subsidized ration is 
distributed; the dealer operating it is commonly called "Kotedar."

|---|---| 
| Dealer denies ration | File complaint with Supply Inspector/DSO | 
| Short quantity given | Report with evidence (receipt/weight discrepancy) |

## TOPIC 19: e-POS / BIOMETRIC AUTHENTICATION 
 
**Definition:** Electronic Point of Sale machines installed at FPS for 
biometric/Aadhaar-based authentication before ration issuance. 
 
**Common Problems & Resolutions:** 
- **Fingerprint fails repeatedly:** Try alternate finger, clean scanner/finger, or use iris 
authentication if device supports it. 
- **Biometric mismatch:** May require re-seeding of Aadhaar/biometric update at Aadhaar 
center. 
- **Network/server down:** Dealer may need to retry later or use offline exception process 
where permitted by department. 
- **OTP-based authentication:** Available as alternate method in some cases for those with 
biometric issues (subject to state provision). 
- **Elderly/manual exception:** Supervisor-level manual override process for genuine 
biometric failure cases (as per department SOP). 
- **Transaction shows "distributed" but ration not received:** This is a serious issue — file 
immediate complaint with photographic/receipt evidence to Supply Inspector/DSO; may 
indicate fraud (see Topic 34).

**Official Source:** UP FCS e-POS operational guidelines.

## TOPIC 20: ONE NATION ONE RATION CARD (ONORC) 
 
**Definition:** A central scheme allowing ration cardholders to access their entitled food 
grains from any Fair Price Shop across India using their existing ration card, primarily 
benefiting migrant populations. 
 
**How It Works:** 
1. Cardholder's Aadhaar is seeded with ration card. 
2. While away from home state/district, cardholder can authenticate at any FPS nationwide 
via e-POS. 
3. Portability transaction fetches entitlement from home record; ration issued from the visiting 
FPS. 
 
**Family Split Transactions:** ONORC allows partial family members to draw their share at 
one location while others draw remaining share at another location (split transaction feature). 
 
**UP Card Usage in Other States:** UP ration cardholders can use ONORC to collect ration 
in other states, subject to Aadhaar seeding and portability activation. 
 
**Other-State Card Usage in UP:** Similarly, other-state cardholders can collect ration at UP 
FPS via ONORC. 
 
**Common Portability Failures:** 
- Aadhaar not seeded/mismatched. 
- Local FPS stock unavailability for portability quota. 
- Technical/network sync issues between state databases. 
 
**Finding Eligible FPS:** Use the Mera Ration app or national portal's FPS locator to find 
nearby ONORC-enabled shops. 
 
**Official Source:** Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution — ONORC 
scheme guidelines.

## TOPIC 24: DUPLICATE RATION CARDS 
 
**Definition:** A situation where the same individual or household is registered under more 
than one ration card (same or different states), which is against NFSA rules (one card per 
household). 
 
**Detection Methods:** Aadhaar seeding cross-verification across state/national databases 
flags duplicates. 
 
**Consequences:** 
- Automatic flagging/suspension of duplicate entries. 
- Possible penalty or benefit clawback in cases of intentional fraud. 
 
**Resolution:** 
1. Voluntarily surrender the extra/incorrect card at the respective office. 
2. Retain only one valid card matching current residence. 
3. Provide surrender certificate when applying for new card elsewhere, if relevant. 
 
**Official Source:** NFSA duplicate detection guidelines; UP FCS surrender process.

## TOPIC 30: INCOME & ECONOMIC CRITERIA

## TOPIC 38: NFSA (NATIONAL FOOD SECURITY ACT) — BASICS 
 
**Definition:** A central law enacted in 2013 to provide legal entitlement to subsidized food 
grains for eligible households, aiming to ensure food and nutritional security.

criteria within the coverage percentage allocated by the Centre for the state's rural and urban 
population.

distribution records.

households for enhanced food security support.

recommendation combined with administrative verification.

## TOPIC 48: SCENARIO-BASED Q&A (Practical Examples)

**Q: "Mere family me 5 members hain, kitna ration milega?"** 
A: Depends on card category — AAY gets a fixed household quantity regardless of member 
count; PHH entitlement is calculated per person, so 5 members would receive 5 units worth 
of entitlement as per current per-person allocation (verify current quantity from official 
source). 
 
**Q: "Meri shaadi ho gayi, wife ka naam kaise add karun?"** 
A: First get her name deleted from her parental ration card (with marriage certificate), then 
apply for addition to your family card via portal or Tehsil/Block office with marriage certificate 
and her Aadhaar. 
 
**Q: "Fingerprint nahi lag raha, ration kaise milega?"** 
A: Try alternate finger or iris scan; if failure persists, request manual exception process at 
FPS through Supply Inspector, or check if OTP-based authentication is available as 
alternative. 
 
**Q: "UP ka ration card hai, Delhi me ration milega?"** 
A: Yes, via One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) — ensure Aadhaar is seeded with your 
UP card, then authenticate at any ONORC-enabled FPS in Delhi. 
 
**Q: "Dealer ration nahi de raha."** 
A: File complaint with local Supply Inspector immediately, citing card number and FPS code; 
escalate to District Supply Officer if unresolved. 
 
**Q: "Mera naam list se hat gaya, kya karun?"** 
A: Check portal for status/reason of removal (could be e-KYC failure, verification issue, or 
duplicate flag); visit Tehsil/DSO office with your card details to inquire and file restoration 
request if wrongful. 
 
**Q: "Father ki death ho gayi, HoF kaise change hoga?"** 
A: Submit death certificate along with HoF change application at Tehsil/Block office or via 
portal; new HoF (typically next eligible adult member) gets updated after verification. 
 
**Q: "Newborn ka naam kaise add hoga?"** 
A: Apply for member addition with the child's birth certificate; Aadhaar can often be added 
later if not immediately available (verify local provision). 
 
**Q: "Aadhaar me naam aur ration card me naam different hai, kya karein?"** 
A: Correct the mismatched name in either the Aadhaar record (via UIDAI) or ration card 
record (via correction module) so both match — necessary for successful 
seeding/authentication.

## TOPIC 49: COMPARISON QUESTIONS 
 
**AAY vs PHH:**

AAY targets poorest-of-poor with fixed household entitlement; PHH covers broader eligible 
households with per-person entitlement. 
 
**Ration Card vs NFSA Eligibility:** 
Holding a ration card doesn't automatically mean NFSA coverage — NFSA eligibility 
(PHH/AAY tagging) determines subsidized entitlement; some cards may exist without active 
NFSA benefit status. 
 
**BPL vs AAY:** 
BPL is an older, broader poverty classification; AAY is a specific NFSA sub-category for the 
most vulnerable, replacing much of the old BPL-based targeting for ration purposes. 
 
**Portability vs Transfer:** 
Portability (ONORC) is temporary — access ration anywhere without changing home 
records; Transfer is permanent — updates your card's home address/FPS entirely. 
 
**Aadhaar Seeding vs e-KYC:** 
Seeding is the one-time linking of Aadhaar to the ration card record; e-KYC is a periodic 
re-verification process (often using the already-seeded Aadhaar) to confirm the beneficiary is 
still active/eligible. 
 
**Application Number vs Ration Card Number:** 
Application number is a temporary tracking ID issued at the time of applying (used until the 
card is approved); Ration Card number is the permanent identifier assigned once the card is 
generated.

# SECTION 1: INCOME CERTIFICATE (आय प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** An Income Certificate is an official document issued by the UP Revenue 
Department certifying the annual income of an individual or family, used for availing 
government schemes, scholarships, EWS benefits, fee concessions, and other 
income-based eligibility purposes. 
 
**Who Can Apply:** 
- Any permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh. 
- Head of family or individual member requiring income proof for personal or scheme-related 
purposes. 
- Students (for scholarship purposes). 
- Parents on behalf of minor children where applicable. 
 
**Eligibility Requirements:** 
- Applicant must be a resident of UP (with valid residence proof). 
- Must declare accurate family income from all sources. 
- No minimum age restriction, though certificates for minors are typically issued reflecting 
parental/guardian income. 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Aadhaar card of applicant. 
2. Residence proof (voter ID, electricity bill, ration card, etc.). 
3. Self-declaration of income / affidavit. 
4. Salary slip (for salaried individuals) or business proof (for self-employed). 
5. Land records (Khatauni) if agricultural income is being declared. 
6. Passport-size photograph. 
7. Bank passbook (in some cases, for cross-verification). 
 
**How Family Income Is Calculated:**

- Sum of income of all earning members residing in the same household under one ration 
card/family unit. 
- Includes salary, business profit, agricultural income, pension, and other regular income 
sources. 
- Excludes one-time gifts/windfalls in most standard calculations (verify specific scheme 
rules as this can vary by purpose — e.g., EWS has its own income definition, see Section 4). 
 
**Whose Income Is Included:** 
- Self, spouse, dependent children, and co-residing parents (if applicable) are typically 
included. 
- Married daughters/sons living separately are generally excluded from the parental 
household income calculation. 
- Definition of "family" may vary slightly depending on the purpose of the certificate 
(scholarship vs EWS vs general purpose) — always check the specific scheme's family 
definition. 
 
**Purpose-Specific Variants:** 
- **For Students/Scholarships:** Often requires income certificate specifically formatted per 
the scholarship scheme's (State/Central) requirement; some scholarship portals have 
integrated income-verification directly with e-District. 
- **For EWS:** Separate detailed criteria apply (see Section 4) — EWS has its own 
income/asset thresholds distinct from general income certificate purpose. 
- **For Government Schemes:** Format and validity period may be scheme-specific; always 
check the requesting department's certificate format requirement. 
 
**Application Process:** 
 
*Online:* 
1. Visit UP e-District portal. 
2. Register/login using mobile number and create citizen account. 
3. Select "Income Certificate" service. 
4. Fill applicant and family income details. 
5. Upload required documents. 
6. Submit and note the **Application/Reference Number**. 
7. Application routed to Lekhpal → Revenue Inspector → Tehsildar/SDM for verification and 
approval. 
 
*Offline:* 
1. Visit the Tehsil office. 
2. Obtain and fill the physical application form. 
3. Attach required documents. 
4. Submit to the concerned Revenue Clerk/Tehsildar office. 
5. Collect acknowledgment receipt with application number. 
 
*Via Jan Seva Kendra/CSC:* 
1. Visit nearest CSC/Jan Seva Kendra with documents. 
2. Operator fills the online application on your behalf. 
3. Pay applicable service charge.

4. Collect receipt/application number printout. 
 
**Fees:** Nominal government fee plus CSC service charge if applied offline through a 
center. *(Verify current amount — this is one of the most frequently revised figures.)* 
 
**Processing Time:** Typically involves multi-stage verification (Lekhpal field verification → 
Revenue Inspector → Tehsildar approval); official timeline is specified under UP Right to 
Public Service Act (Lok Seva Adhikar Adhiniyam). *(Verify current SLA days.)* 
 
**Certificate Validity:** Income certificates typically have a limited validity period (commonly 
tied to financial year) — must be renewed for continued use in subsequent scheme 
applications. *(Verify current validity period, as this varies by purpose too.)* 
 
**Renewal Procedure:** Same as fresh application process; some portals allow renewal 
request referencing the old certificate number for faster processing. 
 
**Status Tracking:** 
1. Visit e-District portal's "Track Application Status" section. 
2. Enter application number or registered mobile number. 
3. View status: Submitted → Under Verification (Lekhpal) → Forwarded (Revenue Inspector) 
→ Approved (Tehsildar/SDM) → Certificate Generated. 
 
**Downloading the Certificate:** 
- Once approved, certificate is available for download as a **digitally signed PDF** from the 
portal using application number/certificate number. 
 
**Certificate Verification:** 
- Certificates carry a unique certificate number and often a QR code for online verification via 
the portal's "Verify Certificate" tool. 
 
**Lost Application Number:** Retrievable via registered mobile number search on the portal, 
or by visiting the Tehsil office with identity proof. 
 
**Corrections (Name/Address/Income):** 
- If error is discovered before approval: request correction during verification stage via 
Lekhpal/Tehsil office. 
- If error discovered after certificate issuance: file a correction application with supporting 
proof; may require fresh verification cycle. 
 
**Wrong Income Entered:** Submit correction request with accurate income proof; may 
trigger re-verification by Revenue Inspector. 
 
**Rejection Reasons:** 
- Incomplete/mismatched documents. 
- Income declared inconsistent with verifiable records (e.g., land holding suggests higher 
agricultural income). 
- Residence verification failure. 
- Duplicate application already in process.

**Reapplication After Rejection:** Correct the specific deficiency and resubmit; or file an 
appeal with SDM if rejection is disputed as incorrect. 
 
**Verification by Revenue Authorities:** Lekhpal conducts field verification (may include 
neighbor/local inquiry); Revenue Inspector reviews Lekhpal's report; Tehsildar/SDM gives 
final approval and digital signature. 
 
**Duplicate Certificate:** Can be re-downloaded anytime from the portal using 
application/certificate number (digital copies don't typically require a separate "duplicate" fee 
like physical documents used to). 
 
**Digitally Signed Certificate:** Current UP e-District certificates are issued with digital 
signatures, making them valid for most official purposes without requiring physical stamping 
— verify acceptance policy with the specific requesting authority (some still prefer physical 
certified copies). 
 
**Complaint/Grievance Procedure:** File grievance via e-District portal's grievance module, 
or escalate to SDM/District Magistrate office for unresolved delays or errors. 
 
**Fake Certificate Consequences:** Submitting false income information for certificate 
issuance can lead to certificate cancellation, benefit recovery, and legal action under 
applicable fraud provisions (IPC sections related to forgery/false declaration may apply). 
 
**Common Portal Errors:** 
- "Application not found" — recheck application number format. 
- "Document upload failed" — check file size/format requirements. 
- "OTP not received" — verify registered mobile number is active. 
 
**Official Source:** UP e-District Portal; UP Revenue Department guidelines; UP Right to 
Public Service Act timelines.

# SECTION 2: CASTE CERTIFICATE (जाति प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** An official document certifying an individual's caste/community status 
(SC/ST/OBC), issued by the Revenue Department, used for reservation benefits in 
education, employment, and government schemes. 
 
**Who Needs One:** 
- Individuals belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), or Other Backward 
Class (OBC) communities seeking to avail reservation benefits. 
 
**Types:** 
1. **SC Certificate** — For communities listed in the State/Central SC list. 
2. **ST Certificate** — For communities listed in the State/Central ST list. 
3. **OBC Certificate** — For communities listed in the State/Central OBC list.

**Eligibility:** 
- Belonging to a caste/community officially recognized in the applicable SC/ST/OBC list for 
Uttar Pradesh. 
- Caste is typically determined by paternal lineage (father's caste), with exceptions/special 
provisions in certain cases (e.g., inter-caste marriage scenarios — subject to specific legal 
precedents and state rules). 
 
**Recognized Caste/Community Lists:** UP maintains its own State List of SC/ST/OBC 
communities, which should be cross-checked against the Central List, as they are not 
always identical (see comparison in this section below). 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Aadhaar card. 
2. Residence proof. 
3. **Proof of caste** — parent's/grandparent's caste certificate, or other historical 
caste-linked documents (old school records, land records mentioning caste, community 
certificates from earlier generations). 
4. Father's caste certificate (strongly preferred where available). 
5. Self-declaration affidavit if no prior family certificate exists. 
6. Photograph. 
 
**What If Parents Don't Have Certificates:** 
- Applicant can submit alternate historical evidence: old revenue records, school leaving 
certificates mentioning caste, voter list entries, or community-based documentary evidence. 
- Local Lekhpal/Revenue Inspector conducts field-level inquiry, sometimes including 
statements from village elders/community members, to establish caste veracity in absence 
of documentary proof. 
 
**Application Process:** 
 
*Online:* Same general e-District flow as Income Certificate — select "Caste Certificate" 
service, fill details, upload documents, submit. 
 
*Offline:* Apply at Tehsil office with physical form and documents. 
 
*CSC/Jan Seva Kendra:* Assisted application submission for a service charge. 
 
**Verification Procedure:** 
1. Lekhpal conducts field verification (may include community/neighbor inquiry, especially in 
absence of parental certificate). 
2. Revenue Inspector reviews. 
3. Tehsildar/SDM gives final approval. 
 
**Tehsil/Revenue Authority Role:** Primary verification and issuance authority chain: Lekhpal 
→ Revenue Inspector → Tehsildar → SDM (final signing authority in most cases). 
 
**Application Status:** Trackable via e-District portal using application number.

**Processing Time:** Multi-stage verification; may take longer than income certificate due to 
more rigorous caste-verification requirements, especially without documented family history. 
*(Verify current SLA.)* 
 
**Fees:** Nominal government fee + CSC charge if applicable. *(Verify current rate.)* 
 
**Download Certificate:** Digitally signed PDF downloadable from portal post-approval. 
 
**Digital Verification:** QR code/certificate number based verification via portal. 
 
**Certificate Validity:** Caste certificates are generally valid permanently (caste doesn't 
change), but many institutions/employers require certificates issued within a recent 
timeframe (e.g., last 6 months to 1 year) for specific application purposes — **this is an 
institutional requirement, not inherent certificate expiry**. 
 
**Renewal Requirements:** Not typically "renewed" in the traditional sense since caste 
status doesn't expire, but a fresh certificate may be requested if the old one is outdated per a 
specific scheme's requirement. 
 
**Correction:** Name/spelling/address corrections follow standard correction process (see 
Section 15) with supporting proof. 
 
**Duplicate/Reissue:** Available via portal re-download; physical duplicate can be requested 
at Tehsil office if needed. 
 
**Rejected Application — Common Reasons:** 
- Caste not found in official State/Central list for UP. 
- Insufficient proof linking applicant to claimed caste. 
- Father's certificate contradicts claimed caste. 
- Verification inquiry inconclusive. 
 
**Caste Not Appearing in Records:** If the community name has a regional/spelling variant 
not matching the official list, applicant may need to provide additional documentary linkage 
or seek official clarification on the correct recognized nomenclature from the Social Welfare 
Department. 
 
**Migration-Related Cases:** Persons who migrated from another state face additional 
scrutiny since caste-list recognition varies by state (a community recognized as OBC in one 
state may not be recognized identically in UP) — requires establishing UP-specific eligibility, 
not just carrying over the other state's certificate. 
 
**Married Person's Certificate Issues:** 
- A married woman's caste certificate is generally based on her father's (natal family) caste, 
not the husband's, as per prevailing legal position in most contexts — though usage/context 
(e.g., for her children) may reference the father's (husband's) caste. This is a nuanced area 
— always verify current judicial/administrative guidance.

**Difference: Caste Certificate vs Category Certificate:** 
- "Caste Certificate" specifically certifies caste/community name. 
- "Category Certificate" broadly may refer to the same document when used to establish 
reservation category (SC/ST/OBC) eligibility for a specific purpose (jobs/admissions) — in 
practice, these terms are often used interchangeably in UP context, but some institutions 
distinguish based on format requirements. 
 
**OBC Certificate vs OBC-NCL (Non-Creamy Layer):** 
- A standard **OBC Certificate** certifies caste/community status only. 
- **OBC-NCL Certificate** additionally certifies that the applicant's family does NOT fall in the 
"creamy layer" (income/status threshold above which OBC reservation benefits don't apply) 
— required specifically for reservation benefits in central government jobs/admissions. 
- OBC-NCL has its own income/asset threshold and validity period (typically needs to be 
recent — commonly renewed annually) distinct from the basic caste certificate. 
 
**State List vs Central List Questions:** 
- UP's **State OBC List** applies for state government jobs/admissions/schemes. 
- The **Central OBC List** applies for central government jobs/admissions/schemes. 
- A community may be listed in one but not the other — applicants must verify which list 
applies to their specific purpose and request the certificate accordingly (certificate format 
explicitly states State List or Central List applicability). 
 
**Grievance/Appeal Process:** File appeal with SDM/District Magistrate if caste verification 
is disputed; further escalation possible to Divisional Commissioner or through Social Welfare 
Department grievance channels; legal recourse available in prolonged disputes. 
 
**Official Source:** UP Social Welfare Department caste list notifications; UP Revenue 
Department caste certificate issuance guidelines; Central List of OBCs (National 
Commission for Backward Classes).

# SECTION 3: RESIDENCE / DOMICILE CERTIFICATE (निवास प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR 
PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** 
- **Residence Certificate:** Confirms an individual currently resides at a specific address 
within UP. 
- **Domicile Certificate:** Confirms an individual is a permanent resident/domicile of the 
State of UP, often required for state-quota admissions, state government jobs, and certain 
scheme eligibilities. 
 
**Difference Between Residence and Domicile:** 
| Aspect | Residence Certificate | Domicile Certificate | 
|---|---|---| 
| Purpose | Confirms current address | Confirms permanent state belonging | 
| Duration emphasis | Current living location | Long-term/permanent state residency | 
| Common use | Local administrative purposes | State quota admissions, state jobs |

*(Note: In practice, many UP processes issue a combined "Residence/Domicile" certificate 
— check specific requesting authority's exact terminology requirement.)* 
 
**Who Qualifies as a UP Resident:** 
- Individuals who have resided in UP for a specified continuous period (duration requirement 
varies by purpose — some domicile certificates require multi-year residency proof, e.g., 
commonly cited as several years of continuous residence, though exact duration should be 
verified from current rules). 
- Persons born in UP to UP-resident families. 
- Persons who have relocated to UP and established long-term residence with supporting 
documentation. 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Continuous residence in UP for the required minimum duration (verify current requirement 
— this varies for different certificate purposes, e.g., education quota vs employment). 
- Valid address proof within UP. 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Aadhaar card. 
2. Address proof (electricity bill, voter ID, rent agreement, property documents). 
3. School leaving certificate/educational records showing UP address history (helpful for 
establishing duration). 
4. Parent's residence/domicile proof (for minors/students applying through parents). 
5. Affidavit of residence. 
6. Photograph. 
 
**Minor/Student Applications:** Typically applied for through parents/guardians, using 
parental address proof and the minor's birth certificate/school records as supporting 
documents. 
 
**Married Applicant Cases:** A married woman may need to establish residence based on 
her husband's UP address (post-marriage domicile) — requires marriage certificate + 
husband's residence proof, distinct from her natal family's domicile status. 
 
**People Born Outside UP But Residing in UP:** Can apply for UP residence/domicile 
certificate by demonstrating sufficient continuous residence duration with supporting 
documents (school records, rental history, utility bills over years, employment records in UP). 
 
**UP Resident Studying/Working Outside the State:** Generally remains eligible for UP 
domicile certificate as long as permanent family residence/address remains in UP; 
temporary residence outside for education/employment typically doesn't affect domicile 
status, but specific proof of permanent UP address must be maintained. 
 
**Application Process:** 
 
*Online:* Via e-District portal — select Residence/Domicile Certificate service, fill details, 
upload documents, submit.

*Offline:* Tehsil office application with physical form. 
 
*Jan Seva Kendra:* Assisted submission for service charge. 
 
**Fees:** Nominal government fee + CSC charge if applicable. *(Verify current rate.)* 
 
**Processing Time:** Standard multi-stage verification (Lekhpal → Revenue Inspector → 
Tehsildar/SDM); *(verify current SLA)*. 
 
**Verification:** Field verification by Lekhpal to confirm actual residence at declared address; 
may include neighbor/local inquiry for duration confirmation. 
 
**Status Tracking:** Via e-District portal using application number. 
 
**Downloading Certificate:** Digitally signed PDF post-approval. 
 
**Validity:** Residence certificates often have limited validity for specific scheme use 
(commonly tied to purpose requirement); domicile certificates for permanent status purposes 
may have longer/indefinite validity but institutions may still request recently-issued copies. 
*(Verify current validity norms.)* 
 
**Renewal:** Fresh application following the same process if validity has lapsed for the 
intended purpose. 
 
**Correction:** Standard correction process (Section 15) for name/address/spelling errors. 
 
**Duplicate/Reissue:** Re-download via portal, or fresh application at Tehsil office. 
 
**Address Change:** If applicant has moved address within UP after certificate issuance, 
may need a fresh certificate reflecting updated address for continued use — old certificate 
doesn't automatically update. 
 
**Rejection Reasons:** 
- Insufficient proof of required residence duration. 
- Address verification failure (Lekhpal unable to confirm residence). 
- Document inconsistency (e.g., conflicting addresses across submitted documents). 
 
**Grievance Process:** File via e-District grievance module or escalate to SDM/DM office for 
unresolved issues. 
 
**Official Source:** UP Revenue Department residence/domicile certificate guidelines.

# SECTION 4: EWS CERTIFICATE (आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR PRADESH

**Important Framing Note:** EWS (Economically Weaker Section) reservation was 
introduced via the **103rd Constitutional Amendment (Central provision)**, applicable to 
those NOT covered under existing SC/ST/OBC reservation. States, including UP, issue EWS 
certificates following the Central income/asset criteria framework, but the **issuance 
procedure, format, and authority is State-specific**. This distinction must always be kept 
clear in answers. 
 
**What Is EWS:** A reservation category for economically weaker individuals belonging to 
the General/Unreserved category (i.e., those not already covered by SC/ST/OBC 
reservation), providing them reservation benefits in education and government employment. 
 
**Who Qualifies for EWS:** 
- Must belong to a category NOT covered under existing SC/ST/OBC reservation. 
- Must meet the prescribed income and asset threshold criteria (Central government notified 
criteria, adopted by UP for state-level issuance). 
 
**EWS Eligibility in Uttar Pradesh:** 
- Family gross annual income below the Central-notified threshold (commonly cited threshold 
exists — **verify current exact figure from official notification**, as this is a fixed number that 
should NOT be guessed). 
- Family should not own/possess notified categories of assets beyond specified limits (see 
asset conditions below). 
 
**Income Requirements:** Combined family income from all sources (salary, business, 
agriculture, profession) below the notified annual threshold. **(Exact figure must be verified 
from current official EWS notification before publishing — do not estimate.)** 
 
**Asset/Property Conditions (General Central Criteria Framework — verify exact figures):** 
- Agricultural land beyond a specified limit disqualifies the family. 
- Residential flat/plot beyond specified area thresholds (varies for notified municipal vs 
non-municipal areas) disqualifies the family. 
- These thresholds are specified precisely in the Central EWS notification and adopted by 
states — **must be verified and inserted with exact figures, not approximated.** 
 
**Family Definition (for EWS purposes):** Includes applicant, parents, siblings (unmarried), 
spouse, and children — a specific definition distinct from general "household" definitions 
used elsewhere; must reflect the exact wording of the EWS notification. 
 
**Whose Income Counts:** 
- **Salary income:** Of all family members as defined above. 
- **Business income:** Net business income of family members. 
- **Agricultural income:** Included in overall family income calculation for EWS (unlike some 
other schemes where it may be treated separately). 
- **Property/Assets:** Considered separately from income — asset thresholds apply 
independently of income threshold (i.e., a family could have low income but still be 
disqualified due to asset holding above the limit).

**Agricultural Land & Residential Property Conditions:** Specific area/size thresholds apply 
(in acres for agricultural land; in square feet for residential plots/flats, varying by 
municipal/non-municipal classification) — **these exact figures must be sourced from the 
current official notification.** 
 
**Special Applicant Scenarios:** 
- **Applicant dependent on parents:** EWS eligibility assessed based on parental family 
income/assets. 
- **Student EWS certificate:** Issued reflecting parental family's income/asset status (student 
typically has no independent income). 
- **Unemployed applicant:** Eligibility based on family (parental/spousal) income, not 
personal income (since unemployed = no personal income). 
- **Married applicant:** Eligibility assessed based on the applicant's own new family unit 
(spouse + children), not the natal family, post-marriage. 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Aadhaar card. 
2. Income proof — self-declaration/affidavit, salary slips, business income proof, agricultural 
income record. 
3. Property-related documents — land records (Khatauni), property registration papers (to 
verify against asset thresholds). 
4. Residence proof. 
5. Caste-related self-declaration confirming NOT belonging to SC/ST/OBC category. 
6. Photograph. 
 
**Application Process:** 
1. Apply via e-District portal (or Tehsil office) selecting "EWS Certificate" service. 
2. Fill income and asset declaration details. 
3. Upload supporting documents. 
4. Submit for verification. 
 
**Issuing Authority:** Typically Tehsildar/SDM level, following Lekhpal field verification of 
both income and asset (land) claims — asset verification often requires cross-check with 
land records (Bhulekh) directly. 
 
**Verification:** More rigorous than standard income certificate due to dual income+asset 
verification requirement; Lekhpal verifies land holdings against Khatauni records specifically. 
 
**Certificate Format:** Follows the standard Central government-prescribed EWS certificate 
format (as adopted for state issuance) — includes specific declarations about income/asset 
compliance. 
 
**Validity Period:** EWS certificates are typically valid for the **financial year** in which 
issued (i.e., need to be freshly issued each year/application cycle) — **this is a key point of 
confusion for users; validity is much shorter than caste certificates and must be clearly 
explained.** *(Verify exact current validity rule.)*

**Financial-Year Issues:** Because EWS certificate validity is tied to financial year, a 
certificate issued in one financial year may not be accepted for an application/admission 
cycle in the next financial year — applicants often need to reapply annually. 
 
**Renewal:** Effectively a fresh application each cycle due to financial-year-bound validity. 
 
**EWS for Admissions:** Educational institutions (following Central/State EWS quota) 
require a recently-issued EWS certificate matching the specific academic year's requirement. 
 
**EWS for Government Recruitment:** Similarly requires a currently-valid EWS certificate 
matching the recruitment cycle's specified financial year. 
 
**State vs Central Requirements:** While the income/asset criteria originate from Central 
notification, **UP issues its own EWS certificates for UP-domiciled applicants**, and the 
format/issuing authority follows UP Revenue Department procedure — a certificate issued 
by another state may not be automatically valid for UP-specific purposes without UP 
domicile establishment. 
 
**Application Status:** Trackable via e-District portal. 
 
**Correction:** Standard correction process for name/address errors; income/asset 
corrections require re-verification. 
 
**Rejection Reasons:** 
- Income above threshold. 
- Asset (land/property) above specified limit. 
- Applicant belongs to SC/ST/OBC category (ineligible for EWS by definition). 
- Documentation insufficient to verify claims. 
 
**Appeal/Grievance:** File with SDM/DM office; escalate through e-District grievance 
module. 
 
**False Information Consequences:** Providing false income/asset declarations for EWS 
certificate constitutes fraud, leading to certificate cancellation, disqualification from the 
benefit already availed (e.g., admission/job), and potential legal action. 
 
**Difference: EWS vs Income Certificate:** 
| Aspect | EWS Certificate | Income Certificate | 
|---|---|---| 
| Purpose | Reservation benefit for economically weak General category | General income 
proof for various purposes | 
| Criteria | Income AND asset thresholds (dual criteria) | Income only | 
| Validity | Financial-year bound (short) | Typically longer, purpose-dependent | 
| Eligibility restriction | Must NOT be SC/ST/OBC | No caste restriction | 
 
**Difference: EWS vs OBC-NCL:** 
| Aspect | EWS | OBC-NCL | 
|---|---|---|

| Applicable category | General/Unreserved category only | OBC category only | 
| Criteria basis | Income + asset thresholds | Income/status threshold (creamy layer criteria) | 
| Purpose | New reservation category for General category poor | Ensures only 
non-creamy-layer OBC avail OBC reservation | 
 
**Critical RAG Instruction:** Always clearly separate **Central EWS eligibility criteria 
(income/asset thresholds — fixed numbers from Central notification)** from **UP-specific 
issuance procedure (Tehsil-level application, Lekhpal verification, e-District portal process)**. 
Do not blend the two into a single unclear statement — users need to know which part is 
nationally fixed and which part is state-process-specific. 
 
**Official Source:** Central Government EWS reservation notification (103rd Constitutional 
Amendment framework); UP Revenue Department EWS issuance guidelines (state-adopted 
procedure).

# SECTION 5: BIRTH CERTIFICATE (जन्म प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** A legal document recording the birth of a child, issued under the Registration 
of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, serving as primary proof of age, identity, and citizenship. 
 
**Registration of Birth:** 
- Every birth occurring in UP must be registered with the concerned registration authority. 
 
**Where Birth Is Registered:** 
- **Hospital birth:** Hospital typically initiates registration process with the local registrar 
(Municipal/Nagar Nigam in urban areas, Gram Panchayat in rural areas). 
- **Home birth:** Parents/family member must report the birth to the local registrar (Gram 
Panchayat Secretary/local Anganwadi/health worker in rural areas; Municipal registrar in 
urban areas). 
 
**Rural vs Urban Registration Authority:** 
- **Rural:** Gram Panchayat (Panchayat Secretary as local registrar). 
- **Urban:** Nagar Nigam/Nagar Palika Parishad/Nagar Panchayat (Municipal Health 
Officer/designated Registrar). 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Hospital birth report (if born in hospital) or attending health worker's certification (if home 
birth). 
2. Parents' Aadhaar cards. 
3. Parents' marriage certificate (in some cases, for record linkage). 
4. Address proof. 
5. Affidavit (for delayed registration cases). 
 
**Child Without Aadhaar:** Birth certificate does NOT require the child to already have 
Aadhaar — in fact, birth certificate is typically a prerequisite document used to later apply for 
the child's Aadhaar.

**Name Addition:** 
- Many birth registrations initially occur without the child's name (especially if registered very 
soon after birth, before naming ceremony). 
- **Name addition** can be done later through a formal request to the registrar within the 
permitted timeframe, submitting the chosen name for official record update. 
 
**Corrections:** 
- **Name correction, Parent-name correction, DOB correction, Address correction:** All 
require submission of a correction application with supporting documentary evidence 
(hospital records, Aadhaar, affidavit) to the concerned Registrar/Sub-Registrar office; may 
require additional verification for significant discrepancies (e.g., DOB changes). 
 
**Delayed Registration:** 
- Births not registered within the standard prescribed period (typically within 21 days as per 
the Act) require **delayed registration** procedure, involving additional documentation 
(affidavit, sometimes a court order or higher administrative authority approval for very old 
delays) and potentially a late fee. 
 
**Very Old Unregistered Birth:** 
- For births several years/decades old with no prior registration, applicant needs to approach 
the District Registrar/authorized authority with substantial supporting evidence (school 
records, affidavits, other historical documents) — process is more rigorous, potentially 
requiring an order from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate or designated authority. 
 
**Late-Registration Requirements:** Increasing levels of documentation/authority approval 
required as the delay period increases (e.g., registration within 30 days may need simple 
affidavit; registration after 1 year may need SDM-level order — **verify current tiered timeline 
from Registration of Births & Deaths Rules as applicable in UP**). 
 
**Fees:** Nominal registration fee; late registration typically attracts an additional late fee 
(increasing with delay duration). *(Verify current fee schedule.)* 
 
**Online Availability:** UP provides online birth certificate application/download via e-District 
or dedicated Civil Registration System (CRS) portal integration. 
 
**Download:** Digitally signed birth certificate downloadable using registration 
number/application reference. 
 
**Verification:** Certificate carries a unique registration number for verification via the 
CRS/e-District portal. 
 
**Duplicate Certificate:** Can be requested online (portal re-download) or offline at the 
registering authority's office using original registration details. 
 
**Lost Certificate:** Retrieve registration number via portal search (using child's 
name/DOB/parents' details) or visit the original registering office.

**Digitally Issued Certificate:** Current system supports digitally signed certificates valid for 
most official purposes. 
 
**Application/Status Issues:** Trackable via portal using application/registration number. 
 
**Rejection:** Rare for standard timely registration; delayed registration requests may be 
rejected if insufficient supporting evidence is provided — requires additional documentation 
and reapplication. 
 
**Grievances:** File with the Chief Registrar (Births & Deaths)/District Registrar office for 
unresolved registration issues. 
 
**Official Source:** Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969; UP Civil Registration 
System (CRS); UP e-District portal.

# SECTION 6: DEATH CERTIFICATE (मृत्यु प्रमाण पत्र) — UTTAR PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** A legal document certifying the date, place, and cause (where recorded) of an 
individual's death, required for legal, financial, and administrative closure purposes. 
 
**Who Reports/Registers a Death:** 
- **Hospital death:** Hospital authority typically initiates registration with the local registrar. 
- **Home death:** Family member/nearest relative must report to the local registrar (Gram 
Panchayat in rural areas; Municipal body in urban areas). 
 
**Documents Required:** 
1. Applicant's (relative's) Aadhaar card and ID proof. 
2. Deceased's Aadhaar card (if available). 
3. Hospital death report/medical certificate of cause of death (if applicable). 
4. Cremation/burial ground certificate (in some registration processes). 
5. Relationship proof of applicant to deceased. 
 
**Applicant/Relative Requirements:** Typically the nearest family member (spouse, child, 
parent) can apply; in absence of family, a witness to the death or the institution 
(hospital/old-age home) where death occurred may report. 
 
**Registration Authority:** 
- **Rural:** Gram Panchayat Secretary (local registrar). 
- **Urban:** Nagar Nigam/Nagar Palika Health Officer/designated Registrar. 
 
**Registration Deadline:** Death must be reported within a prescribed period from the date 
of occurrence (typically within 21 days as per the Registration of Births and Deaths Act) — 
beyond this, delayed registration procedure applies. 
 
**Delayed Registration:** Requires additional affidavit and, for significantly delayed cases, 
higher authority approval (similar tiered structure as birth delayed registration).

**Old/Unregistered Death:** For deaths that occurred long ago without registration, applicant 
must approach the District Registrar with substantial supporting evidence and potentially 
higher administrative approval. 
 
**Corrections:** Name/date/place corrections require a formal correction application with 
supporting proof (medical records, other official documents) submitted to the registering 
authority. 
 
**Online Application/Search:** Available via UP CRS/e-District portal for both application 
submission and certificate search/download. 
 
**Download:** Digitally signed death certificate downloadable via portal using registration 
number. 
 
**Duplicate Copies:** Requestable online (portal) or offline at the registering office. 
 
**Fees:** Nominal registration/duplicate fee; late registration attracts additional fee. *(Verify 
current rates.)* 
 
**Verification:** Certificate verification via unique registration number on portal. 
 
**Uses of Death Certificate:** 
- **Pension closure:** Required to stop pension disbursement of deceased and/or initiate 
family pension for eligible dependents. 
- **Bank/legal uses:** Required for closing bank accounts, claiming insurance, and legal 
succession processes. 
- **Property/inheritance-related uses:** Essential document for initiating mutation 
(Dakhil-Kharij) of land records in favor of legal heirs (see Section 9). 
- **Ration card member deletion:** Required to remove the deceased's name from the 
household ration card (see Ration/PDS domain, Topic 26). 
- **Government benefit updates:** Required to update/discontinue any government scheme 
benefits registered to the deceased. 
 
**Grievances:** File with Chief Registrar (Births & Deaths)/District Registrar for unresolved 
issues. 
 
**Official Source:** Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969; UP Civil Registration 
System; UP e-District portal.

# SECTION 7: FAMILY REGISTER / PARIVAR REGISTER — UTTAR PRADESH 
 
**Definition:** The Family Register (Parivar Register) is a rural administrative record 
maintained at the Gram Panchayat level, listing all households and their family members in a 
village — historically used as a foundational record for identity, residence, and family 
relationship verification in rural UP.

**Who Maintains It:** Gram Panchayat (through the Panchayat Secretary/Lekhpal), 
specifically applicable in **rural areas** of UP. 
 
**Rural Applicability:** This register is primarily a rural instrument; urban areas rely on 
municipal records/other documents for equivalent purposes (urban areas typically don't 
maintain an identical "Parivar Register" system). 
 
**Updates to Family Register:** 
- **Family member addition:** New birth, marriage-in (daughter-in-law), or other new 
member joining household — reported to Panchayat Secretary/Lekhpal for record update. 
- **Member deletion:** Death, marriage-out (daughter), or permanent migration — reported 
for removal from the register. 
- **Birth update:** Reflects new birth registration in family record. 
- **Death update:** Reflects death registration, removing member from active family listing. 
- **Marriage update:** Reflects marital status changes affecting household composition. 
- **Family separation:** When a joint family splits into separate households, requires 
updating/creating separate family register entries. 
- **Head-of-family change:** Similar triggers as ration card HoF change (death, 
restructuring) requiring corresponding Parivar Register update. 
 
**Name/Address Correction:** Submitted to Panchayat Secretary/Lekhpal with supporting 
documents for record correction. 
 
**Documents Required (for updates):** 
1. Relevant life-event certificate (birth/death/marriage certificate). 
2. Aadhaar card of concerned members. 
3. Application/request letter to Gram Panchayat. 
 
**Certified Copy:** A certified copy of the Family Register extract can be requested from the 
Gram Panchayat/Tehsil office for official use. 
 
**Application Procedure:** 
1. Submit application to Gram Panchayat Secretary/Lekhpal (offline, as this is primarily a 
manual/local record, though some digitization efforts may allow online request in certain 
districts). 
2. Attach supporting documents for the specific update/certified copy request. 
3. Local verification by Lekhpal. 
4. Updated record/certified copy issued. 
 
**Fees:** Nominal fee for certified copy issuance. *(Verify current local rate — this can vary 
by Panchayat.)* 
 
**Processing Time:** Varies by Panchayat administrative efficiency; generally a 
locally-handled process without a strict centralized SLA (verify if digitized in your specific 
district for standard timelines).

**Verification:** Lekhpal-level local verification, cross-referenced with other civil registration 
records (birth/death/marriage certificates) where available. 
 
**Uses of Family-Register Copy:** 
- Supporting document for various certificate applications (residence, caste, income) in rural 
areas. 
- Historical family relationship proof in absence of other documentation. 
- Supporting evidence in land inheritance/succession matters. 
 
**Disputes/Errors:** Common issues include outdated entries, missing updates, or clerical 
errors — resolved through application to Gram Panchayat/Lekhpal with corrective evidence. 
 
**Complaint Procedure:** Escalate unresolved Family Register issues to the Block 
Development Officer (BDO) or Tehsildar if Gram Panchayat-level resolution is inadequate. 
 
**Official Source:** UP Panchayati Raj Department Family Register maintenance guidelines.
