## FINAL NOTE ON DATA ACCURACY — AGRICULTURE DOMAIN SPECIFIC RISK 
 
This domain carries the **highest risk of outdated-information harm** among the three 
domains built so far, because: 
 
1. **Money is directly at stake for farmers** — an incorrect MSP rate, subsidy percentage, or 
premium figure could cause direct financial loss or missed opportunity. 
2. **Deadlines are hard cut-offs** — unlike some certificate corrections which can be redone 
anytime, missing a PMFBY enrollment deadline or procurement registration window means 
NO recourse until the next season. 
3. **Notified lists change every cycle** — PMFBY notified crops/districts, procurement 
centres, and scheme-active status are NOT stable year-to-year and must never be treated 
as permanent facts. 
 
**Before publishing the final PDF, verify and insert current figures for (non-exhaustive priority 
list):** 
- PM-KISAN installment amount and current exclusion criteria thresholds 
- KCC interest subvention rate and prompt-repayment incentive rate 
- PMFBY premium rates (Kharif/Rabi/commercial-horticultural), notified crop-district-season 
list, enrollment deadlines 
- Farm machinery/equipment subsidy percentages and caps (current scheme year) 
- Current MSP rates for wheat, paddy, and other procured crops 
- Sugarcane State Advised Price (SAP) for current season 
- SDRF/NDRF crop-loss compensation rates 
- PM-KUSUM farmer contribution percentage and pump cost slabs 
- Current landholding thresholds for marginal/small farmer classification 
- All application/registration window dates (season and year specific) 
 
**Recommended verification sources:** 
- pmkisan.gov.in 
- pmfby.gov.in 
- upagriculture.com (UP Agriculture Department) 
- upbhulekh.gov.in 
- UP Cane Department (Ganna Vibhag) portal 
- Current season's UP Government Agriculture-related Government Orders 
- CACP/Ministry of Agriculture MSP notifications (season-specific press releases)

## 1. UP Scholarship System Basics 
 
**Service Name:** Uttar Pradesh Scholarship & Fee Reimbursement System 
 
**Government Level:** State Government of Uttar Pradesh 
 
**Department:** 
- Backward Class Welfare Department (for OBC students) 
- Social Welfare Department (for SC/ST/Minority/General category students) 
- Department of Education (institutional coordination) 
 
**Academic Year:** 2024-25 (Update annually) 
 
**Objective:** 
To provide financial assistance to economically weaker and socially disadvantaged students 
in Uttar Pradesh to continue their education without financial barriers through scholarships 
(maintenance allowance) and fee reimbursement (tuition and eligible non-tuition fees). 
 
**System Overview:** 
The UP Scholarship system is an online platform that facilitates: 
- Fresh scholarship applications for first-time applicants 
- Renewal applications for continuing students who received scholarship in the previous year 
- Fee reimbursement claims submitted by institutions on behalf of students 
- Multi-level verification (institution → district → state department) 
- Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of scholarship amounts to student bank accounts 
 
**Responsible Departments:** 
 
| Student Category | Responsible Department | Portal Section | 
|-----------------|----------------------|----------------| 
| SC (Scheduled Caste) | Social Welfare Department | SC Scholarship | 
| ST (Scheduled Tribe) | Social Welfare Department | ST Scholarship | 
| OBC (Other Backward Class) | Backward Class Welfare Department | OBC Scholarship | 
| General (Economically Weaker) | Social Welfare Department | General Category | 
| Minority | Social Welfare Department (UP component) / Ministry of Minority Affairs (Central) 
| Minority Scholarship | 
 
**Academic Year Cycle:** 
- Registration and application: Typically July-October 
- Institution verification: August-November 
- District/Department verification: September-December 
- Sanction and payment: November-March 
- Correction window: Usually provided once during November-December

**Fresh vs Renewal Application:** 
 
| Type | When to Apply | Registration | Previous Records | 
|------|--------------|--------------|------------------| 
| **Fresh** | First-time scholarship applicant, or gap of more than one year, or changed 
category/major course type | New registration required | No previous scholarship data | 
| **Renewal** | Continuing student who received scholarship last academic year in the same 
or next level of education | Use previous registration number | Previous year data auto-filled | 
 
**Student Role:** 
- Register on scholarship portal 
- Fill accurate personal, academic, category, income, and bank details 
- Upload required documents 
- Submit application to institution 
- Track status and respond to rejections/corrections 
 
**Institution Role:** 
- Verify student enrollment, attendance, course, fee details 
- Check uploaded documents against physical records 
- Forward or reject application with remarks 
- Submit institutional fee reimbursement data where applicable 
- Act as first point of contact for student queries 
 
**District/Department Role:** 
- Secondary verification of student eligibility 
- Category certificate verification via issuing authority 
- Income certificate verification 
- Aadhaar authentication and DBT validation 
- Final sanction and payment processing 
 
**Scholarship vs Fee Reimbursement:** 
 
| Component | What It Is | Who Receives | How Paid | 
|-----------|-----------|--------------|----------| 
| **Scholarship / Maintenance Allowance** | Fixed amount for books, stationery, living 
expenses | Student (direct to bank account) | DBT to student account | 
| **Fee Reimbursement** | Tuition fee, exam fee, and eligible non-tuition fees | Student or 
Institution (varies by scheme/year) | DBT to student account or institution account | 
 
**Important:** Some schemes provide only scholarship, some only fee reimbursement, and 
some provide both. The specific benefit depends on the scheme, category, and course. 
 
**Official Portal:** [scholarship.up.gov.in](https://scholarship.up.gov.in) (Verify current URL 
annually) 
 
**Helpline/Support:** 
- Institutional Nodal Officer (first contact)

- District Welfare Office 
- Department helpline (varies by category/department) 
 
**Special Notes:** 
- All applications must be submitted online; offline applications are not accepted 
- Aadhaar is mandatory for scholarship application and payment 
- Only one scholarship per student per academic year through UP system 
- Students can apply for Central scholarships separately via National Scholarship Portal

## 2. Pre-Matric Scholarship — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
 
**Service Name:** Pre-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST/OBC/Minority Students — Uttar 
Pradesh 
 
**Government Level:** State Government of Uttar Pradesh (with Central component for 
SC/ST/Minority where applicable) 
 
**Department:** 
- Social Welfare Department (SC/ST/Minority/General) 
- Backward Class Welfare Department (OBC) 
 
**Academic Year:** 2024-25 
 
**Objective:**

To provide financial assistance to students from SC, ST, OBC, Minority and economically 
weaker sections studying in classes 9 and 10 to reduce dropout rates and encourage school 
continuation. 
 
**Eligible Classes:** 
- Class 9 (IX) 
- Class 10 (X) 
 
**Note:** Classes 1-8 may be covered under separate elementary education schemes; verify 
current applicability annually. 
 
**Category Rules:** 
 
| Category | Eligibility Certificate | Issuing Authority | 
|----------|------------------------|-------------------| 
| SC | Scheduled Caste Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | 
| ST | Scheduled Tribe Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | 
| OBC | Other Backward Class (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | 
| Minority | Religion-based (Muslim/Christian/Sikh/Buddhist/Jain/Parsi) | Self-declaration + 
Community certificate where required | 
| General | Economically Weaker Section (where applicable) | Income certificate | 
 
**Income Conditions (2024-25):** 
 
| Category | Annual Family Income Limit | 
|----------|---------------------------| 
| SC | ₹2,50,000 (verify annually) | 
| ST | ₹2,50,000 | 
| OBC | ₹2,00,000 | 
| Minority | ₹2,00,000 | 
| General | ₹1,00,000 (if scheme applicable) | 
 
**Income Calculation:** 
- Father's income + Mother's income + Guardian's income (if parents not alive) 
- From all sources: salary, agriculture, business, pension, rent, etc. 
- Financial year: Previous financial year (e.g., for 2024-25 scholarship, FY 2023-24 income) 
 
**Residency Requirements:** 
- Student must be a domicile/resident of Uttar Pradesh 
- Domicile certificate or residence proof required 
- Student must be studying in a recognized school within Uttar Pradesh 
- UP students studying outside UP: Generally not eligible for state Pre-Matric scholarship 
(verify for exceptions) 
 
**Recognized Institutions:** 
- Government schools 
- Government-aided schools

- Recognized private schools (affiliated to UP Board, CBSE, ICSE, or other recognized 
boards) 
- Schools must be registered on the scholarship portal 
 
**Benefits (2024-25 — example amounts, verify annually):** 
 
| Component | Amount (per annum) | 
|-----------|--------------------| 
| Scholarship/Maintenance | ₹750 - ₹1,000 (varies by category/scheme) | 
| Admission Fee Reimbursement | Actual, up to prescribed limit | 
| Tuition Fee | For private schools where applicable, subject to ceiling | 
 
**Note:** Benefit structure varies by category (SC/ST/OBC/Minority) and may include both 
maintenance and fee components or only one. 
 
**Fresh Application Process:** 
1. **Registration:** Visit scholarship.up.gov.in → Pre-Matric Scholarship → New Registration 
2. **Student Details:** Name, Father's name, Mother's name, Date of birth, Gender, Aadhaar 
number, Mobile number 
3. **Academic Details:** School name, District, Class (9 or 10), Roll number, Previous class 
marksheet 
4. **Category & Income:** Select category, Upload caste/income certificate 
5. **Address:** Permanent address, Correspondence address, Domicile details 
6. **Bank Details:** Account number, IFSC code, Bank name, Branch (account must be in 
student's name, Aadhaar-linked) 
7. **Upload Documents:** Photo, Aadhaar, Previous marksheet, School ID, Caste certificate, 
Income certificate, Domicile certificate, Fee receipt, Bank passbook 
8. **Preview & Submit:** Review all details, Lock/Submit application 
9. **Print Application:** Take printout, submit to school with documents 
 
**School/Institution Submission:** 
- Student submits hard copy and documents to school nodal officer 
- School verifies enrollment, attendance, documents 
- School forwards application online (Approve/Reject) 
 
**Renewal Process:** 
- Student who received Pre-Matric scholarship in Class 9 and is now in Class 10 
- Use same registration number 
- Update class, roll number, current year marksheet, current year fee receipt 
- Re-upload income certificate if previous year's certificate expired 
- Category certificate usually does not need renewal if still valid 
- School verification required again 
 
**Documents Required:** 
 
| Document | Specification | Validity | 
|----------|---------------|----------| 
| Photograph | Passport size, recent, colored, white background | Current year |

| Aadhaar Card | Clear scan, number must match form | Permanent (update if details 
change) | 
| Previous Class Marksheet | Class 8 marksheet for Class 9 applicants; Class 9 for Class 10 
| Previous academic year | 
| School ID / Bonafide Certificate | School letterhead, Principal signature, school stamp | 
Current academic year | 
| Caste Certificate (SC/ST/OBC) | Issued by Tehsildar/SDM, student's name | Usually 
permanent; check issuing authority rules | 
| Income Certificate | Annual family income, issued by Tehsildar/SDM | Valid for current 
financial year (1 year) | 
| Domicile Certificate | UP residence proof | Permanent or as per issuing authority | 
| Bank Passbook / Statement | First page with account number, IFSC, student name | Recent 
(within 3-6 months) | 
| Fee Receipt | School fee receipt for current year | Current academic year | 
 
**Verification Process:** 
1. **Student Submission:** Application submitted to school 
2. **School Verification:** School checks records, forwards to district (7-15 days) 
3. **District Welfare Office:** Verifies certificates, forwards to department (15-30 days) 
4. **Department Scrutiny:** Final check, sanction list prepared (30-45 days) 
5. **Payment Processing:** DBT to student bank account (variable, typically 60-90 days after 
sanction) 
 
**Rejection Reasons:** 
- Aadhaar mismatch (name/DOB/gender) 
- Invalid or expired income certificate 
- Invalid or mismatched caste certificate 
- Income exceeds limit 
- Not a domicile of UP 
- School not recognized 
- Duplicate application 
- Incomplete documents 
- Failed school verification (attendance, enrollment issues) 
- Bank account details incorrect or not Aadhaar-linked 
 
**Payment:** 
- Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to student's Aadhaar-linked bank account 
- Payment in one or two installments (varies by year) 
- SMS notification sent to registered mobile number when payment initiated 
- Check scholarship portal for payment status 
 
**Application Dates & Deadlines (2024-25 example):** 
- Registration opens: July 15, 2024 
- Last date for student application: October 15, 2024 
- Last date for school verification: November 15, 2024 
- Correction window: November 20-30, 2024 
- Sanction list: December 2024 
- Payment: January-March 2025

**Special Cases:** 
- **Students with Disability:** Additional certificate (disability/UDID), may have relaxed 
criteria or additional benefits 
- **Orphan Students:** Guardian income considered, orphan certificate required 
- **Single Parent:** Income of custodial parent considered 
 
**FAQs:** 
 
**Q: I am in Class 8. Can I apply for Pre-Matric scholarship?** 
A: As of 2024-25, Pre-Matric scholarship in UP is for Classes 9-10. Verify if Classes 1-8 are 
covered under a different scheme. 
 
**Q: My family income is ₹2,10,000 and I am SC category. Am I eligible?** 
A: If the SC income limit is ₹2,50,000 for 2024-25, you are eligible. Verify the current year 
income limit. 
 
**Q: I received scholarship last year in Class 9. Do I apply fresh or renewal?** 
A: Apply as Renewal using your previous registration number. 
 
**Q: My school is private and affiliated to CBSE. Can I apply?** 
A: Yes, if your school is recognized and registered on the scholarship portal, and you meet 
category and income criteria. 
 
**Q: Can I apply if I live in UP but study in a school in another state?** 
A: Generally, UP Pre-Matric scholarship requires studying in a UP-based recognized school. 
Check official guidelines for exceptions. 
 
**Grievance:** 
- School Nodal Officer (first contact) 
- District Backward/Social Welfare Officer 
- Helpline: (Department-specific helpline number)

## 3. Post-Matric Scholarship — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
 
**Service Name:** Post-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST/OBC/Minority Students — Uttar 
Pradesh 
 
**Government Level:** State Government of Uttar Pradesh (with Central component for 
SC/ST/Minority) 
 
**Department:** 
- Social Welfare Department (SC/ST/Minority/General) 
- Backward Class Welfare Department (OBC) 
 
**Academic Year:** 2024-25 
 
**Objective:** 
To enable SC, ST, OBC, Minority and economically weaker students to pursue higher 
education (post-Class 10) by providing financial assistance covering maintenance allowance 
and fee reimbursement, thereby improving enrollment and retention in colleges and 
professional courses. 
 
**Eligible After Pre-Matric Stage:** 
Post-Matric scholarship applies to students who have passed Class 10 and are pursuing: 
- Class 11 and 12 (Intermediate) 
- Undergraduate courses (BA, BSc, BCom, B.Tech, BBA, BCA, etc.) 
- Postgraduate courses (MA, MSc, MCom, M.Tech, MBA, MCA, etc.) 
- Diploma and Polytechnic 
- Professional courses (Engineering, Medical, Management, Pharmacy, Law, etc.) 
- Certificate and vocational courses (where officially eligible) 
 
**Course/Institution Eligibility:** 
- Course must be recognized by UGC, AICTE, PCI, BCI, MCI/NMC, State Government or 
other competent authority 
- Institution must be recognized and registered on the UP scholarship portal 
- Government colleges, government-aided colleges and recognized private colleges 
- Distance/Open University courses: Verify scheme-specific eligibility (usually eligible if 
UGC-recognized)

**Category Requirements:** 
 
| Category | Certificate | Issuing Authority | Validity | 
|----------|-------------|-------------------|----------| 
| SC | Scheduled Caste Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | Permanent (unless name/details 
change) | 
| ST | Scheduled Tribe Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | Permanent | 
| OBC | Other Backward Class (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate | Tehsildar / SDM | Annual or 
1-3 years (verify issuing rules) | 
| Minority | Religion-based self-declaration (Muslim/Christian/Sikh/Buddhist/Jain/Parsi) + 
Community certificate where required | Varies | As per scheme | 
| General | EWS Certificate (if scheme applicable) | Tehsildar / SDM | 1 year | 
 
**Income Rules (2024-25 — verify annually):** 
 
| Category | Annual Family Income Limit | 
|----------|---------------------------| 
| SC | ₹2,50,000 | 
| ST | ₹2,50,000 | 
| OBC | ₹2,00,000 | 
| Minority | ₹2,00,000 | 
| General (EWS) | ₹1,00,000 (if applicable) | 
 
**Income Calculation:** 
- Parents' combined income (father + mother) or guardian's income 
- All sources: salary, agriculture, business, rent, pension, interest, etc. 
- Financial year: Previous FY (for 2024-25 scholarship, income of FY 2023-24) 
- Income certificate issued by Tehsildar or SDM 
 
**Application Process:** 
 
### Fresh Application (First-time Post-Matric applicant or gap year): 
1. **Registration:** 
 - Visit scholarship.up.gov.in 
 - Select category (SC/ST/OBC/Minority/General) 
 - Click "New Registration" under Post-Matric 
 - Enter name, date of birth, gender, mobile number, email 
 - Set password 
 - Verify mobile via OTP 
 - Registration number generated and sent via SMS 
 
2. **Student Details:** 
 - Full name (as per Class 10 marksheet) 
 - Father's name, Mother's name 
 - Date of birth, Gender 
 - Aadhaar number (mandatory) 
 - Category, Religion, Disability status

- Mobile, Email 
 - Correspondence and permanent address 
 - District, Block, Village/Town 
 
3. **Academic Details:** 
 - Previous qualification: Class 10 / Class 12 / Graduation, etc. 
 - Board/University 
 - Roll number, Passing year, Marks obtained, Percentage 
 - Current course: Intermediate / UG / PG / Diploma / Professional 
 - Course name (e.g., B.Tech Computer Science) 
 - Year/Semester 
 - College/Institution name (select from portal list) 
 - Enrollment/Registration number 
 - Admission date 
 
4. **Category & Income:** 
 - Upload Caste/Category certificate (PDF/JPG, size limit typically 200-500 KB) 
 - Certificate number, issuing authority, issue date 
 - Upload Income certificate 
 - Income amount, issuing authority, issue date, validity 
 
5. **Domicile:** 
 - Upload Domicile/Residence certificate 
 - Certificate number, issue date 
 
6. **Bank Details:** 
 - Bank account number (must be in student's name) 
 - Re-enter account number 
 - IFSC code 
 - Bank name, Branch name 
 - Upload bank passbook first page or bank statement 
 - Account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT 
 
7. **Document Upload:** 
 - Recent passport-size color photograph 
 - Aadhaar card 
 - Class 10 marksheet (for UG applicants) or highest qualification marksheet 
 - Current year admission receipt/college ID 
 - Fee receipt (tuition + other fees) 
 - Caste certificate 
 - Income certificate 
 - Domicile certificate 
 - Bank passbook/statement 
 - Disability certificate (if applicable) 
 
8. **Fee Details:** 
 - Tuition fee paid 
 - Other compulsory fees (exam, library, sports, etc.; not hostel/transport unless specified)

- Total fee paid 
 - Fee receipt number, date 
 
9. **Preview & Final Submission:** 
 - Review all entered information 
 - Check all documents uploaded correctly 
 - Click "Final Submit" or "Lock" 
 - Once locked, most fields cannot be edited until correction window 
 - Print application form 
 
10. **Submit to Institution:** 
 - Take printout of application 
 - Submit hard copy with all original/attested documents to college nodal officer within 
deadline 
 
### Renewal Application (Continuing students who received Post-Matric scholarship last 
year): 
- Use previous year registration number and password 
- Login to portal 
- Select "Renewal" application 
- Most personal and category details auto-filled 
- Update: 
 - Current year/semester 
 - Current enrollment/roll number 
 - Current year marks (previous year result) 
 - Current year fee receipt 
 - Renewed income certificate if previous expired 
 - Bank details if account changed 
- Upload current year documents 
- Institution verification and approval/forwarding 
- No need to re-upload permanent documents like caste certificate (unless there's a change 
or system requests)

semester/year) | PDF | 300 KB |

**Institution Verification:** 
- College nodal officer logs into scholarship portal 
- Views list of applications from students enrolled at the college 
- Verifies: 
 - Student enrollment and attendance 
 - Course and year correctness 
 - Marks/results match college records 
 - Fee details match college fee structure and receipts 
 - Uploaded documents match physical documents submitted by student 
- Action: 
 - **Forward:** If all details correct → application forwarded to District/Department 
 - **Reject:** If discrepancies found → application rejected with remarks (student can 
correct and reapply if correction window open) 
- Timeline: Institutions typically given 15-30 days after student application deadline 
 
**District/Department Verification:** 
- District Social Welfare / Backward Welfare Officer 
- Checks: 
 - Caste certificate authenticity (cross-check with issuing Tehsil) 
 - Income certificate authenticity and validity 
 - Domicile verification 
 - Aadhaar authentication 
 - Duplicate application check (same Aadhaar, same course, same year) 
 - Bank account and DBT validation 
- Action: 
 - Approve and forward to state department for sanction 
 - Reject with reason 
- Timeline: 15-30 days after institution verification 
 
**State Department Final Scrutiny:** 
- Prepares sanction list 
- Allocates budget 
- Sends payment files to PFMS (Public Financial Management System) or state treasury 
- Timeline: 30-60 days after district verification 
 
**Payment:** 
- Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account 
- Maintenance allowance + Fee reimbursement (or only one component, depending on 
scheme and course) 
- Payment in 1-3 installments depending on scheme 
- SMS and email notification when payment credited 
- Track status: Scholarship portal → Login → Application Status → Payment Status 
 
**Rejection Reasons:** 
- **Aadhaar issues:** Name/DOB/Gender mismatch between Aadhaar, application, and 
Class 10 certificate

- **Invalid caste certificate:** Fake, expired, or issued by unauthorized authority 
- **Invalid income certificate:** Expired, income exceeds limit, issued by wrong authority 
- **Duplicate application:** Student already received scholarship for same course/year, or 
multiple applications with same Aadhaar 
- **Course not eligible:** Course not recognized or not covered under scheme 
- **Institution not recognized:** College not approved or not registered on portal 
- **Fee mismatch:** Fee declared by student does not match institution records 
- **Attendance issue:** Student attendance below minimum (if applicable) 
- **Bank account issue:** Account not in student's name, not Aadhaar-linked, IFSC wrong, 
account closed 
- **Document mismatch:** Name spelling differences across documents 
- **Failed verification:** Institution or district rejected application 
- **Income limit exceeded:** Family income above threshold 
- **Not a domicile of UP:** No valid UP residence proof 
 
**Correction Window:** 
- Usually provided once per academic year (e.g., November-December) 
- Student can edit rejected applications or correct errors 
- Specific fields may be locked (e.g., Aadhaar number, DOB may require offline correction 
request) 
- After correction, application re-enters verification cycle 
 
**Special Cases:** 
- **Gap year students:** May apply as fresh if gap is more than one academic year; provide 
explanation/affidavit if required 
- **Course change:** If student changed course (e.g., BA to B.Com), apply as fresh with new 
course details 
- **College change (migration):** Update institution details; may need fresh application 
depending on system rules 
- **Failed/back paper students:** Renewal eligibility depends on promotion; if detained/failed, 
may not be eligible until promoted (verify scheme-specific rules) 
- **Students with disability:** May have relaxed income/marks criteria; additional benefits; 
upload disability certificate and UDID

professional courses — verify annually)

institution type. Always check official notification for the current academic year.

**FAQs:** 
 
**Q: I received scholarship in Class 12 last year and now I am in first year B.A. Do I apply 
fresh or renewal?** 
A: You apply as **Fresh** because you moved from Intermediate to Undergraduate level. 
Renewal is only within the same course level (e.g., Class 11 to 12, B.A. 1st year to 2nd 
year). 
 
**Q: My family income is ₹2,05,000 and I am OBC. Am I eligible?** 
A: If the OBC income limit is ₹2,00,000, you are **not eligible** as you exceed the limit. 
Verify the exact limit for 2024-25. 
 
**Q: I am a B.Tech student in a private college. Can I get fee reimbursement?** 
A: Yes, if the college is recognized and you meet all eligibility criteria. Fee reimbursement will 
be subject to the maximum limit prescribed for private engineering colleges. 
 
**Q: I changed my college after 1st year. Can I apply for renewal?** 
A: You may need to apply as fresh or update institution details in the renewal form. Check 
portal instructions or contact the new college nodal officer. 
 
**Q: My application was rejected due to Aadhaar name mismatch. What do I do?** 
A: Correct your name in Aadhaar to match your Class 10 certificate (or vice versa) through 
UIDAI. Then apply for correction in the scholarship portal during the correction window. 
 
**Q: Can I get both Central and UP Post-Matric scholarship?** 
A: No, you can receive only one Post-Matric scholarship per academic year. If you apply to 
both Central (NSP) and State (UP), and both approve, you will have to choose one and the 
other will be cancelled.

## 5. Fee Reimbursement — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
 
**Service Name:** Fee Reimbursement for Students — Uttar Pradesh 
 
**Government Level:** State Government of Uttar Pradesh 
 
**Department:** Social Welfare Department, Backward Class Welfare Department, 
Department of Higher Education (coordination) 
 
**Academic Year:** 2024-25 
 
**Objective:** 
To reimburse tuition fees and other eligible compulsory non-refundable fees paid by 
economically weaker and socially disadvantaged students (SC, ST, OBC, Minority, 
General-EWS) studying in recognized institutions in Uttar Pradesh, thereby reducing the 
financial burden of higher education. 
 
--- 
 
### What is Fee Reimbursement? 
 
Fee reimbursement is a component of the scholarship scheme where the **actual fee paid 
by the student** (tuition + eligible non-tuition fees) is refunded either to: 
- The **student's bank account** (Direct Benefit Transfer), or 
- The **institution's bank account** (where the institution waives/adjusts the fee for the 
student) 
 
**Difference from Maintenance Allowance (Scholarship):** 
- **Maintenance Allowance:** Fixed monthly/annual amount for living expenses, books, 
stationery 
- **Fee Reimbursement:** Actual fee reimbursement based on receipts and institution data 
 
Some schemes provide **only fee reimbursement**, some **only maintenance allowance**, 
and some **both**. 
 
--- 
 
### Who Qualifies for Fee Reimbursement? 
 
**Eligible Students:** 
- SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Minority, General (EWS) students 
- Enrolled in recognized Post-Matric courses (Class 11-12, UG, PG, Diploma, Professional) 
- Family income within prescribed limits 
- Domicile of Uttar Pradesh

- Studying in a UP-recognized institution (government, aided, or approved private) 
 
**Ineligible Students:** 
- Students whose family income exceeds the limit 
- Students in unrecognized institutions or courses 
- Students who have already received fee reimbursement from another government scheme 
for the same academic year 
- Students who have not paid the fee (fee reimbursement requires proof of payment) 
 
--- 
 
### Eligible Institutions & Courses: 
 
**Institutions:** 
- Government colleges and schools 
- Government-aided colleges 
- Recognized private colleges and schools (affiliated to recognized university/board, 
approved by UGC/AICTE/State Government) 
- Institutions must be registered on scholarship.up.gov.in 
 
**Courses:** 
- Post-Matric Intermediate (Class 11-12) 
- Undergraduate (BA, BSc, BCom, B.Tech, BBA, BCA, etc.) 
- Postgraduate (MA, MSc, MCom, M.Tech, MBA, MCA, etc.) 
- Diploma and Polytechnic 
- Professional courses (Engineering, Medical, Management, Law, Pharmacy, Architecture, 
etc.) 
- Certificate and vocational courses (where scheme-applicable) 
 
**Excluded:** 
- Courses not recognized by competent authority 
- Institutions not registered on scholarship portal 
- Pre-Matric classes (unless specifically covered under a separate pre-matric fee 
reimbursement scheme) 
 
--- 
 
### Eligible Fees for Reimbursement: 
 
**Included (compulsory, non-refundable fees):** 
- Tuition fee 
- Examination fee 
- Admission fee (one-time, if applicable) 
- Library fee (annual, compulsory) 
- Sports fee (compulsory) 
- Student welfare fee 
- Development fee (compulsory, non-refundable) 
- Laboratory fee (compulsory for science/engineering courses)

- Medical examination fee (if compulsory) 
- Internet/computer fee (if compulsory) 
- Identity card fee (if compulsory, non-refundable) 
 
**Excluded (not reimbursed):** 
- Hostel fee and mess charges 
- Transport fee 
- Caution deposit, security deposit (refundable amounts) 
- Fine, penalty, late fee 
- Extra-curricular or optional activity fees 
- Private coaching or supplementary tuition 
- Stationery, uniform, books (covered under maintenance allowance, not fee reimbursement) 
- Fee for additional certifications, extra exams not part of the course curriculum 
 
**Important:** The institution must provide a **detailed fee breakup** showing compulsory vs 
optional fees. Only compulsory, non-refundable fees are reimbursed. 
 
--- 
 
### Fee Details Submitted by Institutions: 
 
**Institution's Role in Fee Reimbursement:** 
1. **Fee Structure Registration:** 
 - At the beginning of the academic year, institutions submit their approved fee structure to 
the scholarship portal 
 - Fee breakup by course, year, and category (if different fee for different student 
categories) 
 
2. **Student Fee Verification:** 
 - When a student applies for scholarship, the institution verifies: 
 - Fee receipt submitted by student 
 - Actual fee paid by student matches the declared fee on portal 
 - Fee breakup is correct (tuition, exam, other eligible fees) 
 - Institution enters actual fee paid by student in the verification module 
 
3. **Fee Reimbursement Claim:** 
 - Institution submits claim for fee reimbursement on behalf of students 
 - Provides institution bank account details if fee reimbursement is to be credited to 
institution (scheme-dependent) 
 - Or certifies that student has paid the fee and should receive reimbursement in student's 
account 
 
**Institutional Bank Account (where applicable):** 
- Some schemes reimburse fee directly to the institution 
- Institution must adjust the student's fee account (waive or refund) 
- Institution must issue updated fee receipt to student showing adjustment 
 
**Student Bank Account (where applicable):**

- Some schemes reimburse fee directly to student's Aadhaar-linked bank account 
- Student is then responsible to pay the institution if fee was waived or paid late 
 
--- 
 
### Student Claims: 
 
**How Students Claim Fee Reimbursement:** 
1. **Pay the Fee:** 
 - Student must pay the full fee to the institution at the time of admission or as per 
institution's fee schedule 
 - Obtain official fee receipt 
 
2. **Upload Fee Receipt:** 
 - Scan and upload fee receipt during scholarship application 
 - Enter total fee paid, tuition fee, exam fee, other fees separately (as per portal fields) 
 
3. **Submit Application:** 
 - Complete scholarship application (personal, academic, category, income, bank, 
documents) 
 - Submit to institution 
 
4. **Institution Verification:** 
 - Institution verifies fee payment and forwards application 
 
5. **Government Verification & Sanction:** 
 - District and department verify eligibility 
 - Approve fee reimbursement amount (actual fee or prescribed ceiling, whichever is lower) 
 
6. **Payment:** 
 - Fee reimbursement credited to student's or institution's bank account 
 - Student receives SMS/email notification 
 
--- 
 
### Verification Process: 
 
**Step 1: Student Submission** 
- Student uploads fee receipt, enters fee details 
- Final submission to institution 
 
**Step 2: Institution Verification** 
- Institution checks: 
 - Fee receipt authenticity 
 - Fee amount matches institution's record 
 - Fee breakup correct 
 - Student has actually paid the fee (not outstanding) 
- Institution enters verified fee in portal

- Forwards application 
 
**Step 3: District/Department Verification** 
- Cross-checks fee with institution's registered fee structure 
- Ensures fee does not exceed prescribed reimbursement limit 
- Verifies no duplicate fee claim 
- Approves or rejects 
 
**Step 4: Sanction** 
- Department sanctions fee reimbursement 
- Amount sanctioned = Minimum of (Actual fee paid, Prescribed ceiling for that 
category/course/institution type) 
 
--- 
 
### Sanctioned Amount: 
 
**How Sanctioned Amount is Calculated:** 
 
**Formula:** 
``` 
Sanctioned Fee Reimbursement = MIN(Actual Fee Paid, Maximum Reimbursement Limit) 
``` 
 
**Example 1:** 
- Course: B.Tech (Private College) 
- Actual fee paid: ₹60,000 
- Maximum limit for private engineering (SC category, 2024-25): ₹80,000 
- **Sanctioned amount: ₹60,000** (full fee reimbursed) 
 
**Example 2:** 
- Course: B.Tech (Private College)

Treasury

 - **Institution's registered bank account** (scheme-dependent)

processing) 
- SMS and email alert sent when payment credited 
 
**Payment Installments:** 
- Fee reimbursement may be paid in 1-2 installments depending on scheme

- If semester fee, may be paid per semester after each semester's verification 
 
**Checking Payment Status:**

### Disputes: 
 
**Common Fee Reimbursement Disputes:** 
 
**1. Sanctioned Amount Less Than Fee Paid:** 
- **Reason:** Actual fee exceeds prescribed ceiling

- **Resolution:** Student must pay the difference from own sources; no further 
reimbursement 
- **Prevention:** Before admission, check reimbursement limits and choose institution 
accordingly if fee is a constraint 
 
**2. Institution Demanding Fee Despite Reimbursement Approved:** 
- **Reason:** 
 - Reimbursement credited to student account, but student has not paid institution 
 - Or institution has not received reimbursement yet (if paid to institution account) 
- **Resolution:** 
 - If student received payment: Pay institution immediately 
 - If payment delayed: Show scholarship sanction letter to institution; institution should wait 
or provide provisional admission 
 
**3. Fee Reimbursement Not Received (Student or Institution):** 
- **Reason:** 
 - Bank account issue (wrong account number, closed account, IFSC error) 
 - DBT validation failure 
 - PFMS payment pending or failed 
- **Resolution:** 
 - Check payment status on portal 
 - Check PFMS status (if PFMS tracking available) 
 - Contact District Welfare Office with application number and sanction letter 
 - Update bank details if incorrect (during correction window or via written request) 
 
**4. Excess Fee Claimed/Sanctioned:** 
- **Reason:** Student or institution uploaded inflated fee receipt; system did not catch 
- **Resolution:** 
 - Department may recover excess amount from student or institution 
 - Student must refund excess payment if demanded 
 - Future applications may be blocked until recovery 
 
**5. Fee Mismatch Between Student Claim and Institution Verification:** 
- **Reason:** 
 - Student uploaded wrong fee receipt (e.g., previous year, someone else's receipt) 
 - Institution fee structure changed mid-year 
 - Clerical error 
- **Resolution:** 
 - Institution rejects application with remark 
 - Student corrects fee receipt and re-uploads during correction window 
 - Institution re-verifies 
 
**6. Fee Reimbursement for Course Not Covered:** 
- **Reason:** Student applied for fee reimbursement for a course that is not eligible (e.g., 
unrecognized certification course, hobby class) 
- **Resolution:** Application rejected at verification stage; no reimbursement 
 
**7. Duplicate Fee Claim:**

- **Reason:** Student received fee reimbursement from another scholarship (e.g., Central 
NSP and UP scholarship both approved) 
- **Resolution:** 
 - One scholarship must be cancelled 
 - Excess payment recovered 
 - Student may face penalty or disqualification

### Special Cases: 
 
**Case 1: Fee Paid in Installments** 
- Some institutions allow fee payment in 2-3 installments

- Student should upload **cumulative fee receipt** or all installment receipts 
- Reimbursement processed after full fee payment verified, or per installment if scheme 
permits 
 
**Case 2: Fee Waiver by Institution** 
- Some institutions waive fee for meritorious or economically weaker students 
- If fee is fully waived: No fee reimbursement claim (nothing to reimburse) 
- If fee partially waived: Student claims reimbursement only for amount actually paid 
 
**Case 3: Scholarship Received Mid-Year (Student Already Paid Fee)** 
- Student paid full fee at admission (e.g., July 2024) 
- Scholarship sanctioned and payment received in February 2025 
- **Resolution:** Student receives reimbursement in bank account; student's fee account 
with institution is settled 
 
**Case 4: Institution Closed/Merged Before Payment** 
- Rare case: Institution closes or merges before fee reimbursement is credited to institution 
account 
- **Resolution:** Department may credit directly to student account; student must verify fee 
payment status with institution or successor institution 
 
**Case 5: Course Fee Reduced by Court/Government Order** 
- Fee charged initially was ₹1,00,000 
- Court or fee regulation authority orders fee reduction to ₹70,000 
- Student had paid ₹1,00,000 
- **Resolution:** Institution must refund ₹30,000 to student; scholarship reimbursement 
based on approved fee of ₹70,000

### FAQs: 
 
**Q: I paid ₹50,000 fee but received only ₹30,000 reimbursement. Why?** 
A: The prescribed reimbursement ceiling for your course/category/institution type is ₹30,000. 
You must pay the remaining ₹20,000 from your own resources. 
 
**Q: My institution has not received fee reimbursement yet, and they are asking me to pay. 
What do I do?** 
A: Show the institution your scholarship sanction letter and payment status from the portal. 
Request them to wait for payment or provide provisional admission. If they insist, contact the 
District Welfare Office. 
 
**Q: Can I claim fee reimbursement if I have taken an education loan?** 
A: Yes, as long as you meet eligibility criteria. The fee reimbursement will be credited to your 
account. You can use it to repay the loan or for other educational expenses. 
 
**Q: I received fee reimbursement in my account, but I had not paid the college fee yet. 
What should I do?**

A: You must pay the college immediately. The reimbursement is meant to cover the fee you 
paid; if you haven't paid, you are obligated to pay the institution now. 
 
**Q: My college charged hostel fee and mess fee. Can I claim reimbursement for that?** 
A: No. Hostel and mess fees are not covered under fee reimbursement. Only tuition and 
eligible compulsory non-refundable fees are reimbursed. 
 
**Q: I changed college mid-year. Can I claim fee reimbursement for both colleges?** 
A: You can claim fee reimbursement only for the college where you are currently enrolled 
and completing the academic year. If you paid fee at the previous college and left, you may 
need to seek a refund from that institution; scholarship will not reimburse fee for a 
course/institution you did not complete. 
 
**Q: Fee reimbursement was sanctioned but not credited. Whom do I contact?** 
A: Check payment status on portal. If status shows "Payment Sent" but not credited, check 
your bank account passbook/statement, verify account number and IFSC on application. 
Contact District Welfare Office with sanction letter and bank details.

## 6. Student Category Rules — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India

**Service Name:** Category Certificate Rules for UP Scholarship & Education Services 
 
**Government Level:** State Government of Uttar Pradesh 
 
**Department:** Revenue Department (certificate issuance), Social Welfare / Backward 
Class Welfare (scholarship verification) 
 
**Academic Year:** 2024-25 (Rules stable, but verify changes annually) 
 
**Objective:** 
To define and regulate the issuance, validity, and verification of caste/category certificates 
required for availing scholarships and education benefits in Uttar Pradesh, ensuring that only 
eligible students from SC, ST, OBC, Minority, and General (EWS) categories receive 
benefits. 
 
--- 
 
### Student Categories Applicable in UP Scholarship Schemes: 
 
| Category Code | Full Name | Applicable Scholarships | Certificate Required | 
|---------------|-----------|------------------------|---------------------| 
| **SC** | Scheduled Caste | Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, PMOTI | SC Caste Certificate | 
| **ST** | Scheduled Tribe | Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, PMOTI | ST Caste Certificate | 
| **OBC** | Other Backward Class (Non-Creamy Layer) | Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, PMOTI | 
OBC (NCL) Certificate | 
| **Minority** | Religious Minority (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi) | Pre-Matric, 
Post-Matric (Central & State components) | Self-declaration + Community Certificate (where 
required) | 
| **General / EWS** | Economically Weaker Section (General Category) | Specific state 
schemes | EWS Certificate + Income Certificate | 
| **PWD / Divyang** | Persons with Disabilities | All schemes + additional disability-specific 
schemes | Disability Certificate / UDID | 
 
--- 
 
## SC (Scheduled Caste) Students 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Student belongs to one of the Scheduled Castes as notified in the Constitution (Scheduled 
Castes) Order, 1950, as applicable to Uttar Pradesh 
- Student or student's parents must be domiciled in Uttar Pradesh 
 
**Certificate Requirements:** 
 
| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Scheduled Caste Certificate | 
| **Issuing Authority** | Tehsildar, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), District Magistrate (DM) |

| **Required Documents for Certificate** | Parents' caste certificate (if available), Birth 
certificate, Aadhaar, School record showing caste, Family registry (khasra/khatauni showing 
SC status) | 
| **Processing Time** | 7-15 days (varies by district) | 
| **Validity** | Permanent (unless there is a change in name or caste status, which is not 
normally permissible) | 
| **Certificate Content** | Student's name, Father's name, Mother's name, Date of birth, 
Caste name (e.g., "Chamar", "Pasi", "Valmiki"), Certifying that the person belongs to 
Scheduled Caste, Issuing authority signature and seal, Issue date, Certificate number | 
| **Language** | Hindi or English (English preferred for scholarship upload) | 
| **Format** | Government-prescribed format on official letterhead | 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- Income Limit (2024-25): ₹2,50,000 per annum (verify annually) 
- Benefits: Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Fee Reimbursement, Maintenance Allowance 
- No creamy layer restriction for SC (unlike OBC) 
 
**Certificate Verification:** 
- During scholarship verification, the issuing Tehsil office is contacted to verify authenticity 
- Certificate number cross-checked 
- If fake certificate detected: Application rejected, student may face legal action, blacklisting 
 
**Common Issues & Corrections:** 
 
| Issue | Resolution | 
|-------|-----------| 
| **Caste name mismatch** (e.g., certificate says "Chamar", application says "SC-Chamar") | 
Certificate should clearly mention the caste; student should enter exactly as per certificate | 
| **Father's name mismatch** between caste certificate and school records | Correct school 
records or obtain fresh certificate with correct father's name | 
| **Certificate in Hindi, portal requires English** | Get English translation attested by issuing 
authority or gazetted officer; upload both | 
| **Certificate number missing or illegible** | Contact issuing Tehsil to obtain certificate 
number or fresh certificate | 
| **Expired or invalid format** | Caste certificate does not expire, but if format is very old 
(pre-2000s), may need fresh certificate in current format | 
 
--- 
 
## ST (Scheduled Tribe) Students 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Student belongs to one of the Scheduled Tribes as notified in the Constitution (Scheduled 
Tribes) Order, 1950, applicable to Uttar Pradesh 
- ST population in UP is very small; main ST communities: Tharu, Buksa, Bhotia, Jaunsari, 
Raji (mostly in hilly/forest regions) 
 
**Certificate Requirements:**

| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Scheduled Tribe Certificate | 
| **Issuing Authority** | Tehsildar, SDM, DM (in tribal-notified areas, sometimes special ST 
Certificate Issuing Authority) | 
| **Validity** | Permanent | 
| **Certificate Content** | Student's name, Father's/Mother's name, DOB, Tribe name (e.g., 
"Tharu"), "Scheduled Tribe" mention, Issuing authority, Certificate number, Date | 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- Income Limit (2024-25): ₹2,50,000 per annum 
- Benefits: Same as SC 
- No creamy layer for ST 
 
**Verification & Issues:** 
- Same as SC 
- Rare cases of ST certificate misuse in UP (since ST population is small); verification is 
strict 
 
--- 
 
## OBC (Other Backward Class) Students 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Student belongs to one of the castes/communities listed in the UP OBC list (Central OBC 
list also applicable for Central schemes) 
- **Non-Creamy Layer (NCL):** Student's family must not fall under the "Creamy Layer" 
criteria (high-income or high-status families excluded even if caste is OBC) 
 
**Certificate Requirements:** 
 
| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Other Backward Class (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate / OBC-NCL 
Certificate | 
| **Issuing Authority** | Tehsildar, SDM, DM | 
| **Validity** | **Annual or up to 3 years** (varies by issuing authority rules; commonly valid 
for 1 financial year) | 
| **Renewal** | OBC-NCL certificate must be renewed annually or as per validity period, 
because family income/status may change | 
| **Certificate Content** | Student's name, Father's name, Mother's name, DOB, Caste name 
(e.g., "Yadav", "Kurmi", "Lodhi"), "Other Backward Class", **"Non-Creamy Layer"** mention 
(crucial), Issuing authority, Certificate number, Date, Validity period | 
 
**Creamy Layer Exclusion Criteria (as per UP/Central Government orders):** 
- Parents holding constitutional positions (e.g., judges, IAS/IPS officers of certain ranks)

- Parents with gross annual income above ₹8,00,000 (Central creamy layer limit; UP may 
have different limit—verify) 
- Children of persons holding high posts in government, PSU, or having significant 
agricultural/business income 
 
**If student falls under Creamy Layer:** 
- NOT eligible for OBC quota benefits 
- May apply under General category (if financially eligible for General/EWS schemes) 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- Income Limit (2024-25): ₹2,00,000 per annum (OBC NCL) 
- **Important:** Income limit is separate from creamy layer income limit. Even if family 
income is ₹2,50,000 (below ₹8,00,000 creamy layer), if it exceeds ₹2,00,000, student is not 
eligible for OBC scholarship. 
 
**Verification:** 
- OBC certificate number verified with issuing Tehsil 
- Creamy layer status checked (if certificate does not mention "Non-Creamy Layer", 
application may be rejected) 
- Validity date checked; expired certificates lead to rejection 
 
**Common Issues:** 
 
| Issue | Resolution | 
|-------|-----------| 
| **Certificate does not mention "Non-Creamy Layer"** | Obtain fresh OBC-NCL certificate 
clearly stating NCL status | 
| **Certificate expired** | Renew certificate before scholarship application deadline | 
| **Caste not in UP OBC list** | If caste is in Central OBC list but not UP list: may be eligible 
for Central schemes (NSP) but not UP state schemes; verify latest UP OBC list | 
| **Income exceeds limit but within creamy layer limit** | Student not eligible for OBC 
scholarship; may check General/EWS scheme eligibility | 
 
--- 
 
## Minority Students 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Student belongs to one of the notified minority communities in India: 
 - Muslim 
 - Christian 
 - Sikh 
 - Buddhist 
 - Jain 
 - Parsi (Zoroastrian) 
 
**Certificate Requirements:**

| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Community Certificate (for some schemes) / Self-Declaration of 
Religion (for others) | 
| **Issuing Authority** | Varies: SDM, Tehsildar, or self-declaration accepted depending on 
scheme (Central vs State) | 
| **Validity** | Generally permanent (religion does not change annually) | 
| **Certificate Content** | Student's name, Father's name, Religion/Community, Issuing 
authority (if applicable) | 
 
**Note:** 
- For **UP state minority scholarship**, some schemes accept self-declaration of religion 
(student declares religion during application; no separate certificate needed) 
- For **Central Minority Scholarship (Pre-Matric/Post-Matric/Merit-cum-Means)**, community 
certificate from competent authority may be required; verify scheme guidelines 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- Income Limit (2024-25): ₹2,00,000 per annum (for most minority scholarships) 
- Benefits: Pre-Matric, Post-Matric under Ministry of Minority Affairs (Central) and UP 
Minority Welfare (State component) 
 
**Verification:** 
- Religion declared in application cross-checked with school records, Aadhaar, community 
certificate (if uploaded) 
- Less stringent verification compared to caste certificates (since minority status is based on 
religion, which is usually evident from name/school records) 
 
**Common Issues:** 
- Mismatch between religion declared and school records 
- Community certificate in wrong format 
- Confusion between Central and State minority schemes 
 
--- 
 
## General Category / EWS (Economically Weaker Section) 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Students who do not belong to SC, ST, or OBC categories 
- Family income below prescribed limit (typically ₹1,00,000 - ₹3,00,000 depending on 
scheme) 
- Primarily income-based eligibility, not caste-based 
 
**Certificate Requirements:** 
 
| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Income Certificate + EWS Certificate (for reserved quota) OR only 
Income Certificate (for non-quota scholarship) |

| **Issuing Authority** | Tehsildar, SDM, DM | 
| **Validity** | 1 financial year (Income Certificate must be renewed annually) | 
| **Certificate Content** | Family annual income, all sources, issuing authority, certificate 
number, validity | 
 
**EWS Certificate (for reservation, not scholarship):** 
- Introduced for 10% reservation in educational institutions and government jobs 
- Income limit: Up to ₹8,00,000 per annum + property ownership criteria 
- **Not directly used for scholarship**, but may be relevant if a scholarship scheme is 
introduced for EWS quota students 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- Income Limit (2024-25 example): ₹1,00,000 - ₹2,00,000 per annum (varies by scheme) 
- Benefits: Limited state scholarships for general category students; mostly income-based 
schemes 
 
**Verification:** 
- Income certificate verified with issuing Tehsil 
- Income cross-checked with IT returns (if family files tax), property records, employment 
records 
 
--- 
 
## PWD / Divyang (Students with Disabilities) 
 
**Eligibility:** 
- Students with one or more disabilities as per Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 
- Minimum disability percentage: 40% or more (for most benefits) 
 
**Certificate Requirements:** 
 
| Attribute | Details | 
|-----------|---------| 
| **Certificate Name** | Disability Certificate / UDID (Unique Disability ID) Card | 
| **Issuing Authority** | Medical Board constituted by Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / District 
Hospital | 
| **Validity** | Permanent disabilities: Permanent certificate; Temporary/progressive 
disabilities: Renewable (e.g., every 5 years) | 
| **Certificate Content** | Type of disability (locomotor, visual, hearing, intellectual, multiple), 
Percentage of disability, Certifying medical board signatures, Certificate number, UDID 
number | 
 
**Category-Specific Eligibility for Scholarship:** 
- May have **relaxed income limits** or **additional scholarship amount** in some schemes 
- Eligible for **disability-specific scholarships** (e.g., National Fellowship for Students with 
Disabilities) 
- Eligible for all general category scholarships if they also belong to SC/ST/OBC/Minority

**Verification:** 
- Disability certificate verified with issuing medical authority 
- UDID number cross-checked with national UDID database

## Category Mismatch Issues 
 
**Common Category Mismatch Scenarios:** 
 
| Mismatch | Example | Impact | Resolution | 
|----------|---------|--------|-----------| 
| **Category in Aadhaar vs Application** | Aadhaar: No category mention; Application: SC | 
Aadhaar does not have category field; not an issue | Caste certificate is the proof; Aadhaar 
irrelevant for category | 
| **Category in School Records vs Caste Certificate** | School TC: OBC; Caste Certificate: 
SC | Serious issue; indicates fraud or error | Correct school records or obtain correct caste 
certificate; investigation may be initiated | 
| **Caste Name Mismatch** | Certificate: "Pasi"; Application: "SC-Pasi" | Minor issue | Enter 
caste exactly as per certificate | 
| **Category Changed (not permissible)** | Student applied as OBC in Class 10, now 
applying as SC in Class 12 | Not allowed; caste does not change | Application rejected; must 
apply in correct category | 
| **OBC Certificate without NCL Mention** | Certificate issued as OBC but does not say 
Non-Creamy Layer | Application will be rejected | Obtain fresh OBC-NCL certificate | 
| **Minority Community Mismatch** | Application: Muslim; School records: Hindu | 
Investigation; possible fraud | Student must provide correct religion with proof; if fraudulent, 
disqualification | 
 
**Resolution Process for Category Mismatch:** 
1. **Minor Errors (spelling, format):** Correct during correction window; upload fresh 
certificate if needed 
2. **Major Mismatch (different category):** Application rejected; student must apply with 
correct category next year 
3. **Fraudulent Certificate:** Application rejected; student blacklisted; legal action possible 
4. **Issuing Authority Error:** Student obtains corrected certificate from issuing Tehsil with 
explanation; reapply or request review

## FAQs: 
 
**Q: My caste certificate is in Hindi. Can I upload it?** 
A: Yes, but the portal may require an English translation. Get the Hindi certificate translated 
and attested by the issuing authority or a gazetted officer, then upload both. 
 
**Q: I am OBC but my family income is ₹8,50,000. Can I apply for OBC scholarship?**

A: No. If your family income exceeds ₹2,00,000 (OBC scholarship limit for 2024-25), you are 
not eligible for OBC scholarship even if you are NCL for reservation purposes. 
 
**Q: My OBC certificate is 2 years old. Is it still valid?** 
A: Check the validity period mentioned on the certificate. If it states "Valid for 1 year" and is 
expired, you must renew it. If it states "Valid for 3 years" and is within that period, it is valid. 
 
**Q: I belong to General category. Can I get scholarship?** 
A: Yes, if your family income is within the prescribed limit for General category scholarship 
schemes (typically ₹1,00,000 - ₹2,00,000). Check available schemes for General/EWS 
students. 
 
**Q: I am a Muslim student. Do I need a Minority certificate?** 
A: For most UP and Central minority scholarships, you can declare your religion in the 
application. Some schemes may require a community certificate from SDM/Tehsildar; check 
specific scheme guidelines. 
 
**Q: My father is an IAS officer. Can I apply for OBC scholarship?** 
A: No. Children of IAS/IPS officers (above certain ranks) fall under the Creamy Layer and 
are not eligible for OBC benefits, even if the family belongs to an OBC caste. 
 
**Q: Can I change my category from OBC to General?** 
A: You cannot "change" your caste. If you were born into an OBC family, your caste is OBC. 
However, if you are OBC Creamy Layer or your income exceeds OBC scholarship limits, you 
may apply under General category schemes if you meet their eligibility.

For every Health — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India RAG document, use:

Scheme/Service → Government Level → Implementing Department/Agency → 
Objective → Current Status → Beneficiaries → Eligibility → Exclusions → 
Benefits/Coverage → Documents → Registration/Card → Hospital/Facility Process → 
Treatment/Service Process → Payment/DBT → Status → Common Problems → 
Correction → Grievance → Special Cases → District Availability → FAQs → Official 
Source → Notification/Order → Effective Date → Last Verified Date. 
And for this category, do not make your RAG act like a doctor. Its job should be 
government health scheme/service navigation, eligibility, documents, hospital 
discovery and beneficiary assistance. Medical diagnosis or treatment recommendations 
are a separate and much higher-risk problem.

financial-assistance schemes for women and children across UP via Anganwadi network,

### B2. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — UP (Topic Group 3) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY 2.0) 
- **Government Level:** Central Sector Scheme, implemented in UP 
- **UP Implementing Department:** Department of Women & Child Development, UP (via 
Anganwadi network)

- **Objective:** Provide cash incentive for wage-loss compensation and improved 
health/nutrition behaviour among pregnant/lactating women 
- **Active/Historical Status:** Active (revised guidelines effective from FY 2022-23) 
- **Target Beneficiaries:** Pregnant and lactating women (PW&LM) 
- **Eligibility:** All pregnant/lactating women EXCEPT those in central/state government or 
PSU regular employment (already receiving paid maternity benefit); benefit now covers first 
living child unconditionally, and second child only if the child is a girl (under PMMVY 2.0 
revised structure) 
- **Exclusions:** Government employees receiving paid maternity leave; women already 
availing similar benefit under another scheme (unless clarified by revised guidelines); 
miscarriage/stillbirth cases (partial installment already paid is not reclaimed, but full benefit 
not applicable beyond disbursed stage) 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** No income ceiling currently applied 
- **Benefits:** ₹5,000 for first living child (in specified installments); ₹6,000 additional for 
second child if girl child (as per revised 2022 structure) — amounts subject to current GO; 
check portal for latest split 
- **Documents:** Aadhaar card (self and, where applicable, husband), bank 
passbook/account details, Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card, pregnancy registration 
proof 
- **Registration:** At Anganwadi Centre or health facility; can also self-register via PMMVY 
mobile app/CSC 
- **Application:** Form 1-A (pregnancy registration), Form 1-B (after delivery/birth 
registration) submitted to AWW 
- **Verification:** AWW/ANM verify pregnancy and delivery details; CDPO approves 
- **Benefit/DBT:** Direct Benefit Transfer to Aadhaar-linked bank account, installment-wise 
- **Status:** Check on PMMVY portal/app using registration/mobile number 
- **Correction:** Beneficiary detail correction via AWC/CDPO login on portal 
- **Rejection:** Common reasons — Aadhaar mismatch, duplicate application, ineligible (2nd 
child not girl under revised norms, government employee), incomplete documents 
- **Grievance:** AWW → CDPO → DPO → State PMMVY Nodal Cell → Central grievance 
portal (pmmvy.wcd.gov.in grievance module) 
- **Special Cases:** Women without Aadhaar — provisional registration allowed with 
alternate ID pending Aadhaar linkage (see Topic Group 7); miscarriage after 1st installment 
— no recovery of paid installment, subsequent installment not released 
- **District Availability:** All 75 districts via Anganwadi network 
- **FAQs:** "Is PMMVY available for a second pregnancy?" → Only if second child is a girl, 
under current revised norms; "My installment is pending" → Check Aadhaar-bank linkage 
and AWC verification status 
- **Official Source:** pmmvy.wcd.gov.in 
- **Government Order/Notification:** PMMVY Revised Guidelines, effective 01 April 2022 
- **Effective Date:** 01 January 2017 (revised 01 April 2022) 
- **Last Verified Date:** 2025

### B3. Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — UP (Topic Group 4) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)

- **Government Level:** Centrally Sponsored Scheme under National Health Mission 
- **UP Implementing Department:** National Health Mission, UP (cross-referenced to Health 
domain for clinical aspects) 
- **Objective:** Promote institutional delivery to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality 
- **Active/Historical Status:** Active 
- **Target Beneficiaries:** Pregnant women delivering in accredited government/empanelled 
private health facilities; UP classified as a Low Performing State (LPS) — benefits available 
to all pregnant women irrespective of age/parity in rural and urban areas 
- **Eligibility:** All pregnant women opting for institutional delivery in government or 
accredited private facility; BPL/SC/ST home deliveries also eligible for a lower cash 
assistance in LPS states 
- **Exclusions:** Home delivery without ASHA facilitation (reduced/no benefit, except 
BPL/SC/ST provision) 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** No income restriction for institutional delivery in LPS 
states like UP; additional provisions for BPL/SC/ST 
- **Benefits:** Cash assistance for institutional delivery (rural: ~₹1,400; urban: ~₹1,000 — 
verify current NHM UP rate); ASHA incentive paid separately 
- **Documents:** MCP card, Aadhaar, bank account details, BPL/caste certificate (if 
applicable) 
- **Registration:** During pregnancy registration at Anganwadi/health facility with ASHA 
support 
- **Application:** No separate application; benefit auto-processed at time of institutional 
delivery via ASHA/facility records 
- **Verification:** Facility in-charge verifies delivery; ASHA confirms beneficiary details 
- **Benefit/DBT:** DBT to beneficiary's bank account post-delivery 
- **Status:** Check with ASHA/facility or Block Health office 
- **Correction:** Through facility records/Block Community Process Manager 
- **Rejection:** Non-institutional delivery without ASHA involvement (outside BPL/SC/ST 
provision) 
- **Grievance:** ASHA → ANM/Block Health office → CMO → NHM State Grievance Cell 
- **Special Cases:** Delayed payment — escalate to CMO office; multiple births — single 
benefit per delivery event 
- **District Availability:** All districts through CHC/PHC/District Hospitals and empanelled 
private facilities 
- **FAQs:** "How much does JSY pay in UP?" → Depends on rural/urban and category; 
verify current NHM UP rate list; "Payment delayed after delivery" → Contact ASHA/Block 
Health Office for DBT status 
- **Official Source:** nhm.up.gov.in, nhm.gov.in (JSY guidelines) 
- **Government Order/Notification:** JSY Guidelines, NHM 
- **Effective Date:** 2005 (ongoing) 
- **Last Verified Date:** 2025 
- **Related Domain Ref:** Health domain — institutional delivery care, ANC/PNC protocols

### B8. Pregnancy Benefit Eligibility Scenarios — UP (Topic Group 9) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** Special Eligibility Scenarios under PMMVY/JSY 
- **Government Level:** Central, State-implemented 
- **UP Implementing Department:** WCD Department, NHM

- **Active/Historical Status:** Active

 - **First child (any gender):** Full PMMVY benefit applicable

norms

component) 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** None 
- **Benefits:** As per scheme in applicable scenario

- **Application:** N/A beyond standard PMMVY/JSY application

### C2. Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (MKSY) — UP (Topic Groups 11, 12, 16) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (MKSY) 
- **Government Level:** State 
- **UP Implementing Department:** Department of Women & Child Development, UP 
- **Objective:** Improve birth, survival, nutrition, health, education, and social status of the 
girl child; reduce gender-based discrimination 
- **Active/Historical Status:** Active 
- **Target Beneficiaries:** Girl children of eligible resident UP families, from birth up to 
graduation-level education 
- **Eligibility:** Family must be a resident of UP; total family annual income up to ₹3,00,000 
(as per current norms — verify latest GO); maximum two girl children benefit per family, with 
a specific exception provision for the case where twin girls are born as the second delivery 
(i.e., up to 3 daughters may be covered where the first delivery is a single girl and the 
second delivery results in twin/triplet girls) — check current scheme rule for the exact 
multi-birth provision 
- **Exclusions:** Families with income above the prescribed ceiling; adopted children only 
eligible if adoption is legally registered under applicable adoption laws; more than two 
daughters generally excluded except the twin/multiple-birth exception 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** Annual family income ceiling ₹3,00,000 (verify current 
threshold on portal, as it has been revised historically) 
- **Benefits (Stage-wise, current amounts to be verified against latest GO):** 
 1. **Stage 1 — Birth of girl child:** One-time cash incentive 
 2. **Stage 2 — Full immunization (up to 1 year):** Cash incentive on completion of 
immunization schedule 
 3. **Stage 3 — Admission to Class 1:** Cash incentive on school admission 
 4. **Stage 4 — Admission to Class 6:** Cash incentive 
 5. **Stage 5 — Admission to Class 9:** Cash incentive 
 6. **Stage 6 — Admission to Class 10/12 or equivalent vocational course, plus enrolment in 
graduation/2-year diploma course after Class 12:** Final-stage cash incentive 
- **Documents:** Birth certificate, Aadhaar (child and parent), immunization card, school 
admission/bonafide certificate, income certificate, domicile certificate, bank passbook, family 
ID (Ration Card), passport-size photograph 
- **Registration:** Online via mksy.up.gov.in citizen registration portal (self) or through 
Common Service Centre (CSC)/Anganwadi Centre assistance 
- **Application:** Apply at relevant stage with stage-specific evidence document uploaded on 
portal

- **Verification:** Application verified sequentially by Anganwadi Worker/Village-level 
functionary → CDPO/Block Level Officer → District Programme Officer (DPO)/District 
Magistrate approval 
- **Benefit/DBT:** Direct Benefit Transfer to girl child's or guardian's Aadhaar-linked bank 
account per stage 
- **Status:** Track via mksy.up.gov.in using registration ID/mobile number login 
- **Correction:** Beneficiary/guardian can request correction of name, DOB, Aadhaar, bank 
details through portal edit option or DPO office 
- **Rejection:** Common reasons — income certificate exceeds ceiling, more than two 
daughters (without applicable exception), duplicate application, document mismatch, 
incomplete stage evidence 
- **Grievance:** AWC/CSC → CDPO → DPO → State MKSY Nodal Cell (WCD Department) 
→ CM Helpline 1076 
- **Special Cases:** Twin/multiple daughters at second delivery — special provision applies 
(verify current rule); adopted daughters — eligible if legal adoption process completed as per 
adoption law; orphan girls under legal guardianship also eligible with guardian details 
- **District Availability:** All 75 districts 
- **FAQs:** "What is the income limit for Kanya Sumangala Yojana?" → ₹3,00,000 per 
annum family income (verify current threshold); "My daughter just started Class 1 — how do 
I apply for Stage 3?" → Log in to mksy.up.gov.in, select Stage 3, upload school admission 
proof; "Is a second daughter eligible?" → Yes, up to two daughters per family are eligible 
(special exception for twins at second delivery) 
- **Official Source:** mksy.up.gov.in 
- **Government Order/Notification:** UP Cabinet approval GO dated 2019 (scheme launch), 
subsequent revision GOs for income ceiling/benefit amount updates 
- **Effective Date:** 01 April 2019 
- **Last Verified Date:** 2025

### E1. Widow Welfare & Widow Pension — UP (Topic Groups 36-43) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** UP Widow (Vidhwa) Pension Scheme — officially "Rashtriya 
Vayoshri/Vidhwa Pension Yojana" (state-administered, converged with National Social 
Assistance Programme's National Family Benefit/Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension 
Scheme where applicable) 
- **Government Level:** State scheme with Central (NSAP) convergence 
- **UP Implementing Department:** Department of Women & Child Development, UP 
(Widow Pension is administered by WCD in UP, distinct from Old Age/Divyang Pension 
under Social Welfare Department) 
- **Objective:** Provide monthly financial assistance to widowed women for livelihood 
support 
- **Active/Historical Status:** Active 
- **Target Beneficiaries:** Widowed women residing in UP 
- **Eligibility:** Widow aged 18 years and above (specific age band per current GO, 
commonly 18-60 with those above 60 sometimes shifted to Old Age Pension); resident of 
UP; husband's death certificate available; family income within prescribed ceiling 
- **Exclusions:** Widows already receiving old-age pension or another government pension 
of equal/higher value under a different scheme (no dual benefit typically allowed); remarried 
women (eligibility ceases upon remarriage as per scheme rule); income above prescribed 
ceiling 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** Annual family income ceiling as per current UP GO 
(commonly ₹2,00,000 for rural, verify current threshold; historically differentiated rural/urban 
ceilings have applied — check latest notification) 
- **Benefits:** Monthly pension amount (verify current amount from latest GO — has been 
revised periodically, e.g., ₹300-₹1,000 range historically; confirm current disbursed amount) 
- **Documents:** Husband's death certificate, Aadhaar card, residence/domicile certificate, 
income certificate, bank passbook, passport photograph, age proof 
- **Registration:** Online application via UP Widow Pension portal (sspy-up.gov.in or 
wcd.up.gov.in linked portal) or offline through Block/Tehsil/District Social Welfare/WCD office 
- **Application:** Submit application with required documents; can also apply through 
Common Service Centre (CSC)/Jan Seva Kendra 
- **Verification:** Verification by Village-level (Lekhpal/Gram Panchayat) → Block 
Development Officer/CDPO → District Programme Officer/District Magistrate approval 
- **Benefit/DBT:** Direct Benefit Transfer to Aadhaar-linked bank account, disbursed 
monthly/quarterly as per state schedule 
- **Status:** Trackable via application ID on official portal 
- **Correction:** Update bank/Aadhaar/address details via portal login or District WCD office

- **Rejection:** Common reasons — income certificate exceeds ceiling, incomplete 
documents, duplicate beneficiary already receiving another pension, death certificate 
discrepancy 
- **Grievance:** Village/Block office → District Programme Officer (DPO)/District Social 
Welfare Officer → State WCD Grievance Cell → CM Helpline 1076 
- **Payment Failure:** DBT failure due to Aadhaar-bank mismatch, closed account, or 
Aadhaar authentication issue — resolved by updating bank seeding at branch and reporting 
to DPO for reprocessing 
- **Rejection/Cancellation:** Pension can be cancelled upon remarriage, death of 
beneficiary, or discovery of ineligibility (e.g., income misdeclaration); beneficiary/family can 
appeal cancellation to DPO with evidence 
- **Special Cases:** Widow with children — pension continues independently; children may 
separately access education scholarships, Kanya Sumangala (for daughters), or child 
welfare schemes without affecting widow pension eligibility 
- **District Availability:** All 75 districts through District WCD/Social Welfare offices 
- **FAQs:** "How do I apply for widow pension in UP?" → Apply online via the state pension 
portal or at your Block/District WCD office with death certificate, Aadhaar, income and 
residence proof; "My pension has stopped — what should I do?" → Check for Aadhaar/bank 
mismatch, remarriage record flag, or re-verification requirement at DPO office; "Is there an 
age limit for widow pension?" → Yes, check current age band in the applicable GO (verify 
latest notification for exact limits) 
- **Official Source:** sspy-up.gov.in, wcd.up.gov.in 
- **Government Order/Notification:** UP Widow Pension Scheme GO (periodically revised 
for amount/income ceiling) 
- **Effective Date:** Ongoing (scheme predates current GO; amounts revised periodically) 
- **Last Verified Date:** 2025

## SECTION H: MARRIAGE-RELATED WELFARE 
 
### H1. Marriage-Related Welfare Schemes — UP (Topic Groups 73, 74, 75) 
 
- **Scheme/Service Name:** Mukhyamantri Samuhik Vivah Yojana (Chief Minister's Mass 
Marriage Scheme) 
- **Government Level:** State 
- **UP Implementing Department:** Department of Social Welfare / Department of Women & 
Child Development, UP (implemented at District/Block/ULB level) 
- **Objective:** Provide financial assistance for marriage of daughters from economically 
weaker/BPL families through organized mass marriage ceremonies 
- **Active/Historical Status:** Active 
- **Target Beneficiaries:** Daughters of BPL/economically weaker families (including 
widows', destitute women's, and SC/ST/OBC/General category families as per scheme's 
inclusive criteria), of legal marriageable age 
- **Eligibility:** Bride must have attained legal marriageable age (18 years); family income 
within prescribed BPL/economically weaker ceiling (verify current threshold, e.g., ₹2,00,000 
or as notified); UP domicile; participation through organized mass marriage event conducted 
by Gram Panchayat/ULB/Block 
- **Exclusions:** Underage marriage (strictly excluded and illegal); families above income 
ceiling; second marriage of the same beneficiary generally not covered 
- **Income/Category Conditions:** Income ceiling as per current GO; priority to BPL, widow's 
daughters, destitute women, and SC/ST/minority/economically weaker general category

- **Benefits:** Cash assistance to the couple (a portion may be deposited in bride's account, 
part utilized for essential household items/marriage expenses as per scheme structure), and 
provision of basic household items at the mass marriage ceremony 
- **Documents:** Aadhaar (bride and groom), age proof, income certificate, caste certificate 
(if applicable), residence/domicile certificate, bank account of bride, passport photographs 
- **Registration:** Apply through Gram Panchayat/Block Office/Urban Local Body prior to 
scheduled mass marriage event; online application may also be available via respective 
district/Samaj Kalyan portal 
- **Application:** Submit application with documents before the district/block-level cutoff date 
announced for the mass marriage event 
- **Verification:** Verification of age, income, and family details by Gram Panchayat 
Secretary/Block Development Officer/ULB officer; final approval by District Magistrate/District 
Social Welfare Officer 
- **Benefit/DBT:** DBT to bride's bank account for cash component; in-kind items provided at 
the ceremony 
- **Status:** Check with Block/ULB office or district Samaj Kalyan Vibhag 
- **Correction:** Through Block/ULB office prior to event finalization 
- **Rejection:** Underage bride/groom, income above ceiling, incomplete documents, 
application after cutoff date 
- **Grievance:** Block/ULB office → District Social Welfare Officer → State Social Welfare 
Department 
- **Special Cases:** Inter-caste marriage — if a separate active inter-caste marriage 
incentive scheme is currently notified in UP (e.g., Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Scheme for 
inter-caste marriage incentive), eligibility and benefit are evaluated independently from 
Samuhik Vivah Yojana; verify current active status and eligibility criteria (typically one partner 
must be SC/ST) with the Social Welfare Department before advising a citizen, as such 
schemes are periodically revised 
- **District Availability:** Organized periodically at Block/District/ULB level across all districts 
- **FAQs:** "How do I get my daughter's marriage registered under Samuhik Vivah Yojana?" 
→ Apply at your Gram Panchayat/Block office or ULB before the announced mass marriage 
event date, with income, age, and residence proof; "Is there separate assistance for 
inter-caste marriage in UP?" → Check with the Social Welfare Department for the current 
status of any active inter-caste marriage incentive scheme, as eligibility (typically requiring 
one partner to be from SC/ST category) is defined independently 
- **Official Source:** sspy-up.gov.in, socialwelfare.up.gov.in

scheme, periodically revised for benefit amount/income ceiling)

 3. For infants, enrol Aadhaar through Anganwadi-facilitated camps or Aadhaar centre with
