### I5. Application Status, Correction, Rejection Framework (Topic Groups 83, 84, 85)

- **Standard Status Categories (applicable across PMMVY, MKSY, Widow Pension, Samuhik 
Vivah Yojana):** Registered/Submitted → Verification Pending (AWW/Village level) → Under 
Review (CDPO/Block level) → Approved/Sanctioned (DPO/District level) → Payment 
Pending → Payment Processed/Disbursed → Payment Failed (technical) → Rejected 
(eligibility/document failure) 
- **Standard Correction Process:** Beneficiary/guardian requests correction of name, DOB, 
Aadhaar, bank account, address, income, or category detail through the scheme's online 
portal edit function (where available) or by visiting the AWC/CDPO/DPO office with 
supporting documents; corrections are re-verified before status resumes progression 
- **Standard Rejection Reasons (common across schemes):** Duplicate beneficiary entry, 
eligibility criteria not met (income/age/category), document mismatch (name/DOB 
inconsistency across Aadhaar/certificate/application), incomplete verification at village/block 
level, invalid or expired certificate (income/caste/domicile), ineligible family composition (e.g., 
more than two daughters for MKSY without exception) 
- **Appeal/Reapplication:** Rejected applicants may reapply after correcting the identified 
deficiency; formal appeal can be made to the next administrative level (CDPO → DPO → 
State Nodal Cell) 
- **Official Source:** Scheme-specific portals (pmmvy.wcd.gov.in, mksy.up.gov.in, 
sspy-up.gov.in)

## SECTION J: SCENARIO, COMPARISON & CROSS-DOMAIN QUERY BANK 
 
### J1. Eligibility Scenario Questions (Topic Group 94) 
 
**Q: "I am pregnant and live in UP; which benefits may apply?"** 
A: You may check eligibility (each assessed independently) for: (1) Pregnancy registration at 
your local Anganwadi/ASHA; (2) PMMVY cash assistance if this is your first child (or second 
child if a girl, under revised norms); (3) JSY institutional delivery incentive if you deliver at a 
government/empanelled facility; (4) JSSK free delivery/diagnostics/transport at government 
facilities; (5) Take-Home Ration from your Anganwadi Centre. Confirm exact eligibility with 
your AWW/ASHA. 
 
**Q: "I have two daughters; which schemes should I check?"** 
A: Check Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana (MKSY) for both daughters (subject to 
the two-daughter/twin-birth provision and family income ceiling), Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana 
(savings scheme, no income ceiling), and applicable education scholarships as they 
progress through school, each evaluated independently. 
 
**Q: "I am a widow with two children; what assistance is available?"** 
A: You may check UP Widow Pension for yourself (subject to age/income eligibility), and 
independently check education/scholarship schemes and Kanya Sumangala Yojana (if 
children include daughters) for your children — pension and child schemes are evaluated on 
separate criteria and do not affect each other. 
 
--- 
 
### J2. Anganwadi Scenario Questions (Topic Group 95) 
 
**Q: "My child's name is not registered at the Anganwadi."** 
A: Visit your nearest AWC with the child's birth certificate/Aadhaar (if available) and request 
registration; the AWW will add the child to the beneficiary register and Poshan Tracker. 
 
**Q: "THR was not provided this month."** 
A: Report to your AWW first; if unresolved, escalate to the CDPO/Block office, and further to 
the DPO if necessary. 
 
**Q: "I moved to another district — what do I do about Anganwadi services?"** 
A: Register at the Anganwadi Centre in your new location with proof of residence/relocation; 
inform your previous AWC so records are updated to prevent duplicate/inactive entries. 
 
**Q: "My pregnancy registration is incorrect."** 
A: Visit the AWC/ANM where you registered and request correction of details (LMP date, 
contact number, address) with supporting ID. 
 
--- 
 
### J3. Girl-Child Scenario Questions (Topic Group 96)

**Q: "My daughter has entered Class 1; is there a benefit?"** 
A: Yes, under Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana, Class 1 admission is a defined 
benefit stage (Stage 3); apply on mksy.up.gov.in with the school admission proof, subject to 
family eligibility. 
 
**Q: "My Kanya Sumangala installment is pending."** 
A: Check application status on mksy.up.gov.in; common causes include pending document 
verification, Aadhaar-bank mismatch, or stage-evidence not yet approved by CDPO/DPO — 
follow up at your CDPO office. 
 
**Q: "My daughter's Aadhaar name differs from her birth certificate."** 
A: Get the discrepancy corrected — either update Aadhaar to match the birth certificate at 
an Aadhaar Seva Kendra, or correct the birth certificate at the issuing Registrar — then 
update the MKSY/scheme application accordingly. 
 
--- 
 
### J4. Widow Assistance Scenarios (Topic Group 97) 
 
**Q: "My husband died recently; where should I apply for pension?"** 
A: Apply for UP Widow Pension via the state pension portal (sspy-up.gov.in) or at your 
Block/District WCD/Social Welfare office, with the death certificate, Aadhaar, income, and 
residence proof. 
 
**Q: "Pension stopped suddenly."** 
A: This may be due to re-verification requirements, Aadhaar-bank mismatch, or a status 
change (e.g., remarriage flag, income update); check with your DPO/District WCD office for 
the specific reason and required corrective action. 
 
**Q: "Bank account changed — will my pension still come?"** 
A: You must update your new bank/Aadhaar-seeding details with the DPO/District WCD 
office promptly, or payments will fail/be held pending correction. 
 
**Q: "Application rejected — what can I do?"** 
A: Review the rejection reason (commonly income certificate issues, incomplete documents, 
or duplicate beneficiary flags), correct the deficiency, and reapply or file an appeal with the 
DPO office.

### J5. Scheme Comparison Questions (Topic Group 98) 
 
**PMMVY vs JSY:** 
- PMMVY: Central cash-transfer scheme for wage-loss compensation; conditional on 
pregnancy/childbirth event (1st child unconditional; 2nd child only if girl); administered by 
WCD via Anganwadi.

- JSY: Central cash incentive specifically tied to institutional delivery; administered by NHM 
via ASHA/health facility; no restriction on child parity/gender in UP (LPS state). 
- Both can typically be availed for the same pregnancy independently, as they serve different 
objectives (general maternity support vs. institutional delivery promotion) — confirm no 
overlap restriction with current guidelines. 
 
**Maternity Assistance vs Anganwadi Nutrition:** 
- Maternity assistance (PMMVY/JSY) is cash-based, tied to specific pregnancy/delivery 
milestones. 
- Anganwadi nutrition (THR/HCM) is in-kind, continuous support provided through 
registration at the AWC, independent of cash scheme status. 
 
**Kanya Sumangala vs Education Scholarships:** 
- MKSY is a UP state scheme with defined life-stage benefits (birth to graduation) tied to 
family income ceiling and daughter-count conditions. 
- Education scholarships (Pre-Matric/Post-Matric, SC/ST/OBC/Minority) are separate 
Central/State schemes with their own income/category criteria, generally renewable annually 
based on academic enrolment, and can be availed alongside MKSY. 
 
**Widow Pension vs Other Social Pensions:** 
- Widow Pension is specific to widowed women meeting age/income/residency criteria. 
- Old Age Pension and Divyang (Disability) Pension are separate schemes under different 
eligibility criteria (age 60+, disability certification respectively); a woman typically cannot 
draw both Widow Pension and Old Age Pension simultaneously once she crosses into the 
old-age eligibility bracket — confirm current dual-benefit restriction with the Social 
Welfare/WCD Department.

### J6. Cross-Domain Queries (Topic Group 99) 
 
**Q: "I am a woman farmer and also pregnant — what benefits apply?"** 
A: Maternity benefits (PMMVY/JSY/JSSK) are evaluated independently of your farming 
status. Separately, check agriculture-domain schemes such as PM-Kisan (household-based) 
— refer to the Farmer & Agriculture corpus for farming-specific benefits, as these are 
assessed under entirely separate eligibility criteria. 
 
**Q: "I am a widow — can I also get a ration card and pension together?"** 
A: Yes, Widow Pension (WCD/Social Welfare Department) and a Ration Card (Food & Civil 
Supplies Department, cross-domain) are independent entitlements; you should apply for 
both separately, as one does not depend on the other. 
 
**Q: "My daughter got a scholarship — can she still get Kanya Sumangala Yojana?"** 
A: Yes, MKSY and education scholarships are independent schemes with separate eligibility 
and application processes; receiving one does not disqualify her from the other, subject to 
each scheme's own criteria. 
 
**Q: "I am a registered construction worker and pregnant — what applies?"**

A: Check UP BOCW Welfare Board maternity benefit (labour-domain, registration-based) 
independently alongside PMMVY/JSY/JSSK (WCD/Health-domain, pregnancy-based) — 
each is evaluated on its own separate eligibility criteria.

Document ID: HP-UP-001​
Category: Health → Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY​
Government Level: Central Government + State Government (Joint Implementation)​
Implementing Department/Agency: National Health Authority (NHA) — Central | State Health 
Agency (SHA), Uttar Pradesh — State | Also known as: Ayushman Bharat State Health 
Agency UP​
Scheme Name (Full): Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)​
Current Status: Active​
Effective Date: Launched nationally September 23, 2018; implemented in Uttar Pradesh 
from 2018 onward​
Last Verified Date: June 2025 
 
Objective 
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is the world's largest government-funded health assurance 
scheme. Its primary objective is to provide financial protection against catastrophic health 
expenditure to poor and vulnerable families across India, including Uttar Pradesh, by offering 
cashless and paperless access to healthcare services at empanelled government and 
private hospitals. 
The scheme aims to: 
●​ Reduce out-of-pocket health expenditure for economically weaker sections 
●​ Improve access to secondary and tertiary care hospitalization 
●​ Reduce the financial burden caused by serious illness on poor families 
●​ Cover approximately 50 crore beneficiaries at the national level from identified 
households 
 
Implementation in Uttar Pradesh

Uttar Pradesh implements PM-JAY through the State Health Agency (SHA), UP under the 
Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Uttar Pradesh. UP is one of the 
largest implementing states with a significant number of empanelled hospitals across 
districts. 
Key implementation features in UP: 
●​ State Health Agency (SHA) UP coordinates beneficiary management, hospital 
empanelment, claims and grievances 
●​ District-level implementation is managed through Chief Medical Officers (CMOs) and 
District Implementation Units 
●​ Hospitals are empanelled at both government and private levels 
●​ ASHA workers and Arogya Mitras at hospitals support beneficiary access 
●​ The Ayushman Card (also called PM-JAY Golden Card) is issued to identified 
beneficiaries 
 
Beneficiaries 
PM-JAY beneficiaries in UP are identified based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census 
(SECC) 2011 database for rural and urban areas. The scheme does not have an 
income-based eligibility threshold as such — it follows deprivation/occupational criteria from 
SECC. 
Approximate scale in UP: 
●​ Crores of families identified in UP from SECC data 
●​ Both rural and urban families are covered under defined SECC criteria 
●​ Each eligible family can have all members covered (no family-size cap under 
PM-JAY) 
 
Eligibility 
Rural Families — Eligible if at least one of the following deprivation criteria from SECC 2011 
is met: 
1.​ Only one room with kuchha walls and kuchha roof 
2.​ No adult member between 16 and 59 years of age 
3.​ Female-headed household with no adult male member between 16 and 59 years 
4.​ Differently-abled member / no able-bodied adult member 
5.​ SC/ST households 
6.​ Landless household deriving major income from manual casual labour 
Automatically included rural categories:

●​ Households without shelter 
●​ Destitute / living on alms 
●​ Manual scavenger families 
●​ Primitive tribal groups 
●​ Legally released bonded labourers 
Urban Families — Eligible based on occupational categories from SECC 2011, including: 
●​ Ragpicker 
●​ Beggar 
●​ Domestic worker 
●​ Street vendor / cobbler / hawker 
●​ Construction worker / plumber / mason / painter / welder / security guard 
●​ Sweeper / sanitation worker 
●​ Home-based worker / artisan / handicraft worker 
●​ Transport worker (driver, conductor, helper, cart/rickshaw puller) 
●​ Shop worker / assistant / delivery assistant / waiter 
●​ Electrician / mechanic / assembler / repair worker 
●​ Washer-man / chowkidar 
Note: Eligibility is determined from SECC 2011 data. New families not in SECC 2011 may 
not automatically qualify. The Government of India and UP have periodically updated 
inclusion criteria — always verify current status through official channels. 
 
Exclusions 
The following categories are not eligible under PM-JAY: 
●​ Families with two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, fishing boats (unless 
occupational) registered in family name 
●​ Families with mechanized agricultural equipment 
●​ Families with Kisan Credit Card with credit limit of ₹50,000 or more 
●​ Government employees (Central or State) 
●​ Families managed or assisted by Government non-agriculture enterprises 
●​ Families with any member earning more than ₹10,000 per month 
●​ Families paying income tax 
●​ Families with refrigerators 
●​ Families with landline telephone 
●​ Families owning more than 2.5 acres of irrigated land 
●​ Families owning 5 acres or more of irrigated land for two or more crop seasons 
Treatment-level exclusions (services not covered under PM-JAY): 
●​ OPD (Outpatient) consultation charges 
●​ Drug purchase for OPD purposes

●​ Fertility-related treatments 
●​ Cosmetic surgery (unless medically required post-injury/illness) 
●​ Organ transplantation (donor side cost) 
●​ Individual diagnostics without hospitalization 
●​ Self-inflicted injuries 
●​ Substance-abuse-related treatment (in most package categories) 
 
Coverage / Benefits 
●​ Health cover: ₹5,00,000 (Five Lakh Rupees) per family per year 
●​ Nature of coverage: Cashless and paperless hospitalization 
●​ Portability: Beneficiary can avail treatment at any empanelled hospital across India, 
not just UP 
●​ Pre-hospitalization: Medical expenses 3 days before hospitalization (as per 
applicable package) 
●​ Post-hospitalization: Medical expenses 15 days after discharge (as per applicable 
package) 
●​ Covered services: Approximately 1,500+ treatment packages covering surgeries, 
medical treatments, diagnostics needed for admitted treatment, ICU charges, 
medicines during hospitalization, follow-up post discharge (as per package) 
●​ No cap on family size: All members of an eligible family are covered under the ₹5 
lakh annual limit 
 
Documents Generally Required 
1.​ Aadhaar Card (for e-KYC and identity verification) 
2.​ Ration Card / Family Register (to verify family membership in some cases) 
3.​ Mobile number (linked to Aadhaar preferred) 
4.​ Any government-issued identity document if Aadhaar is not immediately available (for 
hospital visit — Arogya Mitra can assist) 
 
Ayushman Card (PM-JAY Golden Card) 
●​ The Ayushman Card is issued after Aadhaar-based e-KYC to eligible beneficiaries 
●​ It contains the beneficiary's name, photo, PM-JAY ID, QR code 
●​ It can be downloaded digitally via the Ayushman Bharat portal or app 
●​ Physical and digital cards are both valid 
●​ Card generation does not create eligibility — eligibility comes from SECC data; card 
is a proof of eligibility

Empanelled Hospitals in UP 
●​ Both government hospitals (district hospitals, medical colleges, CHCs) and private 
hospitals are empanelled 
●​ Hospital empanelment status can change — always verify before treatment 
●​ Empanelled hospitals must have an Ayushman Help Desk (Arogya Mitra) for 
beneficiary assistance 
●​ Hospital list is available on the official PM-JAY portal: pmjay.gov.in and state SHA 
portal 
 
Treatment Process (Summary) 
1.​ Beneficiary reaches empanelled hospital 
2.​ Visits Ayushman Help Desk (Arogya Mitra) 
3.​ Beneficiary verification through Aadhaar/card/PM-JAY ID 
4.​ Eligibility confirmed → admission processed 
5.​ Pre-authorization obtained by hospital (where required) 
6.​ Treatment provided → cashless to beneficiary 
7.​ Hospital submits claim to SHA/insurance company 
8.​ Beneficiary discharged without payment for covered package

What is the Ayushman Card? 
The Ayushman Card (officially called PM-JAY Beneficiary Identification System card or 
commonly referred to as the PM-JAY Golden Card) is a government-issued health identity 
card that: 
●​ Identifies a beneficiary as eligible under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY 
●​ Contains the beneficiary's name, photograph, Ayushman/PM-JAY ID number, QR 
code 
●​ Enables cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals across India 
●​ Acts as a proof of PM-JAY eligibility at the hospital's Ayushman Help Desk 
●​ Can be used in digital (downloaded) or physical form 
Important clarification: The Ayushman Card does not create eligibility. Eligibility is 
determined from the SECC 2011 database. The card is a proof document issued after 
eligibility is confirmed and e-KYC is completed. 
 
Who Can Obtain the Ayushman Card? 
Any person whose name appears in the PM-JAY beneficiary list (based on SECC 2011 data) 
and who completes the required Aadhaar-based e-KYC process is eligible to obtain the 
Ayushman Card. 
●​ All family members listed in the PM-JAY beneficiary database can individually 
generate their Ayushman Card 
●​ Children, women, elderly — all listed members can have their own card 
●​ There is no restriction on multiple family members having individual cards 
 
How to Check Eligibility Before Card Generation

Before attempting to generate the card, a citizen should verify whether their family/name 
appears in the PM-JAY beneficiary list: 
Step 1 — Online Check: 
●​ Visit pmjay.gov.in 
●​ Click on "Am I Eligible?" section 
●​ Enter mobile number → receive OTP 
●​ After OTP verification, search by Name + State + District + Village/Ward OR by 
Ration Card Number OR by SECC/HHD Number OR by PMJAY ID 
Step 2 — Through CSC (Common Service Centre): 
●​ Visit nearest Jan Seva Kendra / CSC 
●​ Operator can check eligibility on the portal 
Step 3 — At Empanelled Hospital: 
●​ Arogya Mitra at the Ayushman Help Desk can check eligibility 
●​ Beneficiary need not have the card already to check eligibility 
Step 4 — Ayushman Bharat App: 
●​ Available on Android Play Store 
●​ Self-check facility for citizens 
If name is found: Proceed to e-KYC and card generation​
If name is not found: May need to verify through district health office; walk-in addition is 
generally not possible without meeting SECC criteria 
 
Card Generation Process 
Method 1 — Through CSC/Jan Seva Kendra (Common Service Centre): 
1.​ Visit nearest CSC/Jan Seva Kendra 
2.​ Operator searches for beneficiary in the system 
3.​ Beneficiary provides Aadhaar card 
4.​ Aadhaar-based e-KYC is performed (OTP on Aadhaar-linked mobile or biometric) 
5.​ Photograph is captured (if required) 
6.​ Card is generated in the system 
7.​ Card can be printed or downloaded 
Method 2 — Through Empanelled Hospital's Ayushman Help Desk (Arogya Mitra): 
1.​ Visit the Ayushman Help Desk at any empanelled hospital

2.​ Arogya Mitra verifies beneficiary in the system 
3.​ e-KYC completed with Aadhaar 
4.​ Card generated and provided 
Method 3 — Self-Generation via Ayushman Bharat App / Portal (where available for 
citizens): 
1.​ Download Ayushman Bharat app or visit the portal 
2.​ Login with mobile number 
3.​ Search family 
4.​ Complete OTP/Aadhaar-based e-KYC for each member 
5.​ Download the generated card as PDF

What is e-KYC in PM-JAY Context? 
e-KYC (Electronic Know Your Customer) in PM-JAY is the Aadhaar-based identity 
verification process that must be completed before an Ayushman Card is generated. It 
ensures that: 
●​ The person claiming the card is genuinely the listed beneficiary 
●​ The beneficiary's current photograph is captured 
●​ The identity is authenticated against the UIDAI (Aadhaar) database 
e-KYC is mandatory for card generation. Without successful e-KYC, the Ayushman Card 
cannot be issued. 
 
Aadhaar Authentication Process 
OTP-Based e-KYC: 
1.​ Beneficiary's Aadhaar number is entered into the system 
2.​ OTP is sent to the mobile number registered with Aadhaar 
3.​ Beneficiary enters OTP to authenticate 
4.​ Identity is verified against UIDAI database 
5.​ Card generation proceeds 
Biometric-Based e-KYC: 
1.​ Beneficiary's Aadhaar number is entered 
2.​ Fingerprint scan is taken using biometric device (available at CSC/hospital) 
3.​ Fingerprint matched against UIDAI records 
4.​ Identity verified

5.​ Card generation proceeds 
When biometric is typically used: 
●​ Mobile number not linked to Aadhaar 
●​ OTP is not received 
●​ Elderly beneficiaries whose fingerprints may be difficult to capture (iris scan may also 
be available in some setups) 
 
Name/DOB Mismatch Issues 
If the name or date of birth in the PM-JAY beneficiary database does not match the Aadhaar 
record: 
●​ The e-KYC may fail or the card may show incorrect data 
●​ The system compares SECC data with Aadhaar data during the process 
●​ Minor spelling differences may still allow card generation with Aadhaar authentication 
Resolution steps for mismatch: 
1.​ Check what the PM-JAY record shows vs. what Aadhaar shows 
2.​ If Aadhaar data is correct and SECC data is wrong → request data correction 
through CSC/hospital help desk with supporting documents 
3.​ If Aadhaar data needs updating → update Aadhaar first at nearest Aadhaar Seva 
Kendra, then retry e-KYC 
4.​ Submit correction documents: Birth certificate, school certificate, ration card (with 
correct details)

Meaning of Cashless Treatment 
Cashless treatment means the eligible PM-JAY beneficiary does not pay money out of 
pocket for covered treatment packages at empanelled hospitals. The hospital directly claims 
reimbursement from the government/insurance agency. The beneficiary receives the 
treatment without paying. 
Key points: 
●​ Cashless = no money to be paid by beneficiary for covered packages 
●​ It does not mean the beneficiary can demand any treatment regardless of package 
availability 
●​ Cashless applies only to packages listed under PM-JAY 
●​ Only empanelled hospitals provide cashless treatment 
 
Beneficiary Process at Empanelled Hospital (Step-by-Step) 
Step 1 — Arrive at Hospital 
●​ Visit any empanelled government or private hospital 
●​ Look for the Ayushman Help Desk (usually at the entrance or OPD area) 
Step 2 — Meet Arogya Mitra 
●​ The Arogya Mitra is a trained hospital staff member at the Ayushman Help Desk 
●​ Inform them you are an Ayushman PM-JAY beneficiary 
●​ They will help you through the entire process 
Step 3 — Beneficiary Verification 
●​ Arogya Mitra will search for your name in the PM-JAY system 
●​ Provide: Name, district, Aadhaar number, PM-JAY ID (if available) or Ration 
Card

●​ Your eligibility is confirmed in the system 
Step 4 — Identity Verification 
●​ Aadhaar-based OTP or biometric verification at the hospital 
●​ Photo on the card/system is compared 
●​ Identity is confirmed 
Step 5 — Admission Processed 
●​ Arogya Mitra and hospital staff initiate cashless admission 
●​ Patient details are entered in the system 
●​ Appropriate PM-JAY treatment package is identified 
Step 6 — Pre-Authorization (If Required) 
●​ For planned/elective surgeries, the hospital submits a pre-authorization 
request to the SHA/insurance company 
●​ Authorization is typically processed within a few hours to a day 
●​ Emergency treatment does not wait for pre-authorization 
Step 7 — Treatment 
●​ Patient receives treatment under the approved package 
●​ All bills are managed between hospital and SHA/insurance 
●​ Patient should not be asked to pay for covered services 
Step 8 — Discharge 
●​ After treatment, discharge is processed in the PM-JAY system 
●​ Patient is discharged without paying for covered services 
●​ Discharge summary and medications (as per package) are provided

Possible Legitimate Reasons for Hospital Declining Treatment 
A hospital may legitimately decline PM-JAY cashless treatment if: 
1.​ Hospital is not currently empanelled for the specific specialty or the required package 
2.​ Annual family limit (₹5 lakh) is exhausted for that year 
3.​ Treatment/package requested is not in the PM-JAY package list 
4.​ Beneficiary identity/eligibility cannot be verified (authentication failure, beneficiary not 
in database) 
5.​ Hospital's ICU/specialty ward beds are full (capacity issue — not a PM-JAY-specific 
refusal) 
6.​ The hospital's PM-JAY empanelment has been suspended or contract has expired 
 
Improper / Illegal Refusal Situations 
A hospital may be improperly refusing PM-JAY treatment if: 
●​ Beneficiary is eligible and the package is available at that hospital, but hospital says 
they "don't do PM-JAY" 
●​ Hospital agrees the patient is eligible but demands full payment first (for a covered 
package) 
●​ Hospital says "PM-JAY beds are full" without offering alternative arrangement 
●​ Hospital staff ask the beneficiary to pay and claim reimbursement later (for a covered 
cashless package) 
●​ Hospital treats beneficiary poorly or disrespectfully to discourage PM-JAY usage 
 
What the Beneficiary Should Ask the Hospital 
If a hospital refuses or is reluctant: 
1.​ Ask specifically: "Is this hospital currently empanelled under PM-JAY for this 
treatment?" 
2.​ Ask to meet the Arogya Mitra at the Ayushman Help Desk 
3.​ Ask for the reason in writing — hospitals should be able to provide a reason 
4.​ Ask: "If you cannot treat me under PM-JAY, can you refer me to a nearby hospital 
that can?" 
5.​ Check the PM-JAY app/portal to confirm hospital empanelment status independently 
 
Grievance Process for Improper Refusal

Step 1 — At the Hospital: 
●​ Speak to the Arogya Mitra and hospital's PM-JAY nodal officer 
●​ Request written acknowledgment of the situation 
Step 2 — Call the Helpline: 
●​ 14555 / 1800-111-565 — PM-JAY national helpline 
●​ Describe the situation, hospital name, date, your PM-JAY ID/Aadhaar 
●​ Helpline can provide real-time guidance and file a complaint 
Step 3 — Online Grievance: 
●​ pmjay.gov.in → Grievance section 
●​ File a complaint against the hospital by name 
Step 4 — SHA UP: 
●​ Contact State Health Agency UP 
●​ District-level SHA representatives can be reached through CMO office 
Step 5 — CMO Office: 
●​ Visit or call the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of the district 
●​ File a written complaint 
 
Escalation Path 
Hospital Arogya Mitra → SHA UP Helpline (14555) → SHA UP Grievance Portal → CMO 
Office → State Health Department UP → NHA Grievance Portal

When Pre-Authorization is Required

Pre-authorization (prior approval) is required for: 
●​ Planned / elective surgeries and procedures (non-emergency) 
●​ High-cost packages that require specific approval before treatment 
●​ Certain specialty packages as defined by NHA/SHA UP 
Pre-authorization is generally NOT required for: 
●​ Emergency cases (treatment can proceed; authorization may be post-facto) 
●​ Packages that are pre-approved for direct treatment 
 
Hospital Responsibilities in Pre-Authorization 
The hospital's responsibility (not the beneficiary's) to: 
1.​ Submit pre-authorization request through the PM-JAY portal/system 
2.​ Provide required clinical information (diagnosis, proposed treatment, supporting 
documents) 
3.​ Wait for authorization or take appropriate action if rejected 
4.​ Inform the patient of the status 
The beneficiary should NOT need to personally file a pre-authorization. This is entirely a 
hospital-side process. 
 
Authorization Timeline 
●​ Standard pre-authorization is typically processed within a few hours to 1 working day 
●​ Emergency authorizations are processed on priority / post-treatment 
●​ Complex cases may take longer 
 
Pending Authorization 
If the authorization is taking too long: 
●​ The Arogya Mitra should follow up with the SHA/insurance company 
●​ Beneficiary can call 14555 to check status if they feel the delay is undue 
●​ Emergency treatment should not be held waiting for authorization 
 
Authorization Rejection

If pre-authorization is rejected: 
●​ Hospital should inform the patient with the reason 
●​ Possible reasons: Package not covered, hospital not empanelled for that package, 
eligibility issue, insufficient clinical information 
●​ Beneficiary can ask: "Why was the authorization rejected?" and request the written 
reason 
●​ If the rejection seems incorrect, the hospital should appeal or the beneficiary can call 
14555 
 
Beneficiary Guidance on Pre-Authorization 
●​ Beneficiaries should know that pre-authorization is the hospital's job 
●​ If a hospital says "authorization has not come" and asks the patient to pay → this is 
suspicious 
●​ A patient should NOT be made to pay for a covered package pending authorization 
for an emergency 
●​ For planned procedures, if authorization is taking time, the beneficiary can ask the 
Arogya Mitra to follow up

Cashless Nature — Beneficiary Does Not File Claims 
Under PM-JAY, the beneficiary is not required to file a claim. The scheme is designed to be 
fully cashless: 
●​ The hospital files the claim directly with the SHA UP / insurance company 
●​ The beneficiary receives treatment without paying (for covered packages) 
●​ Payment flows from government/insurer to hospital — not through the beneficiary

●​ If a beneficiary pays out of pocket for a covered package and then tries to claim 
reimbursement, this is an exceptional process (see below) 
 
How the Hospital Claim Works (For Context) 
1.​ Hospital provides treatment to PM-JAY beneficiary 
2.​ Hospital submits claim with all required documents through PM-JAY system 
3.​ SHA UP or insurance company verifies the claim 
4.​ Claim is approved and payment is made to the hospital 
5.​ This process is entirely between hospital and SHA — beneficiary is not involved 
 
Why Beneficiaries Normally Don't File Claims 
●​ The system is designed for cashless, not reimbursement 
●​ Beneficiaries visiting empanelled hospitals and using the PM-JAY process should not 
pay → no need for reimbursement 
●​ Any payment by the beneficiary for a covered package is an anomaly to be reported 
as a grievance 
 
When Might Reimbursement Be Needed? 
If a beneficiary paid out of pocket at an empanelled hospital for a covered package (which 
should not have happened): 
●​ This is an improper charging situation 
●​ The beneficiary should file a grievance with SHA UP / NHA helpline (14555) 
●​ Reimbursement processes, where available, would be decided by SHA UP on a 
case-by-case basis 
●​ Contact 14555 or SHA UP immediately if you paid money for what should have been 
a cashless PM-JAY treatment 
 
Emergency Treatment Claims 
For emergency treatment: 
●​ Treatment proceeds without waiting for formal authorization 
●​ Hospital files a post-treatment claim

●​ The beneficiary should ensure their PM-JAY details (Aadhaar/PM-JAY ID) are 
provided to the hospital at the earliest possible opportunity for linking the treatment to 
their account

DOCUMENT 17: Fraudulent Ayushman Charges / PM-JAY Fraud 
 
Document ID: HP-UP-017​

Government Level: Central + State​

Current Status: Active​
Last Verified Date: June 2025 
 
Types of PM-JAY Fraud Reported 
1. Fake Treatment Entries (Ghost Treatments) 
●​ Hospital shows treatment in the PM-JAY system for a procedure the patient never 
actually received 
●​ Patient's Ayushman coverage is used without their knowledge 
●​ This reduces the ₹5 lakh annual limit without any benefit to the patient 
2. Package Upcoding 
●​ Hospital performs a minor procedure but claims for a more expensive package 
●​ Patient's coverage is depleted faster 
3. Hospital Shows Admission Without Actual Admission 
●​ Patient was treated as OPD but the hospital records it as inpatient admission in 
PM-JAY system 
4. Misuse of Beneficiary Identity/Card 
●​ Someone else uses a beneficiary's Aadhaar/PM-JAY card for treatment (identity 
theft) 
●​ Beneficiary's annual limit gets consumed by a different person 
5. Fake Ayushman Cards 
●​ Fraudsters create counterfeit Ayushman cards claiming benefits 
●​ These are detected during hospital verification but may be used for minor fraud 
 
Warning Signs for Beneficiaries 
●​ You receive a message that your PM-JAY treatment has been completed but you 
were never treated 
●​ An Arogya Mitra or hospital staff asks you to "cooperate" for registration without 
actual treatment

●​ Someone asks for your Aadhaar and OTP outside of legitimate card generation or 
hospital verification 
 
Complaint Procedures 
For Fraudulent Hospital Treatment Entries: 
1.​ Call 14555 / 1800-111-565 
2.​ File grievance on pmjay.gov.in 
3.​ Contact SHA UP with details 
4.​ Local police complaint for criminal fraud 
For Identity Misuse / Card Misuse: 
1.​ Call 14555 immediately 
2.​ File complaint with SHA UP 
3.​ File FIR at local police station 
4.​ Request that your PM-JAY account be secured/locked pending investigation 
For Fake Ayushman Cards: 
1.​ Report to 14555 and SHA UP 
2.​ File police complaint 
 
Fraud Awareness — Key Points 
●​ Never share your Aadhaar OTP with anyone except during legitimate e-KYC at CSC 
or hospital Ayushman Help Desk 
●​ No one should call you asking for OTP to "generate" or "update" your Ayushman card 
— this is a scam 
●​ Agents demanding fees to help get PM-JAY coverage or card are fraudulent — 
PM-JAY services are free 
●​ Fake websites may mimic pmjay.gov.in — always use the official URL 
●​ You can check your PM-JAY treatment history on the official portal to detect any 
unauthorized entries

What Should an Ayushman Beneficiary Do in an Emergency? 
Immediate Priority: Get Medical Help First 
In a life-threatening emergency, the first priority is accessing emergency medical care — not 
paperwork or PM-JAY processes. 
1.​ Call 108 (Ambulance service in UP) for emergency transport 
2.​ Go to the nearest hospital with emergency services immediately 
3.​ PM-JAY verification can be completed after the patient is stabilized 
 
PM-JAY in Emergencies at Empanelled Hospitals 
If the emergency patient reaches an empanelled hospital: 
●​ Emergency treatment should begin immediately 
●​ Pre-authorization is NOT required before emergency treatment 
●​ PM-JAY identity verification can be completed after the patient is stable 
●​ The hospital can process post-treatment documentation 
Key rule: Empanelled hospitals cannot deny emergency treatment pending PM-JAY 
authorization.

What if the Nearest Hospital is NOT an Empanelled Hospital? 
●​ If the only available hospital in an emergency is not PM-JAY empanelled → go there 
for emergency treatment 
●​ PM-JAY cashless benefit may not apply at a non-empanelled hospital 
●​ After stabilization, the patient can be transferred to an empanelled hospital if needed 
●​ Contact SHA UP helpline (14555) about any reimbursement possibility for 
emergency treatment at non-empanelled facilities — this is an exceptional situation 
governed by specific provisions that should be verified with SHA UP 
 
Finding an Empanelled Hospital for Non-Emergency Cases 
For non-emergency situations, the beneficiary should: 
1.​ Check the PM-JAY portal (pmjay.gov.in → Find Hospital) for empanelled hospitals in 
their district 
2.​ Identify one that offers the required specialty/package 
3.​ Visit with Aadhaar and proceed through the Ayushman Help Desk 
 
Understanding Scheme Limitations in Emergencies 
●​ PM-JAY covers hospitalization only — not emergency OPD consultation alone 
●​ If an emergency requires admission → PM-JAY coverage applies at empanelled 
hospitals 
●​ If an emergency only needed OPD treatment (no admission) → PM-JAY may not 
cover the OPD cost 
●​ Emergency ambulance (108 service) is a separate government service — not 
PM-JAY funded

●​ All women (general) for deliveries at government health facilities (rural and urban)

Registering pregnancy with the government health system is important because it: 
●​ Connects the pregnant woman to ANC services 
●​ Creates the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card 
●​ Enables eligibility verification for JSY and PMMVY benefits 
●​ Ensures ASHA and ANM follow-up during pregnancy

●​ Helps identify high-risk pregnancies early

●​ Primary Health Centre (PHC) — at OPD or MCH department 
●​ Community Health Centre (CHC) — if PHC is not accessible 
●​ Anganwadi Centre — for PMMVY registration (connects to the health system)

●​ As soon as pregnancy is confirmed — first trimester registration is strongly 
recommended 
●​ For PMMVY 1st installment, registration must be within prescribed period (before 
certain weeks of pregnancy) — verify current rules with ANM

Important RAG distinction 
For Uttar Pradesh (UP), India, tag documents by government level: 
●​ UP Government: UP-specific family/citizen records and welfare-service integrations. 
●​ Central Government applicable in UP: Aadhaar, PAN and many election-related 
systems. 
●​ UP implementation: where a Central identity/document system interacts with an UP 
Government benefit. 
Do not label Aadhaar, PAN or Election Commission services as Uttar Pradesh Government 
schemes merely because the user lives in UP. 
For every document, use: 
Document/Service Name → Government Level → Authority → Applicability in Uttar 
Pradesh → Purpose → Eligibility → Required Documents → Application/Enrolment → 
Verification → Fees → Processing → Download/Retrieval → Update/Correction → 
Linking → Status → Rejection → Lost Document → Special Cases → Grievance → 
Fraud/Safety → Related UP Schemes → FAQs → Official Source → Effective Date → 
Last Verified Date.

And this category will be especially useful for SetuAI because a lot of apparent “scheme 
problems” are actually document mismatch problems. If your RAG can connect a failed 
scholarship/pension/PM-KISAN application to the correct underlying identity record, it 
becomes much more useful than a chatbot that merely lists schemes.

For every Business / Self-Employment / Loan — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India record, use: 
Scheme Name → Government Level → UP Implementing Authority → Active/Historical 
Status → Target Entrepreneur → Business Type → New/Existing Business → Age → 
Income/Category Conditions → Education/Training → Project-Cost Limit → Loan Limit 
→ Beneficiary Contribution → Subsidy/Margin Money/Interest Support → 
Collateral/Guarantee → Documents → Registration → Application → Department 
Verification → Bank Appraisal → Sanction → Training → Disbursement → Repayment 
→ Subsidy Adjustment → Status → Correction → Rejection → Grievance → District 
Availability → FAQs → Official Source → Government Order/Guidelines → Effective 
From → Effective To → Last Verified. 
For this domain, keep “eligible for a scheme” and “guaranteed to receive a loan” 
completely separate. A government scheme may make someone eligible to apply, while

Service/Record Name → Government Level → UP Department/Authority →

Appeal/Grievance → Special Cases → Related Farmer/Housing/Utility Services →

For this category, SetuAI should maintain one critical boundary: 
Bhulekh/Khatauni/mutation entries are revenue records, while questions about final 
legal title, inheritance shares, disputed ownership or competing claims can require 
the competent revenue/civil authority or legal determination. Your chatbot can explain 
the procedure and records, but should not invent an ownership verdict from RAG data alone.

indexed. Otherwise queries like “property mutation” can retrieve the wrong procedure for 
Uttar Pradesh (UP), India.

User problem → Service → Government level → Responsible authority → Correct 
grievance mechanism → Complaint draft → Evidence → Status tracking → Escalation

users a Jansunwai link for every problem.

36. Most Important Rule 
SetuAI should never convert a profile match into a guarantee. 
Don't say: 
“You will receive this scheme.” 
Prefer: 
“Based on the information provided, you appear to match these eligibility 
conditions. Final eligibility and approval are determined by the 
responsible government authority after verification.” 
Also distinguish: 
Profile Match ≠ Eligibility Confirmation ≠ Application Approval ≠ Benefit Payment 
That distinction is extremely important for a government-welfare assistant. 
And architecturally, this is the module that can connect everything you've been building: 
Scheme Discovery → Explainable Eligibility → Documents → Application → RAG 
Guidance → Status → Grievance → Alternative Schemes. 
That can become the central flow of SetuAI for Uttar Pradesh (UP), India, rather than 
SetuAI being only a scheme-information chatbot.

**Wage Structure**: 
- Daily wage as per UP state notification 
- Payment through bank/post office account via DBT 
- Equal wages for men and women 
 
**Payment Timeline**: Wages paid within 15 days of work completion 
 
**Grievance System**: 
- Gram Panchayat level complaints

- Social audit process

Title: Old Age Pension Scheme (Vriddhavastha Pension) 
 
Category: Pension & Social Welfare 
 
Government Level: State Government 
 
Responsible Department: Department of Social Welfare, Government of Uttar 
Pradesh 
 
Applicable State: Uttar Pradesh 
 
Purpose: To provide monthly financial assistance to eligible senior citizens with 
limited income. 
 
Who It Is For: Elderly residents of Uttar Pradesh belonging to economically weaker 
families. 
 
Eligibility: Must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh, meet the prescribed age 
criteria, and satisfy the income requirements. The applicant should not be receiving 
another government pension of the same type. 
 
Income Limit: As notified by the Government of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
Age Requirement: As prescribed under the current scheme guidelines. 
 
Category Requirement: Open to eligible senior citizens irrespective of caste, subject 
to scheme rules. 
 
Residence Requirement: Permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh.

Benefits / Entitlement: Monthly pension transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank 
account. 
 
Required Documents: Aadhaar Card, residence proof, income certificate, age proof, 
bank passbook, passport-size photograph, mobile number. 
 
How to Apply: Apply online through the Uttar Pradesh Social Welfare Department 
portal or visit a Common Service Centre (CSC). 
 
Online / Offline Process: Fill out the application form, upload or submit the required 
documents, and submit the application. 
 
Verification Process: Verification is carried out by local authorities before approval. 
 
Application Status: Can be checked online using the application number. 
 
Correction / Update: Personal details, bank account information, or Aadhaar details 
can be corrected through the official portal or CSC. 
 
Renewal: Renewal may be required if specified by the department. 
 
Payment / DBT: Pension is paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the 
registered bank account. 
 
Common Rejection Reasons: Incomplete documents, Aadhaar mismatch, incorrect 
bank details, income exceeding eligibility limits, duplicate pension benefits. 
 
Common Problems: Payment delayed, application pending verification, bank account 
not linked with Aadhaar, rejected application. 
 
Grievance Process: Contact the District Social Welfare Office or register a complaint 
through UP Jansunwai (IGRS). 
 
Official Portal / Source: Uttar Pradesh Social Welfare Department Portal 
 
Last Verified: July 2026

1. Ration & Food Security — Uttar Pradesh (UP), India 
Responsible Department: Department of Food and Civil Supplies, Government of Uttar 
Pradesh. UP's NFSA system includes Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) and Priority 
Household (PHH) ration cards. (National Food Security Act) 
Ration Card 
A ration card identifies an eligible household for receiving food-security benefits through the 
Public Distribution System (PDS). Identification of NFSA beneficiaries and issuance of 
AAY/PHH ration cards is handled by the respective State Government; therefore, Uttar 
Pradesh residents must follow the UP Government's ration-card system and eligibility rules. 
(National Food Security Act) 
NFSA Categories 
Priority Household (PHH): An eligible PHH beneficiary is entitled under NFSA to 5 kg of 
foodgrains per person per month. 
Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY): AAY targets eligible households identified under the 
applicable criteria. Under NFSA, an AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per 
household per month. (National Food Security Act) 
The actual commodity distribution arrangements and applicable government policy should 
always be checked against the current UP/NFSA records. 
New Ration Card

A person who needs a new ration card in Uttar Pradesh should use the application 
procedure specified by the UP Food and Civil Supplies system. NFSA itself states that 
beneficiary identification and ration-card issuance are the responsibility of the State 
Government/UT Administration. (National Food Security Act) 
Typical processing involves: 
Application → household information → supporting documents → verification → eligibility 
determination → ration-card issuance. 
SetuAI should not guarantee approval merely because a user appears to satisfy basic 
conditions. 
Household Members 
Ration-card records may require citizen services such as: 
●​ Addition of a family member 
●​ Removal of a family member 
●​ Addition after birth 
●​ Removal after death 
●​ Changes after marriage 
●​ Correction of member name/details 
●​ Updating household information 
Exact documents and processing requirements should be retrieved from current UP rules for 
the requested service rather than assumed. 
Aadhaar / e-KYC 
Aadhaar-linked identification and authentication may be used within the PDS ecosystem. 
SetuAI should distinguish among: 
Aadhaar seeding → associating Aadhaar information with the beneficiary record. 
e-KYC → identity/details verification through the applicable system. 
Biometric authentication → authentication that may occur during PDS transactions. 
A failure in one process should not automatically be interpreted by SetuAI as cancellation or 
ineligibility. 
One Nation One Ration Card 
One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) enables eligible NFSA beneficiaries to access their 
foodgrain entitlement through portability, including from FPS locations outside their home 
area according to the system's applicable rules. (National Food Security Act) 
This is especially relevant for migrant beneficiaries.

Fair Price Shop / Kotedar 
A Fair Price Shop (FPS), commonly called a ration shop/Kotedar in UP, distributes PDS 
commodities to beneficiaries. 
Useful SetuAI questions include: 
●​ Which FPS is linked to my ration card? 
●​ Where is my nearest FPS? 
●​ How much ration am I entitled to? 
●​ Why did my transaction fail? 
●​ What should I do if the dealer gives less ration? 
●​ Where can I complain about an FPS? 
The Mera Ration system also supports functions including viewing ration-card details, 
entitlement information, transaction history and locating nearby FPSs. (National Food 
Security Act) 
Portability 
A beneficiary temporarily living away from their registered location may need portability 
rather than creation of another ration card. 
SetuAI should therefore ask: 
“Do you want to permanently change your household record, or do you only 
need ration while staying somewhere else?” 
This prevents confusing address modification with ONORC portability. 
Lost Ration Card 
If a physical ration-card document is lost, SetuAI should first determine whether the user 
needs: 
●​ ration-card details, 
●​ an available digital record, 
●​ a replacement/duplicate document, or 
●​ correction of the underlying beneficiary record. 
A lost physical document does not by itself mean that the underlying NFSA beneficiary 
record has disappeared. 
Ration Entitlement 
SetuAI should retrieve entitlement using: 
Card category + household/member information + current applicable 
allocation/distribution policy.

It should not use a single hard-coded ration quantity for every beneficiary. 
Grievances 
Possible ration grievances include: 
Dealer provides less ration → distribution complaint​
Dealer refuses applicable entitlement → FPS/PDS complaint​
Wrong household details → ration-card correction route​
Application pending → application/status grievance​
Authentication problem → PDS authentication/service issue​
Portability problem → ONORC/PDS support 
The NFSA framework includes grievance-redressal mechanisms, and the current NFSA UP 
page identifies a UP PDS grievance system. (National Food Security Act) 
Important RAG Questions

What is a PHH ration card? 
What is an AAY ration card? 
How much ration can I receive? 
How do I add a child to my ration card? 
How do I remove a deceased family member? 
How do I correct my name? 
How do I update my address? 
How do I complete ration-card e-KYC? 
How do I link Aadhaar? 
Why is biometric authentication failing? 
Can I receive ration outside Uttar Pradesh? 
What is ONORC? 
How do I find my FPS? 
What should I do if my Kotedar gives less ration? 
My ration card is missing. What should I do? 
How can I check my ration-card details? 
Where can I complain about ration distribution?

information. 
 
2. Certificates & Revenue Services — 
Uttar Pradesh (UP), India

The Uttar Pradesh Board of Revenue provides citizen-facing access for important revenue 
certificates. Its official system specifically lists Income Certificate, Caste Certificate and 
Residence Certificate, including application and certified-copy services. (Bureau of 
Rehabilitation) 
The UP Revenue Department administers issuance of Income, Caste, Domicile and 
Solvency certificates through the e-District system. (Bureau of Rehabilitation) 
Income Certificate 
An Income Certificate is an official certificate used to establish income according to the 
applicable UP Government procedure. 
It may be required for services such as: 
●​ scholarships, 
●​ fee reimbursement, 
●​ welfare benefits, 
●​ income-based eligibility, 
●​ certain reservation/benefit processes, 
●​ other government services requiring proof of income. 
Typical SetuAI Flow 
User needs Income Certificate 
 ↓ 
Identify purpose 
 ↓ 
Explain UP application channel 
 ↓ 
Show current required documents 
 ↓ 
Application 
 ↓ 
Revenue verification 
 ↓ 
Certificate issued/rejected 
 ↓ 
Status / certified copy / correction 
 
SetuAI should retrieve the current document requirements and validity requirement for 
the user's specific purpose instead of assuming one universal validity period. 
Caste Certificate 
The UP caste-certificate service provides official certification of the applicant's applicable 
social category according to government rules.

SetuAI should cover: 
●​ application, 
●​ required supporting evidence, 
●​ verification, 
●​ application status, 
●​ certificate retrieval, 
●​ certified copy, 
●​ incorrect information, 
●​ rejection, 
●​ reapplication/correction where applicable. 
A chatbot must never infer someone's caste from surname, appearance, locality or 
family name. It should only explain official certification procedures based on information 
voluntarily provided for the service. 
Residence / Domicile Certificate 
UP's revenue system provides a Residence Certificate service. (Bureau of Rehabilitation) 
It can be relevant when an institution, recruitment process, scholarship or government 
programme requires proof that an applicant satisfies its residence/domicile conditions. 
SetuAI should distinguish: 
Current address ≠ automatically domicile/residence eligibility for every government 
benefit. 
The requirements of the particular certificate or scheme must be checked. 
EWS Certificate 
SetuAI should treat an EWS certificate separately from an ordinary Income Certificate. 
A user asking: 
“I have an income certificate, can I use it as EWS?” 
should not automatically receive “yes.” 
EWS eligibility/certification can involve additional applicable conditions and documentation 
beyond merely stating annual income. 
Birth Certificate 
Birth registration/certificate guidance should cover: 
●​ new birth registration,

●​ obtaining a birth certificate, 
●​ delayed registration, 
●​ name-related updates, 
●​ incorrect DOB/details, 
●​ duplicate/certified copy, 
●​ status, 
●​ responsible local registration authority. 
Because birth/death registration may involve the relevant local registrar/local body rather 
than the same revenue workflow as Income/Caste/Residence certificates, SetuAI should not 
merge all certificates into one process. 
Death Certificate 
Coverage should include: 
●​ death registration, 
●​ obtaining the certificate, 
●​ delayed registration, 
●​ correction, 
●​ additional/certified copies, 
●​ status, 
●​ appropriate registration authority. 
Death certificates may then connect with other SetuAI modules: 
Death Certificate 
 ↓ 
Ration member deletion 
 ↓ 
Pension/welfare updates 
 ↓ 
Land inheritance/mutation 
 ↓ 
Bank/DBT record changes 
 
Certificate Status 
SetuAI should understand queries such as: 
My income certificate is pending. 
My caste certificate was rejected. 
My residence certificate is under verification. 
Where can I check my certificate? 
How can I download the certified copy?

It should first identify: 
Certificate type → application/reference details → issuing system → current status 
mechanism → appropriate grievance/escalation. 
Certificate Correction 
Possible correction queries include: 
●​ incorrect name, 
●​ spelling error, 
●​ incorrect parent's details, 
●​ incorrect address, 
●​ incorrect income details, 
●​ incorrect category details, 
●​ DOB mismatch, 
●​ certificate/application data mismatch. 
SetuAI should not tell users to simply edit an issued official certificate. It should explain the 
applicable official correction/reissue process. 
Certificate Validity 
Avoid putting one global rule in the RAG such as: 
“Income certificate is always valid for X months.” 
Instead store: 
Certificate 
Purpose 
Issuing Authority 
Issue Date 
Validity Rule 
Scheme/Institution Requirement 
Official Source 
Last Verified 
 
A certificate may be technically valid under one rule while a particular application demands a 
recently issued certificate. 
Revenue Services Integration 
The UP Board of Revenue also links citizen services involving Bhulekh/Khatauni, Khasra, 
Bhu-Naksha, inheritance and mutation, so SetuAI can connect certificate questions with

the Land & Property corpus rather than duplicating all land knowledge here. (Bureau of 
Rehabilitation)

Rejection Category 1: Aadhaar-Related 
1.1 Name Mismatch

Impact: Application rejected at submission or verification stage 
Resolution: 
1.​ Correct Aadhaar: Visit Aadhaar center → Update name → Receive updated 
Aadhaar (15 days) 
2.​ Or correct Class 10 certificate: Contact Board → Name correction → Reprint 
certificate (30-60 days; difficult) 
3.​ Preferred: Correct Aadhaar to match Class 10 
Steps: 
●​ Download Aadhaar correction form from uidai.gov.in

●​ Visit Aadhaar Enrollment Center with Class 10 marksheet as proof 
●​ Pay fee (₹50) 
●​ Receive acknowledgment slip 
●​ Updated Aadhaar in 15-30 days 
●​ Download e-Aadhaar 
●​ Reapply for scholarship during correction window 
Prevention: Before applying scholarship, verify name matches exactly across 
Aadhaar, Class 10, and bank account

START: Scholarship Payment Not Received

Q1: Check Scholarship Portal Status

Q2: Status "Sanctioned" (Payment Pending) 
 → Payment file not yet generated 
 → Timeline: 15-30 days after sanction 
 → Action: Wait; check portal weekly 
 → If > 45 days: Contact District Welfare Office 
 → Provide: Application number, Sanction letter (if available) 
 
Q3: Status "Payment Sent" (Not Credited to Bank) 
 ↓

 ↓

 Q3b: Verify Bank Account Details on Application 
 ↓ 
 ├─ Account number wrong → Go to Solution A 
 ├─ IFSC wrong → Go to Solution B 
 ├─ Account holder name mismatch → Go to Solution C 
 ├─ Account closed/dormant → Go to Solution D 
 └─ All details correct → Go to Q3c 
 
 Q3c: Payment Failed at PFMS/Bank Level 
 → Check PFMS status (if PFMS reference number available) 
 → Contact District Welfare Office 
 → Request PFMS tracking number

 → Resolution: Update details, request reprocessing 
 
Q4: Status "Payment Credited" (Student Claims Not Received) 
 → Payment actually credited; check thoroughly 
 ↓ 
 Action: 
 1. Check bank passbook (visit branch, print passbook) 
 2. Check online banking/mobile app (transaction history) 
 3. Payment may be in another account (if student has multiple accounts) 
 4. Check account number on scholarship application vs actual account 
 5. If genuinely not credited: Bank issue → Visit branch with scholarship portal 
screenshot showing "Payment Credited" + application number 
 
Q5: Status "Payment Failed" 
 → Check failure reason on portal 
 ↓ 
 Common Reasons: 
 ├─ "Aadhaar not seeded with bank account" → Link Aadhaar at bank; request reprocessing 
 ├─ "Account number invalid" → Correct account number during correction window or submit 
written request to District Office 
 ├─ "IFSC not matching" → Correct IFSC 
 ├─ "Account closed" → Open new account, update details

├─ "Beneficiary name mismatch" → Account not in student's name; open account in own 
name 
 └─ "Other bank rejection" → Visit bank to resolve issue; get bank certificate stating 
issue resolved; submit to District Office 
 
Q6: Pending at Institution 
 → Payment cannot proceed until institution verifies 
 ↓ 
 Action: 
 1. Contact College Nodal Officer 
 2. Ask status: Why pending? 
 3. Common causes: 
 - College hasn't logged in to verify 
 - College rejected (check remarks) 
 - College waiting for some document/clarification 
 4. Provide required documents to college 
 5. Follow up weekly 
 6. If college unresponsive > 30 days: Complain to District Welfare Office 
 
Q7: Pending at District 
 → Institution verified; now district verification pending 
 ↓ 
 Action: 
 1. Visit District Welfare Office (in-person or call) 
 2. Provide application number 
 3. Ask verification status 
 4. Common delays: 
 - High volume of applications 
 - Certificate verification pending with Tehsil 
 - Duplicate check in progress 
 5. If > 45 days at district: Escalate to State Scholarship Cell

●​ Correct account number 
●​ Attach: Bank passbook copy, Aadhaar card, Application printout

●​ Submit in person or via registered post 
●​ Follow up after 7 days 
3.​ After Sanction (Payment Pending): 
●​ Urgent correction needed 
●​ Visit District Office in person 
●​ Carry: All documents + Sanction letter (if issued) 
●​ Request manual correction before payment file generated

PFMS Payment Tracking 
What is PFMS?​
Public Financial Management System — Central government payment platform 
When Used: 
●​ For Central scholarships (NSP) 
●​ Sometimes for State scholarships (if state uses PFMS) 
How to Track: 
1.​ Get PFMS Reference Number: 
●​ Shown on scholarship portal (if integrated) 
●​ Or ask District Welfare Office 
2.​ Track on PFMS: 
●​ Visit pfms.nic.in 
●​ Click "Know Your Payment" 
●​ Enter: Bank account number, PFMS reference/scroll number 
●​ View payment status 
3.​ PFMS Status Meanings: 
●​ Payment Initiated: File sent to bank 
●​ Payment In Process: Bank processing 
●​ Payment Success: Credited to account 
●​ Payment Failed: Bank rejected (see reason)

4.​ If PFMS Shows Success but Bank Account Not Credited: 
●​ Visit bank with PFMS transaction reference 
●​ Bank will reconcile 
●​ Payment usually appears within 24-48 hours after PFMS success

Category: Eligibility 
Q1 (EN): Who is eligible for UP scholarship?​
Q1 (HI): UP scholarship के लिए कौन eligible है?​
A1: Students belonging to SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Minority, or 
economically weaker General category, who are domiciled in Uttar Pradesh, studying 
in recognized institutions, and whose annual family income is within prescribed limits 
(₹2,50,000 for SC/ST, ₹2,00,000 for OBC/Minority, ₹1,00,000 for General) are 
eligible for UP scholarship. 
 
Q2 (EN): What is the income limit for SC scholarship?​
Q2 (Hinglish): SC scholarship ke liye income limit kya hai?​
A2: ₹2,50,000 per annum (as of 2024-25). The income certificate should cover all 
family income sources and be issued by Tehsildar/SDM.

Q3 (EN): Can a student from Bihar studying in UP get UP scholarship?​
A3: No. UP scholarship requires the student to be a domicile/resident of Uttar 
Pradesh. A Bihar domicile student studying in UP should apply for Bihar state 
scholarship, not UP. 
 
Category: Application Process 
Q4 (EN): How to apply for UP scholarship?​
Q4 (Hinglish): UP scholarship ke liye apply kaise kare?​
A4: Visit scholarship.up.gov.in → Select your category (SC/ST/OBC/Minority) → 
Click 'New Registration' (for fresh) → Fill personal, academic, category, income, 
bank details → Upload documents (photo, Aadhaar, marksheet, certificates, fee 
receipt, bank passbook) → Submit → Take printout → Submit hard copy to college 
within deadline. 
 
Q5 (EN): What documents are needed for scholarship application?​
A5: Photograph, Aadhaar card, Class 10 marksheet (or highest qualification 
marksheet), current year admission receipt, fee receipt, caste certificate 
(SC/ST/OBC), income certificate, domicile certificate, bank passbook/statement. All 
in PDF/JPG format, within size limits. 
 
Q6 (EN): What is the last date to apply for scholarship in UP?​
A6: The last date varies each year. For 2024-25 (example), student application 
deadline is typically October 31. Check scholarship.up.gov.in for current year 
notification. Institution verification deadline is usually 30 days after student deadline. 
 
Category: Renewal 
Q7 (EN): I got scholarship last year. Do I need to apply again?​
Q7 (Hinglish): Last year scholarship mili thi, kya fir se apply karna hoga?​
A7: Yes, you need to apply every year, but as 'Renewal' (not fresh). Login with your 
previous registration number, update current year details (year/semester, marks, fee 
receipt, new income certificate), and submit. Renewal is simpler as most data is 
pre-filled. 
 
Q8 (EN): I am in BA 1st year now; I got scholarship in Class 12. Is this renewal or 
fresh?​
A8: This is 'Fresh' application because you moved from Intermediate level to

Undergraduate level. Renewal is only within the same course level (e.g., BA 1st year 
to BA 2nd year). 
 
Q9 (EN): I failed last year. Can I renew scholarship?​
A9: No. If you were detained/failed and not promoted to the next year, you cannot 
renew scholarship until you pass and get promoted. After promotion, apply fresh. 
 
Category: Payment 
Q10 (EN): When will I receive scholarship money?​
Q10 (Hinglish): Scholarship ka paisa kab aayega?​
A10: After your application is verified by institution and district, sanctioned by the 
department, and payment file is processed, scholarship is credited to your 
Aadhaar-linked bank account via DBT. Typical timeline: 60-120 days after application 
submission. Check portal for payment status. 
 
Q11 (EN): Scholarship approved but money not received. What to do?​
Q11 (Hinglish): Scholarship approve ho gayi hai par paisa nahi aaya, kya kare?​
A11: Check payment status on portal. If 'Payment Sent' but not credited: Verify your 
bank account number, IFSC, and Aadhaar linking on application. Visit bank to 
confirm account is active. If all correct, contact District Welfare Office with application 
number and request payment tracking. 
 
Q12 (EN): How much scholarship will I get for B.Tech?​
A12: For B.Tech in UP (2024-25 example): Maintenance allowance 
₹10,000-12,000/year (day scholar) or ₹20,000-24,000/year (hosteller). Fee 
reimbursement: Full fee in government colleges; up to ₹80,000-1,00,000/year in 
private colleges (for SC/ST; limits vary by category). Verify current year amounts 
from official notification. 
 
Category: Documents 
Q13 (EN): My Aadhaar name and Class 10 name are different. What to do?​
Q13 (Hinglish): Aadhaar aur Class 10 me naam alag hai, kya kare?​
A13: You must correct the name mismatch. Preferred: Correct Aadhaar name to 
match Class 10 (visit Aadhaar center with Class 10 marksheet, pay ₹50, updated 
Aadhaar in 15-30 days). Or correct Class 10 name via Board (longer process). After 
correction, apply/reapply for scholarship.

Q14 (EN): How to get caste certificate?​
A14: Visit Tehsil office with required documents (parents' caste certificate if available, 
Aadhaar, birth certificate, school records). Fill caste certificate application form. 
Submit with documents. Tehsildar verifies and issues certificate (7-15 days). Or 
apply online via Jansunwai portal (if available in your district). 
 
Q15 (EN): My income certificate expired. Can I still use it?​
A15: No. Income certificate is valid for 1 year (one financial year). If expired, you 
must renew it before applying for scholarship. Visit Tehsildar/SDM to get a fresh 
income certificate for the current financial year. 
 
Category: Bank & DBT 
Q16 (EN): Can I use my father's bank account for scholarship?​
Q16 (Hinglish): Scholarship ke liye papa ka bank account use kar sakte hain?​
A16: No. Scholarship must be credited to the student's own bank account (in 
student's name, Aadhaar-linked). You must open a bank account in your name and 
use that for scholarship application. 
 
Q17 (EN): How to link Aadhaar with bank account?​
A17: Visit your bank branch with Aadhaar card. Fill Aadhaar seeding form (available 
at branch). Bank will update Aadhaar in your account within 1-3 days. Verify by 
checking passbook or asking bank staff for confirmation. 
 
Q18 (EN): What is IFSC code and where to find it?​
A18: IFSC (Indian Financial System Code) is an 11-character code identifying your 
bank branch. Find it on: Bank passbook (first page), Bank statement, Cheque leaf, or 
search online at bankifsccode.com by entering bank name and branch. 
 
Category: Rejection & Errors 
Q19 (EN): Why was my application rejected?​
Q19 (Hinglish): Mera application reject kyu hua?​
A19: Login to scholarship portal and check 'Application Status' → 'Rejection 
Remarks'. Common reasons: Aadhaar mismatch, invalid/expired certificates, income 
exceeds limit, duplicate application, institution verification failure, bank account

issues. Resolve the issue mentioned in remarks and reapply during correction 
window. 
 
Q20 (EN): Application rejected due to 'Aadhaar authentication failed'. What does it 
mean?​
A20: Your Aadhaar number could not be verified with UIDAI database. Possible 
reasons: Aadhaar number entered wrong, or Aadhaar demographic details 
(name/DOB/gender) do not match application. Verify Aadhaar number, correct any 
mismatch, and resubmit. 
 
Q21 (EN): Can I correct my application after final submission?​
Q21 (Hinglish): Final submit ke baad application correct kar sakte hain?​
A21: After final submission, most fields are locked. However, a 'Correction Window' 
(usually in November-December for 15 days) is provided where you can edit certain 
fields and upload fresh documents. If correction window is closed, submit a written 
request to District Welfare Office for critical corrections (like bank account). 
 
Category: Grievance 
Q22 (EN): My college is not verifying my application. What to do?​
Q22 (Hinglish): College verify nahi kar raha, kya kare?​
A22: First, contact your college nodal officer and ask reason for delay. If they are 
asking for some documents, submit them. If they are unresponsive for more than 30 
days, file a grievance with District Welfare Office. Provide application number and 
explain the delay. 
 
Q23 (EN): How to file a complaint about scholarship?​
A23: Level 1: College nodal officer. Level 2: District Welfare Office (visit in person or 
call). Level 3: State Scholarship Cell helpline/email (check portal). Level 4: Online 
grievance on scholarship.up.gov.in. Level 5: CM Helpline 1076 or 
samadhan.up.gov.in. 
 
Q24 (EN): What is the scholarship helpline number?​
A24: Helpline numbers vary by department and category. Check 
scholarship.up.gov.in → Contact/Help section for current helpline. For SC/ST: Social 
Welfare Department helpline. For OBC: Backward Class Welfare Department 
helpline. Or contact District Welfare Office directly.

Category: Institution & Courses 
Q25 (EN): My college is not showing in the institution dropdown. What to do?​
Q25 (Hinglish): Mera college dropdown me nahi aa raha, kya kare?​
A25: Your college is not registered on the scholarship portal. Ask your college 
principal/nodal officer to register the institution on scholarship.up.gov.in by submitting 
recognition documents. Until registration is complete, students cannot apply. Follow 
up with college administration. 
 
Q26 (EN): Is scholarship available for distance/open university courses?​
A26: It depends on the scheme and course. If the distance/open university course is 
UGC-recognized (like IGNOU) and the course is eligible (e.g., BA, B.Com, BCA), it is 
generally eligible. Check the specific scheme guidelines for current year or ask the 
nodal officer. 
 
Q27 (EN): Can I get scholarship for a private engineering college?​
A27: Yes, if the college is AICTE-approved and registered on the scholarship portal, 
and you meet eligibility criteria. However, fee reimbursement is subject to a 
maximum limit (e.g., ₹80,000/year for SC/ST in private engineering). If your fee is 
higher, you pay the difference. 
 
Category: Specific Scenarios 
Q28 (EN): I am an OBC student with income ₹1,80,000. Am I eligible?​
A28: Yes. OBC income limit is ₹2,00,000/year (2024-25). Your income of ₹1,80,000 
is within the limit. Ensure you have a valid OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate and 
income certificate. 
 
Q29 (EN): I belong to SC category but my family income is ₹3,00,000. Can I apply?​
A29: No. Even though you are SC, the income limit is ₹2,50,000 (2024-25). If your 
family income exceeds this, you are not eligible for SC scholarship. Check if any 
other general category or merit-based scholarship is available. 
 
Q30 (EN): I study in a madrasa. Can I get scholarship?​
A30: If the madrasa is recognized by the UP Madrasa Board or affiliated to a 
recognized university, and offers courses equivalent to regular education (e.g., 
Alim/Fazil equivalent to Class 12/Graduation), it may be eligible. Check with the 
madrasa administration and the Minority Welfare Department.

Q31 (EN): I changed my college in 2nd year. Can I renew scholarship?​
A31: Yes, you can renew if you moved within the same course level (e.g., BA 1st 
year in College A, BA 2nd year in College B). Update the new institution details in 
the renewal form. The new college will verify your application. Provide 
migration/transfer certificate if required. 
 
Q32 (EN): I am doing a 5-year integrated BA-LLB. Which scholarship category?​
A32: Apply under Post-Matric (PMOTI). For years 1-3, you may be treated as UG 
level; years 4-5 as PG level (depending on scheme rules). Check the scheme 
notification or portal instructions for integrated courses. Apply fresh in Year 1, renew 
in subsequent years. 
 
Q33 (EN): Can I get scholarship if I took admission through management quota?​
A33: Yes, as long as the institution is recognized, the course is eligible, and you 
meet category/income/domicile criteria. The admission route 
(merit/management/donation) does not affect scholarship eligibility, but the fee you 
paid must be verified by the institution. 
 
Q34 (EN): I am a girl student. Is there any additional scholarship?​
A34: Apart from the main Post-Matric scholarship, check for girl-specific schemes 
like 'Kanya Vidya Dhan' (UP), 'Balika Shiksha Protsahan', or Central schemes like 
'Pragati/Saksham' (for technical education). These have separate eligibility and 
application processes. 
 
Q35 (EN): I have a disability. What additional benefits can I get?​
Q35 (Hinglish): Mujhe disability hai, kya additional benefits milenge?​
A35: Students with 40%+ disability (certified by Medical Board) may have: Relaxed 
income limits, Higher scholarship/maintenance amount, Additional disability-specific 
scholarships like 'National Fellowship for Students with Disabilities' (Central). Upload 
Disability Certificate and UDID card with scholarship application. 
 
Category: Intermediate / Class 11-12 
Q36 (EN): I am in Class 11. Which scholarship should I apply for?​
A36: Post-Matric Intermediate Scholarship. Visit scholarship.up.gov.in, select your 
category (SC/ST/OBC/Minority), apply under 'Post-Matric (Intermediate)', fill details, 
upload Class 10 marksheet, Class 11 admission receipt, fee receipt, and other 
documents.

Q37 (EN): Can I renew scholarship from Class 11 to Class 12?​
A37: Yes. If you received scholarship in Class 11, apply as 'Renewal' for Class 12. 
Use the same registration number, update class to 12, upload Class 11 marksheet 
and Class 12 fee receipt. 
 
Category: Diploma / Polytechnic 
Q38 (EN): I am doing diploma after Class 10. Am I eligible for scholarship?​
A38: Yes. Diploma after Class 10 is covered under Post-Matric Diploma/PMOTI 
scheme (depending on scheme categorization). Ensure your polytechnic is 
AICTE-approved or State Board of Technical Education recognized, and you meet 
category/income criteria. 
 
Q39 (EN): After diploma, I entered B.Tech 2nd year (lateral entry). Do I apply fresh or 
renew?​
A39: Apply 'Fresh' for B.Tech because you changed course (from Diploma to 
B.Tech). If you received scholarship during diploma, that was under Diploma 
scheme. B.Tech is a new application under UG/Professional scheme. 
 
Category: Professional Courses 
Q40 (EN): I am doing MBBS in a private college with annual fee ₹10,00,000. How 
much scholarship will I get?​
A40: For SC/ST students (2024-25 example), fee reimbursement in private medical 
colleges is capped at ₹1,00,000-1,50,000/year (verify current limit). You will receive 
only up to the limit; remaining ₹8,50,000-9,00,000 you must pay yourself. 
Maintenance allowance will be separate (₹12,000-24,000/year). 
 
Q41 (EN): Is scholarship available for law students (LLB)?​
A41: Yes. LLB (3-year or 5-year integrated) students are eligible if the college is 
BCI-approved and registered on the portal. 3-year LLB after graduation may be 
counted as PG. 5-year BA-LLB may be counted as UG for first 3 years and PG for 
last 2 years (verify scheme). 
 
Q42 (EN): Can pharmacy students get scholarship?​
A42: Yes. B.Pharm, M.Pharm, and D.Pharm students are eligible if the institution is

PCI-approved. B.Pharm falls under UG Professional; D.Pharm under Diploma; 
M.Pharm under PG Professional. 
 
Category: Multiple Scholarships 
Q43 (EN): Can I apply for both UP scholarship and Central NSP scholarship?​
A43: You can apply to both, but you can accept only one. If both are approved, you 
must choose one and the other will be cancelled/refunded. Duplication of benefits is 
not allowed. 
 
Q44 (EN): I got a college scholarship. Can I also get government scholarship?​
A44: If the college scholarship is privately funded (by college trust/alumni), you may 
receive both college and government scholarship (check college rules). If the college 
scholarship is government-funded (e.g., fee waiver by government in that college), 
you may not get both for the same fee component. 
 
Category: Special Cases 
Q45 (EN): I took a gap year after Class 12. Can I apply for scholarship now in BA 1st 
year?​
A45: Yes. Apply as 'Fresh' student. You may need to provide an explanation/affidavit 
for the gap year
